description: On 1 December 2024, the Nigerian troops clashed with a Zamfara militia in Yar Galadima village location coded to the closest populated area, Dan Sadau (Maru, Zamfara). The troops were supported by the Air Force and struck scores of the fleeing militia. They recovered several arms, including explosive devices from them. Scores of fatalities coded as 20.

On 1 December 2024, an armed group shot and killed a police officer and abducted a former member of the House of Representatives between Gwantu and Nunku, location coded to the closest populated area, Nunku (Akwanga, Nassarawa). The hostage was on his way to Abuja when the attackers killed his police escort and abducted him. The abductors demanded an unspecified millions of naira for his release.

On 1 December 2024, Unguwar Galadima defense militia clashed with a Zamfara militia attempting to attack their community in Unguwar Galadima, also called Galadima (Bungundu, Zamfara). The militia launched the attack to avenge the recent killing of their leader. The defense militia repelled the attack, killed several of the invading militia, and recovered ten rifles. Two residents were injured during the attack. Several fatalities coded as 3. The Nigerian troops waylaid the militia as they escaped from the village, coded separately.
On 1 December 2024, two Marlian boys members clashed and injured 2 Marlian boys near the Koran Tanki Musa area in Maiduguri (Maiduguri Metro, Borno).

On 1 December 2024, ISWAP fighters abducted a male passenger after setting up an illegal checkpoint in Binduldul village (Gubio, Borno) for an unknown reason. They robbed other passengers of their valuables and stole fuel from vehicles.
On 1 December 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted 10 farmers in the Janbako community (Maradun, Zamfara) for an unknown reason.

On 1 December 2024, a Sokoto militia attacked Dan Arne, location coded to the closest populated area, Tsabre (Isa, Sokoto) and Tozai villages, coded separately. Casualties unknown. No further details.

On 1 December 2024, a Kaduna militia attacked and killed 2 people and abducted three others in the Anguwan Maidoki community, location coded to the local administrative headquarters, Kajuru (Kajuru, Kaduna).
On 1 December 2024, the Aye (Black Axe) clashed with Eiye in Kwale (Ndokwa West, Delta). Casualties unknown. No further details.

On 1 December 2024, four armed men (likely a cult militia due to the nature of the killing and their prevalence in the area) shot and killed a commercial motorcyclist in the Sabo area of Ijebu-Ode (Ijebu Ode, Ogun).
On 1 December 2024, armed men (likely cult members due to the nature of the killing and their prevalence in the area) shot and injured 1 person in Igando (Alimosho, Lagos) for an unknown reason.
On 1 December 2024, a Katsina militia shot and killed 1 person on the outskirts of Bakori (Bakori, Katsina). The militants looted food supplies.
On 1 December 2024, a Kaduna militia opened fire indiscriminately, injuring 3 people in Maraban Kajuru (Kajuru, Kaduna). The militia abducted six people, including a police officer.
On 1 December 2024, a Zamfara militia attacked and killed 1 person and injured 2 others in Maru (Maru, Zamfara). They abducted an unspecified number of others.
On 1 December 2024, a Sokoto militia attacked Tozai (Isa, Sokoto) and Dan Arne villages, coded separately. Casualties unknown. No further details.
On 1 December 2024, the Aye (Black Axe) shot and injured 1 person at Okhoro in Benin City (Oredo, Edo) for an unknown reason.

On 1 December 2024, the Nigerian troops clashed with a Katsina militia in Kakumi (Bakori, Katsina). The troops repelled the militia's attack on the village, leaving 1 person injured. There were no fatalities.

On 1 December 2024, GSF personnel and Unguwar Galadima defense militia clashed with the Zamfara militia in Maru LGA, coded to Maru (Maru, Zamfara). The militia attacked the community and killed an unspecified number of people. GSF personnel and the defense militia recovered weapons and IEDs. Unspecified fatalities coded as 3.

On 1 December 2024, a Sokoto militia attacked the Dan Tudu community in Dan Tudu (Sabon Birni, Sokoto). 10 people were killed and an unspecified number of people were abducted. An unspecified number of livestock was rustled.
On 1 December 2024, suspected ISWAP/Boko Haram (JAS) attacked and killed 7 people who had gone in search of firewood in Logmani, Gamboru ward (Ngala, Borno).

Around 2 December 2024 (as reported), police clashed with a Jigawa militia attempting to abduct a man at Tudun Ghana Quarters in Malam Madori (Malam Madori, Jigawa). The abductors were outgunned and escaped without the hostage.

On 2 December 2024, the Dullu-led Zamfara militia group clashed with the Najaja faction of Zamfara militia, killing Najaja's brother and one of his commanders in a location (likely Zamfara state based on the predominance of the group activities in the state), location coded to the state capital, Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara). The clash erupted over a power tussle between the groups. There were two fatalities.

On 2 December 2024, a Sokoto militia shot and killed nine members of the Dantudu defense militia and injured one in Dantudu Lajinge village, also called Dan Tudu (Sabon Birni, Sokoto). Another source reported the victims were slaughtered, and the attackers abducted their wives. The injured member escaped being killed and was later taken to the hospital.
On 2 December 2024, ISWAP fighters attacked farmers, killing 1 on their farm in Njimtilo town in Konduga LGA, location coded to the local administrative headquarters, Konduga (Borno).
On 2 December 2024, Boko Haram (JAS) attacked and killed 4 people in Firgi village around Pulka (Gwoza, Borno). They also stole four bicycles.
On 2 December 2024, a Katsina militia attacked and killed 3 people in Tashar Kadanya village in the Dan Alhaji Yangayya ward (Batsari, Katsina).
On 2 December 2024, a Zamfara militia shot and killed 4 people and abducted one other in the Gwashi community (Bukkuyum, Zamfara).
On 2 December 2024, ISWAP fighters abducted eleven females in Chiddu Bura village, location coded to the local administrative headquarters, Konduga (Borno) for an unknown reason.
On 2 December 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted seven people from Dogon Dajin Wanke village, also called Wanke (Gusau, Zamfara) for an unknown reason.

On 2 December 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted an unspecified number of people after blocking the Anka Road near Kwanar Maje (Anka, Zamfara). The Zamfara State Community Protection Guards were deployed to the area (no contact with the militia).

On 2 December 2024, a Sokoto militia attacked and killed two people and abducted 2 others after setting up an illegal checkpoint along the Isa-Galadi road, location coded to the closest populated area, Isa (Isa, Sokoto).
On 2 December 2024, a Sokoto militia attacked and killed 1 person and abducted two others in the Takalmawa community, location coded to the closest populated area, Kurawa (Sabon Birni, Sokoto).
On 2 December 2024, the Eiye and the Buccaneer clashed and killed at least 2 people in the Obada area of Abeokuta North LGA, location coded to Ake (Abeokuta North, Ogun).

On 2 December 2024, a Taraba militia abducted and assaulted a man along the Maraban Apawa- Zing road, location coded to the closest populated area, Apawa (Lau, Taraba). The Nigerian troops rescued the hostage (likely without confrontation with the abductors.).

On 2 December 2024, an unidentified armed group shot at the vehicle of a former member of the House of Representatives and killed his police escort along a road between Nunku and Gwantu, coded to Nkuku (Akwanga, Nassarawa). The former member of the House of Representatives and his wife were abducted.
On 2 December 2024, the Nigerian troops clashed with ISWAP/ Boko Haram (JAS) and repelled their attack on Wulgo town (Ngala, Borno). There were no fatalities.

On 2 December 2024, a Niger militia (described as bandits) abducted 34 civilians, including 8 men and 26 women in Unguwar Magiro, location coded to the closest known populated area, Kagara (Rafi, Niger).

On 3 December 2024, suspected Ifon militia shot and killed a farmer on his farm in Oke Eletu, location coded to the closest populated area, Ifon (Orolu, Osun). The victim, who was from Ilobu, was killed on his farm in a disputed area between his people and the Ifon. His killing has generated tension between the two communities and there is a likelihood of the renewal of clashes between them.

Around 3 December 2024, an unidentified armed group (likely cult militia based on the nature of killing) shot and killed a man around Ihiala town (Ihiala, Anambra). The victim was shot twice in the head a day before his wedding.

Around 3 December 2024 (as reported), a Sokoto militia attacked and killed nine people in Dan Tudu (Sabon Birni, Sokoto). They injured one person and abducted several men and women. They also looted some valuables from the village.
On 3 December 2024, Boko Haram (JAS) attacked and killed 5 people collecting firewood around the Marte axis of Marte (Marte, Borno). CJTF members were mobilized to recover their bodies.

On 3 December 2024, a Sokoto militia clashed with a Goronyo defense militia while attempting to attack Gorau village, location coded to the local administrative headquarters, Goronyo (Goronyo, Sokoto). The defense militia repelled the attack, and 2 of its members were injured. There were no fatalities.

On 3 December 2024, an unidentified armed group opened fire indiscriminately and abducted one person at YKC Roundabout in Obio/Akpot LGA, location coded to the local administrative headquarters, Rumuodomaya (Obio, Rivers) for an unknown reason.
On 3 December 2024, the Eiye and the Buccaneers clashed and killed 1 member around a gas station in Oluwo (Abeokuta North, Ogun).
On 3 December 2024, the Aye (Black Axe) and the Eiye clashed and shot 1 person dead in the Iju Ishaga, also called Iju (Ifako, Lagos). Another person was injured.
On 3 December 2024, KSCWC and the Kankara defense militia clashed with a Katsina militia and repelled their attack on Kankara town (Kankara, Katsina). The militia retreated. There were no fatalities.

On 3 December 2024, a Sokoto militia attacked and killed 1 person and abducted 4 others after blocking the Kagara-Balla road in Goronyo LGA, location coded to the closest populated area, Kagara (Goronyo, Sokoto).
On 3 December 2024, a Niger militia (described as bandits) abducted a civilian in Shafaci community (Borgu, Niger).
On 3 December 2024, a Niger militia (described as bandits) abducted a civilian in Babanna ward, location coded to Babanna (Borgu, Niger).

On 4 December 2024, a Kogi militia abducted one person in Agbadu, also spelt as Agbado (Kabba, Kogi), after they had picked up nine people, including an LGA councilor in the neighboring Odo-Ape, coded separately.
On 4 December 2024, a Kogi militia abducted nine people, including an LGA councilor, in Odo-Ape (Kabba, Kogi). The hostages were picked up from their various homes in the community.

On 4 December 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted a Ministry of Justice director and his niece along the Abak-Ikot Abasi road, location coded to the closest administrative headquarters, Abak (Abak, Akwa Ibom). Police rescued the hostages the following day and killed three of the abductors, coded separately.

On 4 December 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a truck driver along the Ishiagu-Okigwe highway, location coded to the closest populated area, Ishiagu (Ivo, Ebonyi). The killing was suspected to be related to a communal clash between the Umuobor, Akaeze, and their neighbors, Ogwor, Ishiagu in Ivo LGA.
On 4 December 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted ten people in Uli village in Kyaram ward (Bukkuyum, Zamfara). 1 of the hostages escaped with injuries.

On 4 December 2024, the Nigerian troops killed several Kaduna militants in various locations, including Ruwan Sanye, Randa, Rafin Gora, Libere Gari, and Libere Makaranta in Kauru LGA, location coded to the local administrative headquarters, Kauru (Kaduna). The troops rescued 25 hostages. Several fatalities coded as 10.

On 4 December 2024, a Sokoto militia attacked and injured 1 person and abducted four others in Sabon Garin Dole village (Goronyo, Sokoto). They also looted shops and livestock. One of the hostages later escaped.
On 4 December 2024, the Eiye and Maphite clashed and injured an unspecified number of people in Agbarho town (Ughelli North, Delta). There were no fatalities.
On 4 December 2024, the Aye (Black Axe) and the Eiye clashed and killed 3 people along ECOWAS Road in Ojo (Ojo, Lagos).
On 4 December 2024, a Sokoto militia abducted a man from his residence in Yar Abba (Sokoto North, Sokoto) for an unknown reason.

On 4 December 2024, a Kaduna militia attacked a church in Farin Dutse, Bital Ward (Kauru, Kaduna), killing 1 person and injuring many among the 50 people abducted from the village. They later returned the remaining 49 captives with various injuries. It is unclear if a ransom was paid for their release.

On 5 December 2024, a Kogi militia opened fire and shot a pastor dead on the road between Idofin and Makutu road, a few kilometers to Isanlu (Yagba East, Kogi). The militia abducted three other occupants in the car conveying the pastor and took them to the bush. They demanded a 10 million naira ransom.

On 5 December 2024, police and AVG clashed with a suspected IPOB/ESN militia on the Umuchu-Amesi-Uga Road in Ajalli (Orumba South, Anambra). A police officer and AVG member sustained gun injuries. The AVG operational vehicles were hit by bullets and burned. There were no fatalities.

On 5 December 2024, police clashed with an unidentified armed group, killing three and rescuing two hostages in Ikot Ukpong (Abak, Akwa Ibom). The hostages were abducted a day before, coded separately. Other abductors managed to escape the police onslaught.
On 5 December 2024, police shot and killed a member of an unidentified cult group in Rivers state, location coded to the state capital, Port Harcourt (Port Harcourt, Rivers).

On 5 December 2024, a Katsina militia killed two people in Ungwan Mai Kawo, also called Ungwan Kawo (Kankara, Katsina). They also killed one person each in Gidan Damo and Gidan Umoru, coded separately.
On 5 December 2024, a Katsina militia killed one person and injured four others in Burdugau (Malumfashi, Katsina). They set a car ablaze.

On 5 December 2024, the Nigerian troops clashed with IPOB/ESN fighters while raiding their enclaves in Uhuala-Aku, location coded to a close village, Umuanu Aku (Okigwe, Imo). The militants managed to escape the military's onslaught. The troops recovered One G3 rifle, two pump action rifles, three Dane guns, one locally fabricated pistol, one MG belt, two AK 47 rifle magazines, 12 rounds of 5.56mm ammunition, and five rounds of 7.62mm NATO ammunition. There were no fatalities.

On 5 December 2024, suspected IPOB/ESN abducted a retired Archbishop of the Nnewi Province of the Anglican Communion and his driver while traveling from Nnewi to Umuchu, location coded to the victims' destination, Umuchu (Aguata, Anambra).
On 5 December 2024, a Sokoto militia attacked and injured 1 person and abducted many others in Gajit village in Lajinge ward (Sabon Birni, Sokoto). They rustled some cattle.

On 5 December 2024, a Taraba militia attacked the sister and the mother of the Taraba State Governor along Kente Road, location coded to the closest populated area, Kente (Wukari, Taraba). Their police escort accidentally shot and injured the governor's sister in the stomach while repelling the militia's attack. The sister died a few days later.

On 5 December 2024, ISWAP/BH (JAS) attacked and killed two people in Uvaha Uvaha (Gwoza, Borno) and Kwatara village, coded separately. The victim included an IDP returnee from Gadamayo, community, coded separately. 2 fatalities shared across 2 events; 1 fatality coded.

On 5 December 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted a journalist at Irete (Owerri West, Imo). The hostage was the Assistant Editor-in-Chief of the News Agency of Nigeria for the Owerri office. The abductors released him on 7 December 2024 after an undisclosed ransom was paid.

On 5 December 2024, a Katsina militia attacked and killed one person each at Gidan Damo and Gidan Umoru, location coded to the closest populated area, Dan Azuba (Kankara, Katsina). They killed two others at Ungwan Mai Kawo, coded separately. There were two fatalities.

On 5 December 2024, ISWAP/BH (JAS) attacked and killed 2 people in Kwatara, location coded to the local administrative headquarters, Gwoza (Gwoza, Borno), and Uvaha village, coded separately. The victim included an IDP returnee from Gadamayo, community. 2 fatalities shared across 2 events; 1 fatality coded.

On 5 December 2024, a Niger militia (described as bandits) shot and killed 1 civilian in Kasamani, location coded to the closest known populated area, Shiroro (Rafi, Niger) and injured another. They also abducted 22 civilians.

On 5 December 2024, a local defense militia intervened and clashed with a Niger militia (described as bandits) in Marami, location coded to the closest known populated area, Karengi (Borgu, Niger) while Niger militia were demanding ransom payments from civilians. 5 Niger militants were killed and two escaped without the ransom.

On 5 December 2024, a local defense militia clashed with a Niger militia (described as bandits) in the bush near Kigbera (Borgu, Niger). 7 Niger militia members were killed and two defense members were injured.

On 6 December 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted and stripped a Delta State University female student naked in Abraka (Ethiope East, Delta). She was released on 7 December 2024 after collecting a million naira ransom.

On 6 December 2024, a Katsina militia attacked and killed one person and injured several others in Dankunuji, location coded to a nearby village, Damarke (Kankara, Katsina), and Yargoje, coded separately. They abducted several people from the communities. One fatality shared across the two events; zero fatality coded.
On 6 December 2024, a Taraba militia shot and killed two people in Jalingo (Jalingo, Taraba). The victims, a clergyman and a young woman were shot dead in two different locations.

On 6 December 2024, police shot and killed 17-year-old students of the Delta State University of Science and Technology in Ozoro (Isoko North, Delta). The victim was shot over an altercation concerning a fireworks shooting.

On 6 December 2024, a Sokoto militia attacked and killed 3 civilians at an illegal checkpoint mounted by the militia at Lambar Rabah Junction along the Chacho - Rabah road (Rabah, Sokoto). 12 civilians were abducted.
On 6 December 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted and later killed 1 civilian from Sintali near Kojoli (Jada, Adamawa) for an unknown reason. No further information available.
On 6 December 2024, a Sokoto militia abducted 10 civilians from Gajit village in the Sabon Birni LGA (Sabon Birni, Sokoto). The militia looted an unspecified number of livestock.

On 6 December 2024, the Kwanar Dikke militia attacked and killed 2 civilians at an illegal checkpoint mounted by the militia in Kwanar Dikke along the Dikke - Tafoki road, location coded to closest populated area Tafoki (Faskari, Katsina). 2 other civilians were abducted.
On 6 December 2024, a Kaduna militia attacked and killed 2 civilians in Dogon Dawa (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). The attackers looted 2 cows.
On 6 December 2024, a Katsina militia attacked and killed 5 farmers in Yar Goje in the Kankara LGA (Kankara, Katsina). The militia looted livestock.
On 6 December 2024, a Zamfara militia attacked and injured 1 civilian along the Gusau-Sokoto Road near Kadauri (Maru, Zamfara). The militia abducted an unspecified number of civilians.

On 6 December 2024, the military forces clashed and repelled an attack from ISWAP/Boko Haram (JAS) militants in Damboa (Damboa, Borno) when the militants attempted to attack the town. Casualties unknown.

On 6 December 2024, an unidentified militia (likely Dogon Santsi militia based on location) shot and injured 5 civilians at an illegal checkpoint mounted by the militia near Dogon Santsi along the Gusau - Magami road (Gusau, Zamfara). The militia abducted 12 other civilians.

On 6 December 2024, a Katsina militia attacked and killed one person and injured several others in Yargoje (Kankara, Katsina) and Dankunuji, coded separately. They abducted several people from the communities. One fatality shared across the two events; one fatality coded.

On 7 December 2024, police clashed with a Katsina militia along the Katsina-Magamar Jibia road at Kwanar Makera village, location coded to the closest populated area, Magama Jibia (Jibia, Katsina). The clash erupted while the police responded to a distress call about the militia's abduction of ten passengers on the road. The police rescued the passengers, while the militants escaped with gunshot injuries. There were no fatalities.

On 7 December 2024, police clashed with a Katsina militia while attempting to abduct ten passengers on the Funtua-Gusau road at Marabar Bangori, also called Bangori (Faskari, Katsina). The police rescued ten passengers while the militants escaped with gunshot injuries. There were no fatalities.

On 7 December 2024, the Nigerian troops clashed with a Taraba militia in Ikayor village, location coded to the state capital Jalingo (Jalingo, Taraba). The militants were outgunned and fled. The troops recovered a red Toyota Corolla vehicle, a motorcycle, a military camouflage trouser, and a Beretta pistol with one round of 9mm ammunition. There were no fatalities.

On 7 December 2024, a Sokoto militia abducted a newly wedded bribe and four bridesmaids after the wedding in Kwaren Gamba, close to Kuka Teke village, location coded to a nearby village, Kwatsal (Sabon Birni, Sokoto).
On 7 December 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted at least 51 civilians, including women and children in Gidan Maidanko in the Maradun LGA (Maradun, Zamfara).

On 7 December 2024, the military forces carried out a military operation on an IPOB/ESN camp in Okposi community (Ezza North, Ebonyi). 2 IPOB/ESN members were arrested, and the military recovered firearms and a motorcycle. Casualties unknown.

On 7 December 2024, the military forces carried out a military clearance operation on an IPOB/ESN camp in Agu Orba in the Ekwegbe community (Igbo Etiti, Enugu). The military forces recovered firearms. Casualties unknown. No further information available.
On 7 December 2024, Eiye militia killed a member of the Aye militia (Black Axe) at the Signboard bus stop, Iyana Isashi in the Ojo LGA (Ojo, Lagos).
On 7 December 2024, Eiye militia killed 1 member of the Aye militia (Black Axe) at Harmony Estate near the Federal University of Agriculture in Abeokuta (Abeokuta South, Ogun).
On 7 December 2024, Eiye militia shot and injured a member of the Maphite militia in Agbarho (Ughelli North, Delta).
On 7 December 2024, a Zamfara clashed with the Ruwan Kura vigilantes in Ruwan Kura, closest town Ruwan Rana (Bukkuyum, Zamfara). 1 civilian was killed.
On 7 December 2024, a Kaduna militia attacked and injured 2 civilians at a pastoralist settlement in Kurutu village (Kachia, Kaduna). The attackers looted livestock.
On 7 December 2024, a Katsina militia attacked and killed 2 civilians in Burdugau (Malumfashi, Katsina) for an unknown reason.
On 7 December 2024, a police officer shot and killed 1 teenager while attempting to arrest him in Ozoro community (Isoko North, Delta).
On 7 December 2024, a Sokoto militia attacked and killed 2 civilians in Kagara (Goronyo, Sokoto). 1 civilian was injured, and 6 others were abducted.

Around 7 December 2024 (as reported), Nigerian troops and the Tsafe Defense militia clashed with a Zamfara militia around Yankuzo area in Aso Hills, location coded to the closest populated area, Yankuzo (Tsafe, Zamfara). The Nigerian Air Force supported the infantry with air strikes, killing many fleeing militia members. Many fatalities, coded as 10.
On 7 December 2024, a Sokoto militia abducted 5 civilians, including a bride and her 4 bridesmaids, in Kukaa village in the Sabon Birni LGA (Sabon Birni, Sokoto).

On 7 December 2024, military forces clashed with a Kaduna militia near Hayin-Dam Forest near Janjala community (Kagarko, Kaduna). 3 militia were killed. The military forces recovered the stolen livestock from Kurutu (coded separately).

On 7 December 2024, a Katsina militia attacked and killed 2 civilians at an illegal vehicle checkpoint mounted by the militia along the Yar Goje - Dankumeji Road in the Kankara LGA (Kankara, Katsina). The militia abducted 8 civilians.
On 7 December 2024, a Katsina militia attacked and killed 6 civilians in the villages of Gidan Damo, Gidan Umoru, and Unguwa Mai Kawo in the Kankara LGA (Kankara, Katsina).
On 7 December 2024, Aye militia killed 1 member of the Eiye militia in Apete (Akinyele, Oyo) and injured another.

On 8 December 2024, the Nigerian troops, police, and the Bena defense militia engaged a Kebbi militia in a firefight along the Mairairai- Bena Road, location coded to the closest populated area, Ben (Danko, Kebbi). The troops engaged the militia while responding to their activity, where they had abducted 36 people after blocking the road. The troops outgunned them, and many of them escaped with gunshot wounds. They released all the hostages unhurt. There were no fatalities.

On 8 December 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted over 50 people, including 43 women and children, from Kakin Dawa village in the district of Gidan Goga (Maradun, Zamfara). The militia invaded the village at night and opened fire indiscriminately, making people scampered for safety. They searched house to house and abducted the hostages.

On 8 December 2024, a Kebbi militia abducted at least 36 civilians at an illegal vehicle checkpoint mounted by the militia along the Mairari - Bena Road, location coded to the closest populated area Bena (Danko, Kebbi). The military forces intervened and rescued the victims. It is unknown if clashes occurred.
On 8 December 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted at least 7 civilians, including 3 teenage girls, on the outskirts of Bakura town (Bakura, Zamfara).
On 8 December 2024, Aye (Black Axe) militia killed a member of the Eiye militia in Obantoko (Odedah, Ogun).
On 8 December 2024, Maphite and Eiye militias clashed in Agbarho (Ughelli North, Delta). 1 civilian was killed.
On 8 December 2024, a Kaduna militia attacked and killed 1 civilian in Angwaku community in the Kajuru LGA (Kajuru, Kaduna). 4 other civilians were abducted.

On 8 December 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a truck driver along the Okigwe - Ishiagu expressway (Ivo, Ebonyi). The attack was linked to a land dispute between the Umuobor, Akaeze, and Ogwor communities in Ishiagu.
On 8 December 2024, a Katsina militia attacked and killed 1 civilian in Gidan Inu village in the Bakori LGA (Bakori, Katsina). The militia abducted 3 civilians.
On 8 December 2024, a Kaduna militia abducted a nursing mother and her 2 children at Maraban Kajuru (Kajuru, Kaduna).
On 8 December 2024, Aye (Black Axe) and Eiye militias clashed near Samonda neighborhood in Ibadan (Ibadan North West, Oyo). 1 militia was killed.
On 8 December 2024, Eiye militia riding on three motorcycles killed 1 civilian at Sango Oju Irin, location coded to closest town Ibadan (Ibadan North West, Oyo) for an unknown reason.

On 9 December 2024, the Nigerian troops clashed with an unidentified armed group in a forest in Ugbolu (Oshimili North, Delta). The troops rescued four hostages held by the armed group. The hostages were abducted and had spent several days while their ransom negotiation was ongoing, coded separately. There were no fatalities.
Around 9 December 2024 (as reported), police attacked and injured a driver over his refusal to pay a hundred naira bribe in Enugu, location coded to the state capital, Enugu (Enugu North, Enugu).

On 9 December 2024, suspected Umuogwor militia attacked and killed between six and seven members of the Aka Eze community while returning from the farm in Aka Eze (Ivo, Ebonyi). The killing was not unrelated to a lingering land dispute between the two communities.

On 9 December 2024, Boko Haram (JAS) militants abducted 10 females (ages not specified) in Kaine village in Yoyo district (Kukawa, Borno). The militants demanded a ransom of three million Naira for each victim, with threats to force them into marriage if the demands were not met.

Around 9 December 2024 (between 6 - 12 December), ISWAP claimed to have attacked the Nigerian troops, killing one soldier in Gamboru-Ngala, also called Gamboru (Ngala, Borno). They also seized some firearms.

Around 9 December 2024 (between 6 - 12 December), ISWAP claimed to have attacked the Nigerian troops, killing many soldiers in Dalwa (Askira Uba, Borno). The attack led to the destruction of military equipment. Unknown casualties coded as 3.
On 9 December 2024, ISWAP militants clashed with CJTF members at ISS Camp in the Ngala LGA (Ngala, Borno). 1 CJTF member was killed. The CJTF recovered two AK-47 rifles.
On 9 December 2024, an unidentified militia attacked and injured 2 civilians in Unguwar Dahiru in the Funtua LGA (Funtua, Katsina) and at least 10 civilians were abducted.
On 9 December 2024, a Sokoto militia attacked and killed 2 civilians in Bulbuli (Yabo, Sokoto). 2 others were abducted.

On 9 December 2024, a Sokoto militia attacked and killed 1 civilian at an illegal vehicle checkpoint mounted by the militia at the Lambar Rabah Junction along the Rabah Expressway in Rabah (Rabah, Sokoto). 1 civilian was injured, and 3 others were abducted.
On 9 December 2024, Eiye militia killed 1 civilian in Idi-Ito (Afijio, Oyo) for an unknown reason.

On 9 December 2024, Ukwu Oba youths macheted and injured four people, including a retired Naval officer, in Isheagwu, also spelled as Ishiagu (Aniocha South, Delta), over a land ownership claim. The youth attacked the people while surveying their land boundaries, which had been constantly disputed by their neighboring Ukwu Oba. The attack triggered an exodus of people from the community.

On 9 December 2024, a Kogi militia opened fire sporadically and hit (likely injured at the time of report) one person while attempting to abduct a man in Okene (Okene, Kogi). The hostage was an aide to the former governor of Kogi State.
On 9 December 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted an aide to a former governor from his restaurant in Okene (Okene, Kogi) for an unknown reason.

On 26 August 2024, a Katsina militia abducted five people in Unguwar Randa village in Funtua LGA, coded to Funtua (Katsina).

Around 26 August 2024 (as reported), a Sokoto militia abducted 150 people from villages around Sabon Birnin (Sabon Birnin, Sokotoato). They also rustled over 1000 cattle from the villages.

On 26 August 2024, a Niger militia (described at bandits) abducted one, and shot and injured another in Zadawo community (Borgu, Niger).

On 27 August 2024, a Kaduna militia clashed with KADVIS, killing two members and two farmers in the Tasake community, Ungwan Mayana area of Gayam (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). On 27 August 2024, the Nigerian troops opened fire and killed two militants from a Kaduna militia in Kurmin Kare (Kachia, Kaduna). A militia spy arrested by the soldiers led them to their hideout, where they opened fire on sighting the militants.

On 27 August 2024, a Kaduna militia opened fire sporadically and abducted scores of commuters forcefully stopped in Kwaga village (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). On 27 August 2024, the Nigerian troops ambushed and clashed with Boko Haram (JAS), killing five militants in Logomani village (Ngala, Borno). The troops recovered one AK-47 rifle, a magazine, and two bicycles.

On 27 August 2024, the Nigerian troops and the villagers repelled the Jimmu Sumail-led Zamfara militia attempting to attack Matunga, also spelled Matusgi (Talata Mafara, Zamfara). The troops killed twenty-five militants, while three villagers died in the confrontation. Other militiamen managed to escape but were ambushed at Magamin Diddi village, coded separately. On 27 August 2024, the Gbenpakan militia (predominantly farmers) clashed with armed Fulani pastoralists in the Gbenpakan community, coded to Ilua (Saki West, Oyo). On 27 August 2024, an unidentified armed group engaged in a firefight with a security guard in the Amiyi community, also called Ochuche-Umuodo (Ogbaru, Anambra). The guard sustained gunshot injuries and died two days later.
On 27 August 2024, a Zamfara militia killed one person in Badarawa village (Shinkafi, Zamfara).
On 27 August 2024, the Aye (Black Axe) clashed with the Vikings in Awada, Onisha North LGA, coded to Onitsha (Anambra). One militant was killed.
On 27 August 2024, an unidentified armed group opened fire sporadically and abducted three people in the Dakwa area of Dei-Dei (Bwari, FCT).
On 27 August 2024, a Katsina militia attacked and killed two people and abducted five females in Yargoje village (Kankara, Katsina).
On 27 August 2024, ISWAP/Boko Haram (JAS) raped and killed 1 young woman in Gwoza LGA, location coded to LGA HQ, Gwoza (Gwoza, Borno).

On 28 August 2024, a soldier attached to OPHD Sector 6 shot and killed a police DPO at a checkpoint around Dan Marke (Bukkuyum, Zamfara). The police DPO was traveling to attend a conference when the soldier stopped him and shot him in the head despite identifying himself as a police officer.

Around 28 August 2024 (as reported), the Nigerian troops ambushed Boko Haram (JAS), killing two militants along their supply route in Wille village in Gujba LGA, coded to Gujba (Yobe). The troops recovered one FN rifle, a magazine, and a bicycle.

On 28 August 2024, a Niger militia attacked and injured a man and abducted his daughter in the New Bwari community (Tafa, Niger). The hostage was rescued by the Nigerian soldiers at a checkpoint around 16 September 2024 when they intercepted the militia's vehicle fleeing an offensive in Kagarko LGA. The hostage exposed his abductors at the checkpoint and was rescued.

On 28 August 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted fifty people from the Tundun Wada area in Talata Mafara LGA, coded to Talata Mafara (Zamfara). The hostages included women, children, an Islamic cleric, and his students.
On 28 August 2024, a Niger militia attacked Bassa village (Shiroro, Niger). Casualty Unknown. No further details.

On 28 August 2024, an unidentified armed group opened fire sporadically and injured the Chief Security Officer (assumed to be unarmed) of the Obosi community in Idemili South LGA, coded to Obosi (Idemili South, Anambra).
On 28 August 2024, IS/Boko Haram (JAS) abducted two people in search of firewood around Dikwa town (Dikwa, Borno).
On 28 August 2024, IS/Boko Haram (JAS) attacked the Nigerian troops around the Custom House IDP Camp, Galmeri in Jere LGA, coded to Khaddamari (Borno). There were no fatalities.
On 28 August 2024, IS/BH (JAS) attacked the Nigerian troops along the Konduga-Bama Road, around the Konduga town (Konduga, Borno). There were no fatalities.
On 28 August 2024, a Katsina militia attacked Matazu town (Matazu, Katsina). No further details.

On 29 August 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted not less than three people in Mafara town, also called Talata Mafara (Talata Mafara, Zamfara). The militants invaded the town when the residents were asleep.

On 29 August 2024, police engaged in a firefight with a sea pirate kingpin in Uyanga, also called Uyanga Okpo Usun (Akamkpa, Cross River). The police shot and killed the pirate kingpin and recovered one G3 rifle with four live ammunition in the confrontation.

On 29 August 2024, a Katsina militia shot and killed the leader of the Kandawa defense militia and four Community Watch Corps members in an ambush along the Batsari- Yar Gamji Road, coded to Yar Gamji (Batsari, Katsina). They abducted three residents. There were five fatalities.

On 29 August 2024, the Nigerian troops clashed with the Bello Turji-led Zamfara militia while on patrol en route to Kwashebawa (Zurmi, Zamfara). Two of the troops' Mine Resistant Ambush Protected vehicles (MPRAPs) were bogged down in the mud, forcing them to abandon the trucks. The militia took over the trucks and set them on fire. There were no fatalities.

On 29 August 2024, police, KSCWC, and a communal defense militia clashed with a Katsina militia holding one person hostage in Faru village (Jibia, Katsina). The police rescued the hostage. There were no fatalities.
On 29 August 2024, an Adamawa militia killed two female students (unspecified reason) of the Federal College of Education Yola (FCE) in Yola town (Yola-North, Adamawa).
On 29 August 2024, ISWAP fighters clashed with MNJTF and CJTF in Wulgo village (Ngala, Borno). The militants injured a Cameroonian soldier of the MNJTF and CJTF member. There were no fatalities.

On 29 August 2024, the Aye (Black Axe) and the Eiye clashed in Oko Afo in Badagry LGA, location coded to local administrative headquarters, Badagry (Lagos). At least three people were injured during the confrontation.
On 29 August 2024, the Nigerian troops clashed with a Plateau militia after the militia set up an illegal checkpoint in Bokkos town (Bokkos, Plateau). The troops killed one militant.

On 29 August 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and wounded a man and abducted four members of his family in the Tundun Fulani extension area of Bwari, coded to Ushafa, also spelled as Ushapa (Bwari, FCT). Other sources reported that the man was shot dead as he managed to escape while his wife and two children were abducted.
On 29 August 2024, a Katsina militia attacked and killed two people at the Gidan Mai Kada community in Matazu LGA, coded to Matazu (Katsina). They also rustled domestic animals.

Around 30 August 2024 (as reported), the Nigerian troops clashed with a Kaduna militia and killed one in the Gayam area (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). They recovered a PKT machine gun with eight rounds of ammunition, a Baofeng radio, multiple communication devices, one SMF magazine, and 14 mobile SIM cards.

On 30 August 2024, suspected Boko Haram (JAS) attacked and killed three students of Faudiya School, Hausari (Geidam, Yobe). The students were asleep when the armed group shot and killed them, but one managed to escape with gunshot injuries. The school is affiliated with the Shia Islamic Movement of Nigeria (IMN).

On 30 August 2024, police clashed with a Katsina militia at the Kwanar Makera Bridge in Jibia LGA, location coded to the locality capital Jibia (Jibia, Katsina). One person was rescued by the police. There were no fatalities.

On 30 August 2024, a Sokoto militia attacked and killed an unspecified number of people and abducted others in the Sakanaw community, also spelt Sakanau (Tambuwal, Sokoto). Unspecified fatalities coded as 3.
On 30 August 2024, ISWAP fighters attacked two people fetching firewood along the Gulumba Gana Road in Dikwa LGA, location coded to the locality capital Dikwa (Borno). They killed one of the victims.

On 30 August 2024, an armed group abducted and killed a 19-year-old student in the Project Quarters area of Lafia (Lafia, Nassarawa). The abductors initially demanded a 30 million naira ransom but later reduced it to 17 million naira. They killed the hostage after collecting the 17 million naira ransom demanded.

Around 30 August 2024 (as reported), the Nigerian troops clashed with a Kaduna militia and killed seven in Kampanin Doka, also spelled as Kamfanin Doka (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). The troops recovered three AK-47 rifles, eight AK-47 magazines (four empty and four loaded with 120 rounds of 7.62mm ammunition), one magazine carrier, six motorcycles, three mobile phones, two Baofeng radio sets, and three pairs of civilian clothes.

On 30 August 2024, police clashed with suspected IPOB militants (due to their dominance and attack pattern) in Atani (Ogbaru, Anambra). The militants, numbering about 30, invaded the LGA secretariat, setting a section of the building on fire. The police repelled them as they set a section of the magistrate court and traditional ruler's building on fire. They retreated after a gunfight with the police. There were no fatalities.
On 30 August 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted an unspecified number of people in the Ruwan Gora community in Talata Mafara LGA, location coded to the locality capital Ruwan Bore (Zamfara).

On 31 August 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a Senior Special Assistant to the Speaker of the Edo State House of Assembly in transit between Ozalla and the Uhomora community (Owan West, Edo).

The troops killed the kingpin and five of his members in the onslaught. They recovered five Dane guns, ammunition, and other items. There were six fatalities.

On 31 August 2024, a Kogi militia opened fire and killed three KSVS members, including their leader, in Ankpa town (Ankpa, Kogi). The attackers trailed the defense militia to a place around the stadium and opened fire on them.

On 31 August 2024, the Nigerian troops and hunters engaged a Kaduna militia in a firefight, killing three in the Nasarawa-Jibo Forest near Gidan Azara (Kachia, Kaduna). The troops rescued four hostages while other militants escaped with gunshot wounds.

On 31 August 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a man and abducted his wife and two others along Emure-Supare Road, coded to Supare (Akoko South West, Ondo). The victims were ambushed while returning from Emure after a family event. They demanded a 30 million naira ransom for their release.

On 31 August 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted two people along the Asaba-Benin Highway, coded to Umunede (Ika North East, Delta). The police invaded the abductor's hideout on 5 September 2024 and rescued the hostages without a gunfight. The abductors fled on sighting the police and abandoned a Dane gun with ten rounds of live cartridges.

On 31 August 2024, police clashed with a Katsina militia after they abducted two people in Gandun Saki village in Dan-Musa LGA, location coded to the locality capital Kanawa (Katsina). The militia managed to escape, and the police rescued two hostages. There were no fatalities.
On 31 August 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted an unspecified number of people after blocking the Damri-Bakura Road in Bakura LGA, location coded to the locality capital Damri (Zamfara).
On 31 August 2024, the Aye (Black Axe) and the Eiye clashed and killed one member along the ECOWAS Road in Ojo (Ojo, Lagos).
On 31 August 2024, two unidentified cult militias clashed around the Imude Roundabout in Shibiri, Ojo LGA, location coded to the closest populated area Ojo (Lagos). There were no fatalities.

On 31 August 2024, an unidentified armed group opened fire indiscriminately at a vehicle, killing one person around Oyimo River, along the Emure- Supare Road in Emure LGA, location coded to the closest populated area, Emure-Ekiti (Ekiti).
On 31 August 2024, a Sokoto militia abducted six females from the Dan Aduwa community in Sabon Birni LGA, location coded to the locality capital Dan Tudu (Sokoto).

On 31 August 2024, a Sokoto militia attacked and injured two people in the Zalla Bango community in Sabon Birni LGA, location coded to the locality capital Tsamaye (Sabon Birni, Sokoto). They abducted many others.
On 31 August 2024, a Katsina militia blocked the Malumfashi-Katsina Road and abducted three people around Yan Tumaki town (Dan-Musa, Katsina).

On 1 July 2024, Nigerian troops engaged IPOB/ ESN militants in an armed clash at the militant's hideout in Ama Hausa, also spelled as Ama Awusa in Okigwe LGA (Imo). The militants fled and abandoned a cache of weapons that was recovered by the troops. No casualties.
On 1 July 2024, a suspected Fulani militia attacked an killed three IDPs near Agagbe town (Gwer West, Benue) as they were returning from their farm.
On 1 July 2024, a Kaduna militia killed one civilian and abducted scores of residents at Tudun-Jega and Unguwar Amir in Birnin Gwari (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna).

On 1 July 2024, DSS operatives tortured and injured a man at the Bekaji-round in Jimeta (Girei, Adamawa). He was ambushed in the middle of the road while driving, manhandled and forcefully dragged out of his car by the DSS operatives. The victim was hospitalized.
On 1 July 2024, the Aye (Black Axe) and the Eiye cult (SEC) clashed and killed one cult member in Akowonjo, Egbeda (Alimosho, Lagos).

On 1 July 2024, Nigerian troops engaged IPOB/ ESN militants in an armed clash at the militant's hideout in Ezeinyen Okwe Umucheke (Onuimo, Imo) coded to Okwe. One militant who was a leader was killed and the others fled.

On 1 July 2024, a Niger militia attacked and killed a woman in front of her children and abducted four others in Daupe village (Tafa, Niger). The militia received eighty million naira to release the hostages.

On 1 July 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted one person from his residence in the Edjakota area, also spelled as Adjekota (Ughelli North, Delta). The police later arrested the abductors and shot one dead on 5 July 2024, coded separately.

On 1 July 2024, the Nigerian troops engaged a Katsina militia in a firefight after the militia killed a university lecturer at his residence in the Low-cost Estate, Dutsin Ma (Dutsinma, Katsina). The militia abducted fourteen people, including two of the deceased children. The troops rescued ten hostages.
On 1 July 2024, suspected Mahmuda militants clashed with a local defense militia in Gallah (Agwara, Niger). 4 Mahmuda militants and 1 defense militia member were killed. Fatalities coded as 5.

On 2 July 2024, police forces engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash in an attempt to rescue to civilians who were abducted from Shagamu - Ijebu-Ode expressway (Shagamu, Ogun) (coded separately). Two members of the group were killed, four abductees including three Indians were rescued.
On 2 July 2024, rival cult militias clashed along the Uratta Road in Okwu Uratta, Uratta (Owerri North, Owerri). Casualties Unknown.

On 2 July 2024, a Kaduna militia killed a 14-year old boy who was abducted alongside his mother and siblings from their residence in Mahuta, coded to nearby Kamazo (Chikun, Kaduna). The victim was killed as a threat by the militia to show their seriousness with the demands for ransom. Location coded to where the victims were abducted from.

Around 2 July 2024, MNJTF attacked and killed several ISWAP fighters while responding to a distress call on the abduction of three people in Damsuri village, about 16 kilometers from Gajiram (Nganzai, Borno). The troops rescued the three hostages. Several fatalities coded as 3.

On 2 July 2024, two factions of OSTMAS engaged in firefights in different parts of Oshogbo (Osogbo, Osun) over a battle for supremacy and control of the motor parks in the state. Casualties are unknown.
Around 2 July 2024 (as reported), a Zamfara militia attacked the Askarawa defence militia, killing three between Bukuyum And Gumi, coded to Bukuyum (Bukkuyum, Zamfara).
On 2 July 2024, an unidentified armed group killed eleven civilians at Ayati (Ukum, Benue) when they invaded the area and shot sporadically.
On 2 July 2024, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists abducted a couple at Ndegwu Okuku road (Owerri West, Imo) as the were en route to buy land in the area.
Around 2 July 2024 (as reported), policemen attacked and beat up a civilian around Alausa area (Ikeja, Lagos). The victim was a passer-by and the reason for the attack is unknown.

On 2 July 2024, a Kaduna militia ambushed and killed five soldiers along the Abuja-Kaduna Highway at Alheri Prayer Ground in Chikun LGA, coded to Chikun (Kaduna). The soldiers were deployed to guard worshippers at the praying ground when the militia killed them and set one of their operational vehicles on fire.
On 2 July 2024, Mahmuda militia abducted the village head of Bankebara in Babanna (Borgu, Niger). He was later released on 4 July 2024.
On 2 July 2024, a Kebbi militia (described as bandits) shot and injured 1 local defense militia member in Kaoje Gwamba area, location coded to Kaoje (Bagudo, Kebbi).

On 3 July 2024, the Gbage and Chigbaga communities clashed over land ownership in Ebbo Gbacinku ward of Lapai LGA, coded to Gbage (Lapai, Niger). Four people were shot and injured and hospitalised. A motorcycle and a tractor were also burnt during the faceoff. There were no fatalities.

On 3 July 2024, an unidentified armed group killed the youth leader of Ododougwa-Ogume and dumped his body at the Ododougwa-Ogume junction (Ndokwa West, Delta) coded to Obodougwa. The victim was macheted to death, his body and motorcycle were set ablaze.

On 3 July 2024, the Aye cult militia killed an Eiye member (unarmed) on the campus of Tai Solarin University in Ijebu-Ode (Ijebu Ode, Ogun). They dragged the victim out of the examination hall before they shot him. They also stabbed him and then hit him in the head with a brick.
On 3 July 2024, the Aye (Black Axe) and the Eiye (SEC) cult militias clashed in Ijagun (Odogbolu, Ogun). Casualties Unknown.

On 3 July 2024, military forces ambushed a Kaduna militia and engaged them in an armed clash at Kurmin Aja in Kagarko LGA (Kaduna). Two militia members were killed, others fled into the bush, rifles, ammunition and magazines were recovered.

On 3 July 2024, Elegi and Katakpa communities clashed over land ownership in Ebbo Gbacinku ward of Lapai LGA, coded to Elegi (Lapai, Niger). Three Katakpa members were shot and injured in the confrontation. There were no fatalities.
On 3 July 2024, a Kogi militia abducted an unspecified number of passengers of a commercial bus in Okene (Okene, Kogi). The passengers were in transit from Edo state to Abuja when they were abducted.

On 4 July 2024, a Kaduna militia ambushed soldiers and engaged them in an armed clash at Audu-Jangwan village in Kachia LGA (Kaduna), coded to Kachia. Five soldiers were killed and their truck was burned down.

Around 4 July 2024 (as reported), the Nigerian troops engaged a Kaduna militia in armed clash and dislodged them at Jangeme Ruwan Kunku general area, coded to Igabi (Igabi, Kaduna). They recovered one PKT gun from fleeing militiamen. There were no fatalities.

Around 4 July 2024 (as reported), Nigerian troops clashed with a Kaduna militia and killed two in Gamagira (Soba, Kaduna). The troops recovered one AK-47 rifle and one magazine loaded with seven rounds of 7.62 mm special ammunition, a Tecno mobile phone, a phone charger, and a cash sum of one hundred and two thousand, ten naira.

Around 4 July 2024 (as reported), police engaged an unidentified armed group in a firefight in a forest bordering the Gwagwa and Dei-Dei, coded to Gwagwa (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The armed group were suspected to have abducted one person on 12 June 2024 and killed the hostage after collecting a ransom, coded separately. The police arrested five members of the group and recovered four AK-47 rifles from them. There were no fatalities.
On 4 July 2024, an unidentified cult militia shot and injured one person in Awka (Awka South, Anambra).

On 4 July 2024, Nigerian police engaged an unidentified armed group in a firefight, killing nine in the Ladipo area of Mushin (Mushin, Lagos). Two members of the armed group escaped with gunshot wounds. The group had been under police surveillance for weeks and was suspected of targeting wealthy people for abduction in Lagos state. Police recovered four AK-47 rifles, four locally made semiautomatic pistols, nine AK-47 magazines, three walkie-talkies, one POS machine and a loudspeaker. They also recovered one black Toyota 4Runner and a blue Lexus RX350.
On 5 July 2024, a Sokoto militia abducted thirty people from the Gwadodi community in Rabah LGA, coded to Rabah (Sokoto).

On 5 July 2024, police forces engaged an unidentified armed group in a firefight after storming their hideout in the Oviri-Ogor community (Ughelli North, Delta). One member of the group was fatally injured and later died while receiving treatment at the hospital. The police had arrested three members of the group before the clash. They recovered an AK-49 rifle from the scene. The armed group was responsible for the abduction of one person in Edjakita on 1 July 2024, coded separately.

On 5 July 2024, policemen fired gunshots into the air and killed a civilian at Imala/ Elega area of Abeokuta (Abeokuta South, Ogun) as he was locking up his shop. The victim was hit by a stray bullet, some sources claimed that the policemen were pursuing a suspect in a raid, while others claimed that they were drunk.

On 5 July 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted at least nine people, including a woman and her three children, in Akure North LGA, coded to Irese (Akure North, Ondo). One of the hostages escaped.

On 5 July 2024, Nigerian troops, in conjunction with CJTF and Hybrid Forces, killed 11 ISWAP fighters during a firefight in Jongo, Sambisa Forest in Bma LGA, coded to Banki (Bama, Borno). One Hybrid Forces fighter got injured. The troops recovered 99 rounds of 7.62mm x 54 ammo links, 19 rounds of 7.62mm x 39 special ammo, three AK-4 rifle magazines, 47 rounds of ammunition, two locally made guns, and two hand grenades.

On 5 July 2024, a Kaduna militia abducted a 79-year old man from his residence at Biniki community (Kauru, Kaduna). The abductee was the former president of the National Union of Electricity and Gas Workers which is now called NUEE. There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 5 July 2024, suspected Fulani pastoralists attacked and injured some Amotekun Corps officers on the Akure-Ado expressway in Akure (Akure South, Ondo). They came under attack while moving about 120 cows seized over the allegation that they grazed on a farm and destroyed farmlands in Osi and Igboba Communities. The Corps repelled the attack and evacuated the injured officers to the hospital. There were no fatalities.

On 5 July 2024, a Fulani militia engaged Amotekun Corps in an armed clash at Igoba (Akure North, Ondo) when the corps responded to a report of cows destroying farms in the area. One Amotekun operative was seriously wounded, others sustained different degrees of injuries and they retreated from the area.
On 5 July 2024, IS/BH fighters shot and killed the Bulama Bacha community leader around Horre Nayiwa in Gujba LGA, coded to Gujba (Yobe). They also set his house on fire.

On 6 July 2024, Nigerian troops and hunters ambushed Boko Haram fighters, attempting to blow up the powerline near Kasesa Village on the outskirts of Damaturu (Damaturu, Yobe). The militiamen abandoned their vehicle with two damaged tyres and blood stains from injuries sustained during the confrontation. The troops recovered eight improvised explosive devices (IEDs) with detonating cords. There were no fatalities.
On 6 July 2024, a Niger militia abducted five civilians from Garam community (Tafa, Niger). The abductees included a pregnant woman, and four other persons.

On 6 July 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted a juju priestess and eleven people in Egbo community (Ughelli South, Delta) while they were performing sacrifices. Five other persons had been abducted prior to that of the priestess' group.
On 6 July 2024, a policeman shot and injured a lady in the Oria- Abraka community, Abraka (Ethiope East, Delta).

On 6 July 2024, Nigerian troops of Operation Hadin Kai, with the Hybrid Forces and CJTF, killed four Boko Haram fighters during a confrontation in the Sambisa Forest area in Bula Dalo, coded to Bula Dadobe (Bama, Borno). The troops recovered 80 rounds of 7.62mm x 54 metal links, 2 FN rifle magazines, and 2 G3 rifle magazines.
On 6 July 2024, soldiers raided the camp of a Kaduna militia in Iche forest, Kagarko LGA (Kaduna). 162 cattle that were previously rustled by the militia were recovered, casualties are unknown.

On 6 July 2024, a Katsina militia numbering up to 100 who were dressed in hijabs killed one person and abducted 22 to 25 residents from Runka village (Safana, Katsina). The abductees 14 of whom were members of the same family included men, women and children, residents claimed that the assailants may have been coordinated from three camps.

On 6 July 2024, a Kaduna militia abducted two journalists and some members of their families from their homes in Danhono 2 community (Chikun, Kaduna). The wife of one of the journalists was released on the same day because of health issues. The hostages were released on 12 July 2024 after six days in captivity. There was no report of ransom payment.
On 6 July 2024, ISWAP fighters abducted three people who were fetching firewood in Awulari village in Bama LGA, coded to Garno (Bama, Borno). The militia demanded a million-naira ransom.

On 6 July 2024, Boko Haram (JAS) clashed with ISWAP in Kwatar Shalla Shuwari, coded to Mafa (Mafa, Borno). They killed sixteen ISWAP fighters and seized eight water vessels, several weapons, and a large amount of cash (Naira).

On 6 July 2024, Boko Haram (JAS faction) militants clashed with ISWAP militants at Shuwari, Kwantan Kawule and Tumbun Rogo in Kukawa LGA (Borno), coded to Kukawa. An unspecified number of ISWAP militants were killed by the rival group who were from the Buduma faction of JAS and also seized eight water vessels carrying ISWAP fighters. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.
On 6 July 2024, ISWAP fighters shot and killed a community leader in the Mahadiya community in Gujba LGA, coded to Buni Yadi (Gujba, Yobe).
On 6 July 2024, a Zamfara militia shot and killed two people and injured two others after setting up a checkpoint along the Birnin Yero- Jangeru Road, coded to Jangeru (Shinkafi, Zamfara).

On 30 July 2024, a joint security team (likely the military and the police) engaged the IPOB/ESN in a firefight while raiding their hideout in Isseke (Ihiala, Anambra). The shooting triggered panic in the area. There were no fatalities.

On 30 July 2024, suspected IPOB militants opened fire and killed a police officer and a resident in the Nworieubi community (Mbaitoli, Imo). The attackers emerged from a bush and opened fire on the people. Many people were injured in the shooting. There were two fatalities.
On 30 July 2024, the Aye (Black Axe) clashed with the Buccaneers on the Osun State University campus in Okuku (Odo-Otin, Osun). Unknown fatalities.
On 30 July 2024, an unidentified armed group killed two people and abducted 20 others, including 18 women, in Tsamaye (Sabon Birni, Sokoto). No further information is available.

On 30 July 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed two police officers while trying to abduct a former MP on a church premises located on Ogajifo Street in Asaba (Oshimili South, Asaba). The armed group took away the former MP and her children, while her driver and a passerby were also killed in the incident. The hostages were released on 9 August 2024. There were four fatalities.

On 30 July 2024, a Plateau militia abducted one person from his residence in Anguldi, coded to Bukuru (Jos South, Plateau). The militants demanded a fifteen million naira ransom for the release of the hostage.

Around 30 July 2024 (as reported), the Nigerian troops engaged a Benue militia in a firefight at Gbeji- Afia near Chito (Ukum, Benue). The militants were riding on motorcycles when they encountered the troops, and the gunbattle ensued. The militia leader was shot dead, while others escaped with gunshot wounds. The troops recovered one AK 47 rifle and magazine, seven rounds of 7.62MM special ammunition, two mobile phones, and assorted charms

On 30 July 2024, the Nigerian troops and CJTF clashed with IS/ Boko Haram (JAS), killing two in Lantari, Mojori, Bula Malo, and Baramari villages in Bama LGA, coded to Bama (Borno). They recovered arms and ammunition.

On 30 July 2024, suspected IPOB militants enforcing a 'sit at home' order shot a man at Orji (Owerri North, Imo). The militants moved to the Nkwo Orji market, where they set the Imo State Government Waste Management Agency vehicle on fire, coded separately. Many traders scampered for safety and abandoned their wares.
On 31 July 2024, the Eiye and the Vikings clashed and injured one cult member in Obiaruku, also Obiaruku Quarters (Ukwuani, Delta).

On 31 July 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked and killed four police officers on duty at Orji Road in Owerri (Owerri Municipal, Imo). They took away the police rifles. The killing triggered panic and caused residents to scamper for safety. There were shootings in different parts of the city, including the Ikenegbu area, Wethedral Road, Government House, and Okigwe Road.

On 1 June 2024, an unidentified armed group, suspected to be members of the host community, abducted and killed a student of Alex-Ekwueme Federal University, Ndufu Alike Ikwo (Ikwo, Ebonyi). The decomposing body of the victim was recovered under the bridge at Ako stream in Nwakpu village on 17 June 2024. The police arrested four suspects.
On 1 June 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked a police station at Orokam (Ogbadibo, Benue). At least one policeman was injured.
On 1 June 2024, Black Axe militia also called Aiye and SVC militia clashed at the Auchi polytechnic campus 2 gate (Etsako West, Edo). Two people were killed.
On 1 June 2024, suspected Fulani pastoralists shot and killed a man at Opanda (Uzo Uwani, Enugu). The victim was coming from Adani to Opanda when he was attacked.
On 1 June 2024, suspected Fulani pastoralists gang-raped a 13-year-old girl and killed another man trying to rescue the girl in Ugwu-Uvuru (Uzo Uwani, Enugu).
On 1 June 2024, an unidentified armed group killed a man at his residence in Akunba (Akoko South West, Ondo).

On 1 June 2024, a Plateau militia waylaid two Rigwe youths on a motorcycle while returning from the Gero mining site, coded to Gero (Jos South, Plateau). They killed one of the victims and injured the other.

Around 1 June 2024 (as reported), an unidentified armed group abducted 5 civilians along Takum - Katsina-Ala road (Takum, Taraba). The victims include the brother of a retired general, his wife, daughter and two other women. The man was released after an undisclosed amount was paid as ransom, the abductors refused to release his wife and daughter and one of the other women escaped around 30 June.
On 1 June 2024, Black Axe militia also called Aiye and Maphites clashed at different locations in Benin City (Oredo, Edo) including Idokpa Auchi road and Agbor road. Two militia members were killed.
On 1 June 2024, a presumed unidentified cult militia killed a member of an unidentified cult militia at the 3rd East Circular road in Benin City (Oredo, Edo).
On 2 June 2024, a Niger militia abducted six people from Adogo Mallam near Mashegu (Mashegu, Niger).

On 2 June 2024, a Niger militia abducted thirty people from Kankuru village, a kilometer away from Kuchi (Muya, Niger). They proceeded to Adogon-Mallam and Tungan-Kawo villages and abducted 26 people there on 2 and 3 June, coded separately.

On 2 June 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted a woman around the Federal Science Technical College, Ijebu Imushin (Ijebu East, Ogun). The hostage was on a motorcycle with her daughter when the armed group waylaid them and dragged her into their vehicle. No ransom was demanded.
On 2 June 2024, Black Axe militia also called Aiye, clashed with SVC militia at Osisioma (Osisioma, Abia). Casualties are unknown.
On 2 June 2024, Black Axe militia also called Aiye and SEC militia clashed in the vicinity of Olode (Egbeda, Oyo). One militia member was killed.
On 2 June 2024, ISWAP militants fired mortar rounds targeting a position of state force, coded as military forces at Malam Fatori (Abadan, Borno). Casualties are unknown.
On 2 June 2024, a Taraba militia shot and killed the village head of Usmanu in Karim Lamidu LGA, coded to Karim Lamido (Taraba). Many residents fled the community.

On 2 June 2024, Nigerian troops clashed with a Kaduna militia attempting to rustle cattle from a Fulani settlement in Gidan-Makeri near Janjala (Kagarko, Kaduna). The troops were on patrol around the Janjala-Gidan Makeri axis when they engaged the militia. They killed two members of the militia.

On 2 June 2024, Black Axe militia also called Aiye, attacked a member with an unidentified rival cult militia in a shop at Wire road in Benin City (Oredo, Edo). The targeted militia member escaped, one sales attendant was mistakenly killed.

On 2 June 2024, a Katsina militia shot and killed the Malumfashi LGA Administrative Secretary in Malumfashi (Katsina). The militia had traced him to his house before they finally caught him at the mosque. The assailants shot him while leaving the mosque after the evening prayer. His assassination might be related to his role in the peace and stability program in the council. The militias were not favorably disposed to the program.

On 3 June 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a local lawmaker and a youth leader at Isu (Onicha, Ebonyi). The duo were riding on a motorcycle when the assailants waylaid them and opened fire at them, killing the two. One of the victims was the councilor representing Enuagu ward in the Onicha Legislative Council, and the other was the Onicha LGA coordinator of the National Youth Council of Nigeria.
On 3 June 2024, Black Axe also called Aiye militia clashed with Maphite militia at Siluko road (Ovia South West, Edo), coded to Iguobazuwa. One militia member was killed.

Around 3 June 2024 (as reported), an unidentified armed group killed the father of a former Attorney-General of Nasarawa state around Akwanga (Akwanga, Nassarawa). He was abducted a few days before his killing, coded separately. His abductors killed him for refusing a ransom payment for his release.
On 3 June 2024, Black Axe also called Aiye militia members wounded a member of Maphite militia a KB estate in Ikpoba hill (Ikpoba Okha, Edo), coded to Idogbo.

On 3 June 2024, a Niger militia abducted about 20 people from communities around Tunga-Kawo, also called Kawo (Shiroro, Niger). They also rustled over two hundred cattle from the communities. The militia moved from house to house, selecting their victims without any interference.

On 3 June 2024, ISWAP abducted 4 civilians including an elderly man at an illegal vehicle checkpoint which they mounted at Azare (Hawul, Borno). The elderly man was later released, there are no reports on ransom payment or demands.

On 3 June 2024, ISWAP militants ambushed an engaged state forces, coded as military forces in an armed clash at Bula Yobe - Kote area (Bama, Borno). One soldier and an unspecified number of militants were killed, three soldiers were declared missing, unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 3 June 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted one person from El-Rufai Estate in the Kuchiko Resettlement Development Area (KRDA) of Bwari (Bwari, FCT). The armed group, numbering about sixteen, visited two houses but only succeeded in one due to the timely arrival of the military.

On 3 June 2024, a Katsina militia abducted two lecturers of the Federal University, Dutsin Ma (Dutsinma, Katsina). The militia raided their houses at the Government Reservation Area (GRA) and forced them out. The son of one of the lecturers was also abducted. Other residents were dispossessed of valuables items.

On 3 June 2024, police engaged a Plateau militia in a firefight and killed two in the Fangha area of Daffo (Bokkos, Plateau). The militiamen attempted to abduct some people when the police were alerted and responded. Other militiamen escaped with gunshot wounds. The police recovered a locally fabricated revolver gun loaded with four 7.62MM rounds of ammunition, two phones, one dagger, and one knife.

On 3 June 2024, a Plateau militia shot and killed five people, including a pastor and his wife, in Kimakpa, coded to Kwal (Bassa, Plateau). The assailants attacked their victims in the middle of the night. Two other persons were injured during the attack.

On 3 June 2024, a Plateau militia shot and killed two people out of the three people returning from the farm around Miango (Bassa, Plateau). The third person hid in the bush and escaped from the assailants. The incident took place on the same day a pastor and four other people were killed in the area, coded separately.

On 3 June 2024, suspected Fulani pastoralists attacked and injured between six and ten people in the Antsa community (Makurdi, Beneu). They attacked the people with knives and machetes around 1 am when some residents were still drinking in the community. The assailants fled when the military arrived and started shooting (no confrontation). The attack triggered a demonstration in the community, coded separately.

On 3 June 2024, suspected Fulani pastoralists attacked and injured people with machetes in Akawe Torkula Polytechnic at North Bank (Makurdi, Benue). They fled when the military arrived and started shooting (no confrontation).

On 3 June 2024, a Niger milita (described as bandits) abducted a groom during his wedding ceremony in Papiri (Agwara, Niger). The attackers accused his fiance of having a romantic relationship with a Niger milita leader.

On 3 June 2024, a Niger militia (described as bandits) fired warning shots and abducted two civilians on the Zungeru-Tegina road, location coded to Tegina (Rafi, Niger) while the militia were crossing the road with stolen cattle.

On 4 June 2024, a Kogi militia abducted a pastor's wife from her residence in Lokoja (Lokoja, Kogi). The abductors were said to have trailed the woman from an eatery to her house and sporadically opened fire to scare off the people before they took her away. They demanded a 32-million-naira ransom for the release of the hostage.

On 4 June 2024, police clashed with an unidentified armed group attacking the Divisional Police headquarters in Ezzamgbo, also spelt as Ezamgbo (Ohaukwu, Ebonyi). The armed group, numbering about eight, invaded the police station and opened fire sporadically before the police repelled them. The confrontation triggered panic in the area and disrupted the palliative sharing program organized by the LGA chairman. The attackers set a vehicle and motorcycle ablaze while retreating. There were no fatalities.

On 4 June 2024, a Katsina militia (for three days) carried out multiple attacks on about 13 communities in Dutsinma LGA, coded to Dogon Ruwa (Dutsinma, Katsina) and Safana LGA, coded separately. They killed between 27 - 40 people in the attacks, plundered the communities and rustled animals. The attacks forced the residents to desert their homes. The communities affected included Tashar Kawai Mai Zurfi, Sabon Gari Unguwar Banza, Dogon Ruwa, Sanawar Kurecen Dutsi, Unguwar Bera, Kuricin Kulawa, Larabar Tashar Mangoro, Sabaru, Ashata, Unguwar Ido, Kanbiri, Kunamawar Mai Awaki and Kunamawar 'Yargandu. Twenty-seven fatalities shared across six events (two LGAs for three days). Five fatalities coded.

Around 4 June 2024 (as reported), a Kaduna militia tortured and killed a pharmacist abducted from Ida, coded to the place of abduction, Ida (Kagarko, Kaduna). The victim was abducted with fifteen others on 8 May 2024 while watching a football match at a community viewing center.
On 4 June 2024, Maphites killed a member of Black Axe militia, also called Aiye at Agbor road (Ikpoba Okha, Edo) coded to Idogbo.

On 4 June 2024, the police in the anti-scavenging task force shot and killed a scraps dealer and injured another person in Abakpa Texaco near Abakpa Nike (Enugu East, Enugu). The victims were shot for resisting the Task Force from confiscating their multi-millionaire naira worth of goods in their depot. The shooting triggered panic, and the whole Abakpa Texaco area was deserted.
On 4 June 2024, Black Axe militia also called Aiye and SEC militia clashed in Atan (Ado-Odo, Ogun). One person was killed.

On 5 June 2024, suspected Boko Haram (JAS) fighters abducted four Christian youths from a bus around Kamuya village (Biu, Borno). The militia selectively picked the Christian passengers on the bus. They killed three of the hostages. The whereabouts of the fourth person are not known.
On 5 June 2024, Black Axe also called Aiye and SVC militia clashed at Heaven street, near the Auchi polytechnic campus gate (Etsako West, Edo). One militia member was killed.

On 5 June 2024, police and KADVIS engaged a Kaduna militia in a firefight while attempting to abduct the Paramount Ruler of Ninzo Chiefdom at his palace in Fadan-Ninzo (Sanga, Kaduna). Around 5 June 2024 (as reported), a Niger militia shot a seven-year-old boy dead in Kapana village (Muya, Niger). The boy was one of many people abducted from the community, but they later shot him dead when he could not trek well due to his ailment.

On 5 June 2024, a Niger militia attacked and killed three people in Bassa (Shiroro, Niger). They abducted scores of people and rustled many cattle in the village. Four villagers who fled the attack drowned while returning home on the following day.

On 5 June 2024, a Niger militia shot and killed at least seven people and abducted twenty others in the communities in the Lakpma area coded to Gwadara Irina (Shiroro, Niger). The later moved to Roro and killed one person, coded separately.
On 5 June 2024, a Niger militia shot and killed an unspecified number of young men aged 20 to 35 in the Roro community (Shiroro, Niger). Unspecified fatalities coded as 3.

On 5 June 2024, a Zamfara militia clashed with the police and the Community Protection Corps while trying to attack the Magarya community in Kanwa ward (Zurmi, Zamfara). They killed thirteen people, including seven police, one Community Protection Corps member and five residents trying to flee the village during the attack. They set Magarya Model Primary School, a car and a set of furniture on fire. The attack triggered an exodus of people from the village. They also rustled three camels and some cows, sheep and goats.
On 5 June 2024, Black Axe militia also called Aiye, clashed with SVC militia at World Bank area of Aba (Aba South, Abia). An unspecified number of militia members were wounded.
On 5 June 2024, Black Axe militia also called Aiye, clashed with SVC militia at Jos (Jos South, Plateau). One militia member was killed.

On 5 June 2024, a Niger militia attacked Unguwar- Madi village, coded to Elena, also spelt as Irina (Shiroro, Niger). The attack triggered an exodus of the villagers from their homes, and sought refuge at Elena. There were no fatalities.

On 5 June 2024, a Niger militia attacked farmers in Kasmani village in Shiroro LGA, coded to Shiroro (Niger). They set many houses and property on fire. Dozens of farmers consequently fled the community. They sought refuge at Elena. There were no fatalities.
On 5 June 2024, an unidentified cult militia killed a member of a rival militia at Odobo junction, near Evbuotubu market junction (Egor, Edo).
On 5 June 2024, Black Axe militia also called Aiye clashed with Maphite militia members at a bar in Benin City (Oredo, Edo). One militia member was killed.

On 5 June 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked and killed an unspecified number of civilians at different communities in Oke-Ogun (Kajola, Oyo) coded to Okeho. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.
