On 6 June 2024, suspected Ikale communal militia shot and killed a man on his farm in Igbobini (Okitipupa, Ondo). The victim was an indigene of Igbobini, and his killing connected to land ownership disputes between the two communities.
On 6 June 2024, a communal clash took place in Oghara (Ethiope West, Delta) and one person was killed.
On 6 June 2024, ISWAP militants fired mortar rounds targeted at position of state forces, coded as military forces at Banki town (Bama, Borno). Casualties are unknown.
On 7 June 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted at least seventeen people in Boraye village, Gada district, coded to Gada (Bungudu, Zamfara).
On 7 June 2024, the Aye (Black Axe) and the Vikings cult militias clashed and killed one militiaman in Emene (Enugu East, Enugu).

On 7 June 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a man abducted in Jilli village (Gubio, Borno). The abductors claimed they killed the hostage when he attempted to escape their custody. They released his body after his family paid a 5 million naira ransom out of the 10 million naira demanded.

On 7 June 2024, NSCDC officials abducted a businessman at Amaedim Ngwogwo community in Ishiagu (Ivo, Ebonyi) over a land related dispute. The NSCDC claimed the abductee was arrested for obstructing a land matter in the community.

Around 7 June 2024 (as reported), some hunters arrested, tortured and killed a 14-year-old teenager in Maiha LGA, coded to Maiha (Maiha, Adamawa), over the suspicion of stealing 20,000 naira. The police arrested the hunters.

On 7 June 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted at least 30 travelers including several students at Uke (Karu, Nassarawa) as they were travelling to Abuja from Nassarawa state. There are no reports on ransom demands. The families of two of the victims were contacted and a ransom of 10 million naira each was demanded. The abductees were released on 11 June after a collective ransom of 40 million naira was paid.

On 7 June 2024, suspected Boko Haram fighters numbering about fifty, attacked and killed twenty people in Bassa (Shiroro, Niger). Ten youths among the victims were beheaded for refusing to join the militant group. The militia had threatened the villagers who refused to join them not to return to their homes; otherwise, they would be killed. The victims returned to the village to get some food items for their families at the IDP camp when the Boko Haram fighters attacked them.

On 7 June 2024, police forces in collaboration with the DSS and hunters raided the hideouts of an unidentified armed group in Gidan Dogo (Kachia, Kaduna) and Kweti forest (coded separately). Four members of the group were arrested, the camps were destroyed and abductees were rescued. Casualties are unknown.
On 7 June 2024, an unidentified armed group injured many people while raiding a residence around Rafin Zurfi (Bauchi). They went away with an undisclosed amount of money and some valuable items.

On 7 June 2024, police and the Katsina Community Watch clashed with a Katsina militia and killed three militiamen in Duva village, Maibakko (Sabuwal, Katsina). The militiamen were intercepted while trying to abduct some women from the village. They opened fire at the police, and the police responded, killing them and thwarting the abduction. The police rescued all the hostages.

On 7 June 2024, police forces in collaboration with the DSS and hunters raided the hideouts of an unidentified armed group in Kweti forest (Kachia, Kaduna) , coded to Kachia, and Gidan Dogo (coded separately). Four members of the group were arrested, the camps were destroyed and abductees were rescued. Casualties are unknown.
On 7 June 2024, a suspected unidentified cult militia clashed with soldiers and wounded three of them at the Okomu oil palm plantation (Ovia South West, Edo).

On 7 June 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a top PDP politician while driving around the Neke Odenigbo community (Isi Uzo, Enugu). The victim was an aspirant for Isi-Uzo LGA chairperson. His assassination was not unrelated to his political aspiration and growing popularity in the area. Other sources report that a former councilor of Ikem 1 ward who was the victim was abducted by the assailants who demanded for a ransom of 100 million naira.

Around 7 June 2024 (as reported), an unidentified armed group were engaged in an armed clash by an off-duty soldier who disarmed a member of the group after they abducted him along Ekpoma - Okene - Lokoja road (Esan West, Edo). The soldier rescued himself and other civilian abductees, he also recovered a pistol. Casualties are unknown.
On 7 June 2024, two unidentified cult groups clashed and killed a rival member along Ngwa Road, Aba North LGA, coded to Ehere (Aba North, Abia).

On 8 June 2024, military troops of Operation Udo Ka engaged IPOB militants in an armed clash at Igboro forest in Arochukwu LGA (Abia). 6 militants were killed, one soldier was wounded, arms, ammunition and 3 IEDs were recovered in the operation which was a reprisal by the troops over a previous attack that happened on May 30.
On 8 June 2024, a Kaduna militia killed one civilian and abducted 31 others at Kokob village in Kufana ward (Kajuru, Kaduna). The abductees consisted of 24 females and 7 males.

On 8 June 2024, an unidentified armed group killed nine civilians at Tarorshi and Apirgwa villages in Kente ward (Wukari, Taraba). An unspecified number of persons were injured and properties were destroyed.
On 8 June 2024, the Buccaneers cult militia and the Eiye clashed at the Moshood Abiola Polytechnic, Abeokuta (Abeokuta South, Ogun). No further details.

On 8 June 2024, the Nigerian troops engaged a Katsina militia in a firefight after the militia abducted at least ten people and rustled sixteen cows in Gidan-Maga village, Malumfashi LGA, coded to Unguwar Mai Rabo (Malumfashi, Katsina). The troops rescued the hostages and recovered the rustled cows. There were no fatalities.
On 8 June 2024, an unidentified armed group killed two civilians at Tse-Deke village (Wukari, Taraba). An unspecified number of persons were injured and properties were destroyed.
On 9 June 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted one person from Kinnari village (Mobbar, Borno).
On 9 June 2024, the Vikings cult militia killed an Aye (Black Axe) member at Railway Orie in Emene (Enugu East, Enugu).
On 9 June 2024, a Kaduna militia shot and injured one person and abducted three others in the Angwar Daniel community, coded to Unguwar Danbaki (Chikun, Kaduna).

On 9 June 2024, an unidentified armed group of five abducted a retired school principal from his residence at Ikot Abassi (Mkpat Enin, Akwa Ibom). The victim was blindfolded and taken away on a motorcycle, a ransom of 20 million was demanded.

Around 9 June 2024 (as reported), troops of Operation Whirl Punch conducted fighting patrols and engaged a Kaduna militia in an armed clash at Dantarau community in Kajuru LGA (Kaduna). 5 militia members were killed, weapons and ammunition were recovered.
On 9 June 2024, a Niger militia killed a man while he was working on his farm at Kuchini community (Shiroro, Niger) coded to Kuta.

On 9 June 2024, an unidentified armed group and Nigerian army troops who responded to a distress call engaged in an armed clash along Ughelli - Patani road (Ughelli North, Delta). An unspecified number of civilians who were abducted while they were traveling in a commercial vehicle were rescued. Some occupants of the vehicle were declared missing.
On 9 June 2024, ISWAP fighters gathered 100 civilians and opened fire on them, killing an unspecified number of people in Doro Naira (Kukawa, Borno). Unspecified fatalities coded as 10.
On 9 June 2024, a Niger militia abducted two civilians from Guyi Kushaku village in Galadima ward, coded as Galadima Kogo (Shiroro, Niger). There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 9 June 2024, a Katsina militia ambushed policemen and Katsina state community corps officials at Kurmeji in Kankara LGA (Katsina) when they responded to a distress call. Four policemen and two community corps members were killed.

On 9 June 2024, a Katsina militia attacked and killed between 28 to 50 farmers at Gidan Boka, Dan-Nakwabo in Kankara LGA (Katsina) and Yargoje (coded separately). 28 fatalities split across 2 events coded as 14.
On 9 June 2024, the Vikings cult militia killed an Aye (Black Axe) militiaman in the Aguoye area of Awka LGA (Awka South, Anambra)

On 9 June 2024, a Kaduna militia abducted a catholic priest from the church's rectory at Zaman Dabo community (Zangon Kataf, Kaduna). The abductee was released on 10 June 2024, there are no reports on ransom demands and payment.

On 5 April 2024, an unidentified armed group blocked the road and attacked some Muslims going for night prayer in Minna (Minna, Niger).There were no fatalities.

Around 5 April 2024, an unidentified armed group suspected to be assassins killed a lawyer at his hometown, Orodo (Mbaitoli, Imo). The victim's decomposing body was found on 5 April, and the reason for the attack is unknown.

On 5 April 2024, police forces in collaboration with Nigerian navy and army troops clashed with unidentified armed groups in Amiyi and Ochuche areas of the forest (Ogbaru, Anambra) coded to Atani. Hideouts of the armed groups were raided and destroyed, 9 IEDs were recovered and defused by the police during the operation that lasted several hours. Casualties are unknown.

On 5 April 2024, a Katsina militia attacked Tuge village (Musawa, Katsina) and killed three people, including two males and the daughter of Tuge Ward's Councilor. They abducted the Tuge village head and another male resident. The militia looted and burned down many houses.
On 5 April 2024, a Katsina militia attacked a market and opened fire on the traders and buyers in Yan Tumaki (Dan-Musa, Katsina). They killed two people and injured many others.

On 5 April 2024, ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants ambushed Nigerian troops and engaged them in an armed clash around Kamuya village (Biu, Borno). One soldier was killed and four others were wounded, the troops pursued the militants to their hideout and engaged them in a clash (coded separately).

On 5 April 2024, Nigerian troops engaged Boko Haram/ ISWAP militants in an armed clash after they chased them to their hideout in the Timbuktu Triangle, coded to Damboa (Damboa, Borno). The militants had ambushed the troops (coded separately), 6 militants were killed, 5 rifles and 103 rounds of ammunition were recovered by the troops.

On 6 April 2024, a Niger militia ambushed a Yansakai militia that was on their trail and engaged them in an armed clash at Dogon Daji in Mariga LGA (Mariga, Niger). 30 Yansakai militia members and an unspecified number for the Niger militia were killed. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.
On 6 April 2024, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked and killed two farmers while they were on the way to their farm in Adani (Uzo Uwani, Enugu). The victims were siblings.

On 6 April 2024, a Kaduna militia abducted four farmers at Bishini community in Kagarko LGA (Kaduna). The victims were clearing their fields when they rounded up, there are no reports on ransom demands.

On 6 April 2024, a suspected unidentified cult militia clashed with policemen and a local defense militia member at Obidianso water front in Mile 1, Diobu (Port Harcourt, Rivers). One defense militia member was killed, during the raid which was based on intelligence that the cult militia was planning to attack a rival militia.

On 6 April 2024, a suspected unidentified cult militia killed a former member of a local defense militia at D-Line, Port Harcourt (Port Harcourt, Rivers). The victim was sacked from the defense militia over claims that he was involved in criminal and cult related activities, the reason for the attack is unknown.

On 6 April 2024, a Katsina militia engaged NSCDC officials in an armed clash when they attempted to attack a federal government owned silo in Dutsin Ma LGA (Dutsinma, Katsina). The militia was repelled and an unspecified number of them fled with injuries. The NSCDC claimed that the attack was an attempt to abduct the manger of the grain reserve.
On 6 April 2024, an unidentified group killed a businessman and abducted a lady who was commuting with him in his car along airport road in Uyo (Uyo, Akwa Ibom) as he was returning from his farm.

On 7 April 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted many travelers along Gidan Kano village (Talata Mafara, Zamfara) when they blocked the road in large numbers. One of the abductees was the officer in charge of Talata Mafara LGA, whose corpse was found the following day (coded separately).

On 7 April 2024, a Zamfara militia led by Kachalla Dankarami ambushed and clashed with another militia led by Dangote in Dumburum (Zurmi, Zamfara). Dangote and two of his brothers were killed, the clash was related to a clash between the two groups over stolen cattle. Dankarami, also called Goska was wounded and an unspecified number of his followers were killed. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 7 April 2024, ISWAP abducted an off-duty police officer travelling with his wife and children along Damboa- Biu road near Shokotoko, coded to Damboa (Damboa, Borno). The family was travelling for an Eid celebration when ISWAP fighters abducted them. They killed the police officer but released his wife and children.

On 7 April 2024, an unidentified armed group engaged a local defense militia who were guarding the home of the LGA chairman in an armed clash at Tokulo community (Bwari, FCT). Policemen responded and provided reinforcement which foiled the attack and one policeman was killed.
On 7 April 2024, two unidentified cult militias clashed in Awka (Awka South, Anambra). Three persons were killed in the clash.
On 7 April 2024, an unidentified armed group killed a civilian in Gwer West LGA coded to Naka (Gwer West, Benue). Several other persons were wounded.
On 7 April 2024, an unidentified armed group killed four civilians including one who was beheaded in Ikpele (Agatu, Benue). Three other victims were amputated.

On 7 April 2024, a suspected Fulani militia clashed with soldiers, police forces and neighborhood watch operatives who trailed them in Ikem (Isi Uzo, Enugu) after the militia abducted a woman. The abductee was released following the gunshots from the security agents. Casualties are unknown.

On 8 April 2024, an unidentified armed group wounded a civilian and shot at the tires of a vehicle when they laid siege on the Otukpo-Adoka-Oweto highway (Apa, Benue) coded to Ugbokpo. One woman was also abducted.

On 8 April 2024, presumed soldiers killed two aides of the rivers state gubernatorial candidate of the NRM and arrested him from his residence at Usokun (Degema, Rivers). The man who also a former militant leader in the Niger-Delta, the police claimed it was another security agency that carried out the operation and sources described them dressed in military uniform. The reason for the attack and arrest is unknown, the NRM candidate was released on 10 April.

Around 8 April 2024 (as reported), the Nigerian troops attacked and cleared some Zamfara communal militia camps in Babban Doma, coded to Baba-Doka (Maru, Zamfara), Maitukunya, Dansadau and Dangurgu. They killed several militiamen and captured some alive. Several fatalities coded as ten and split across four events coded as 2

Around 8 April 2024 (as reported), the Nigerian troops attacked and cleared some Zamfara communal militia camps in Dan Sadau (Maru, Zamfara), Maitukunya, Babban Doma and Dangurgu. They killed several militiamen and captured some alive. Several fatalities coded as ten and split across four events coded as 3.

Around 8 April 2024 (as reported), the Nigerian troops attacked and cleared some Zamfara communal militia camps in Dan-Gurgu (Maru, Zamfara), Maitukunya, Dansadau and Babban Doma. They killed several militiamen and captured some alive. Several fatalities coded as ten and split across four events coded as 2.

On 8 April 2024, a Zamfara militia killed the officer in charge of Talata Mafara LGA after he was abducted alongside other travelers that day before along Gidan Kano village (Talata Mafara, Zamfara). The militia dumped the victim's corpse in the bush and directed his family to where it was, they claimed to have killed him 20 hours after he was abducted.

On 8 April 2024, the Dan Karami camp of the Zamfara militia attacked the Kachalla Dan Chaki camp in an infighting in Dangara village, coded to Zurmi (Zurmi, Zamfara). Dan Karami attacked Kachalla Dan Chaki when he learned his plan to avenge the killing of his boss, Sani Dangote, whom Dan Karami had killed on 7 April 2024, coded separately. He killed Kachalla Dan Chaki and scores of his fighters. Scores coded as 20, in addition to the fatality of Kachalla Dan Chaki.

On 8 April 2024, a Zamfara militia was repelled by NSCDC operatives when they attempted to attack a community near the Federal College of Education in Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara). The militia fled and casualties are unknown.

Around 8 April 2024 (as reported), the Nigerian troops of the 145 Battalion in Damasak, with air support, attacked ISWAP fighters around Bulaburin, coded to Bula (Fika, Yobe). The troops killed an ISWAP fighter and dislodged others from the enclave. There was one fatality.

Around 8 April 2024 (as reported), the Nigerian troops attacked and cleared some Zamfara communal militia camps in Mai Tukunya (Tsafe, Zamfara), Dansadau, Babban Doma and Dangurgu. They killed several militiamen and captured some alive. Several fatalities coded as ten and split across four events coded as 3.

On 8 April 2024, a suspected Tiv militia attacked commuters who were traveling from Sukundi to Wukari (Wukari, Taraba) and killed three persons. Two other victims sustained varying degrees of injuries and the assailants stole two. Motorcycles belonging to the victims.

On 8 April 2024, Nigerian army troops raided the camp of a Zamfara militia led by Yellow Janbros and engaged them in an armed clash at Dangunu in Maru LGA (Zamfara). One militia member was killed, the camp was destroyed, firearms and 15 bags of stolen grains were recovered.

On 8 April 2024, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists killed a man and injured his son when they attacked them on their farm at Onicha-Ebia in Ikem (Isi Uzo, Enugu) and then abducted a man and his daughter from Umueje in Ikem-Etiti (Isi Uzo, Enugu).
On 9 April 2024, Klansmen and Black Axe militia engaged in an armed clash at Afaha Atai (Eket, Akwa Ibom). One person was killed after he resisted being abducted.
On 9 April 2024, Icelander and Greenlanders engaged in an armed clash at Amarata (Yenagoa, Bayelsa). One person was killed in the clash.

On 9 April 2024, the Nigerian troops of Operation Hadin Kai engaged Boko Haram (JAS) in a firefight and killed four at Ngauru Forest in Bama (Bama, Borno). The troops arrested seventeen Boko Haram family members and profiled them for rehabilitation. There were four fatalities.

Around 9 April 2024 (as reported), the Hybrid forces comprising the military, police, and State Security Service, in conjunction with CJTF, ambushed and killed four Boko Haram (JAS) fighters along Dikwa- Gajibo road, coded to Gajibo (Dikwa, Borno). The troops recovered food items and other logistic materials.

On 9 April 2024, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked and killed two IDPs on their farms in Umogidi (Otukpo, Benue). They injured two others and abducted one person. They demanded a five-million-naira ransom for the release of the hostage. The IDPs had left their camp at Adoka in search of food in their home before they were attacked. There were two fatalities.
On 9 April 2024, an unidentified armed group killed one person at the UNIZIK temporary site junction in Awka (Awka South, Anambra). The attack was related to an ongoing cult clash.

On 10 April 2024, the Nigerian troops attacked the Sani Tari camp of the Zamfara communal militia in Birnin Magaji LGA, coded to Birnin Magaji (Kiyawa, Zamfara). Sani Tari, the kingpin, escaped, but the Nigerian military killed several of his fighters. Several fatalities coded as 10.

On 10 April 2024, NSCDC shot and killed a woman in Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara) while they were chasing after armed youths. The victim was hit by a stray bullet at the Eid prayer ground and her death resulted in a riot (coded separately).

On 10 April 2024, soldiers beat up a journalist at Kuje (Kuje, FCT) as he was returning from work. The victim claimed that the soldiers attack residents from 9:30pm and accuse them of returning home late.

On 10 April 2024, the Nigerian troops clashed with suspected armed Fulani pastoralists after the pastoralists attacked Upu village (Otukpo, Benue). The pastoralists retreated and fled to the bush. There were no fatalities.

On 11 April 2024, the Nigerian police engaged the head of Orashi Marine Iceland Deck Cult in a firefight and shot him dead at his herbalist house in Ibusa (Oshimili North, Delta). The cultist has been on the police wanted list since 2017 for killing many people. He opened fire, trying to escape from the police, when the police invaded his hideout. The police recovered a tinted Black Toyota Highlander with an AK 47 rifle, Pump Action gun, Improvised Explosive Devices (IED), Police and Armed Camouflage.

On 11 April 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked a police checkpoint at the Isheke Junction on the outskirts of Abakaliki (Abakaliki, Ebonyi). One police officer was shot dead, and another was fatally injured. The armed group set a police patrol van on fire. There was one fatality.

On 11 April 2024, the Bilya Mai Logo Rumawa group of Katsina communal militia invaded another militia camp around the Rugu Forest in Safana LGA, coded to Safana (Safana, Katsina). The two rival camps engaged in a supremacy war, resulting in the killing of several militiamen. Several fatalities coded as 10.
On 11 April 2024, an unidentified armed group killed a driver at Chikara village (Kogi, Kogi) and abducted his 16 passengers. Six of the abductees were later released on the same day.

On 11 April 2024, an unidentified cult militia killed two suspected members of a rival militia at the Campus II gate of Auchi polytechnic in Auchi (Etsako West, Edo). The attack was related to a clash between rival militias.

On 11 April 2024, the Nigerian military invaded Olota (Ughelli South, Delta) in connection with the killing of 17 military officers in the neighboring Okuama community a few weeks back. They burned two houses and destroyed another. The troops beat and injured a community leader before taking him away with nine other suspects. They recovered four G3 rifles and magazines, one Pump Action Semi-Automatic Gun, three Sub-Machine Guns and magazines, as well as 476 live cartridges from the village. They also recovered five locally fabricated guns, a large plastic bag containing a substance suspected to be cannabis sativa and two-speed boats with 75 horsepower.

On 11 April 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted a Channel TV reporter from his home at Rumu-Osi (Obio, Rivers). The abductors demanded a 30 million naira ransom for his release. The armed group released the hostage on 12 April 2024, and no ransom payment was declared for his release.

On 11 April 2024, hunters clashed with Yan Babeli militia who were part of the entourage of the district head of Miri at Tashan Babiye in Bauchi (Bauchi, Bauchi) when the district head was making a procession to the state government house as part of the Eid celebration. Four persons including the son of the district head were killed in the clash, the district head claimed that the hunters attacked his entourage and planned to assassinate him.

On 11 April 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a former President General of Amansea Development Union at his residence in Amansea, also spelt as Amansee (Awka North, Anambra). The victim was offering morning prayer when the assailant entered his house and shot him point blank.

On 12 April 2024, suspected Fulani pastoralists attacked Mandung-Mashu, also called Mandung (Bokkos, Plateau) and Kopnanle villages, coded separately. The armed pastoralists shot and killed at least twelve people from the two villages. They also set fire to homes and worship places. Twelve fatalities split across two events coded as 6.

On 12 April 2024, troops of the joint task force of Operation Hadarin Daji carried out an offensive and engaged a Zamfara militia in an armed clash at Baba-Doka (Maru, Zamfara), Kaboro and Gobirawar Challi (coded separately). 12 militia members were killed, others fled with gunshot wounded and the troops recovered weapons, ammunition, 18 cows and 10 motorcycles. 12 fatalities split across 3 events coded as 4.

On 12 April 2024, troops of the joint task force of Operation Hadarin Daji carried out an offensive and engaged a Zamfara militia in an armed clash at Kaboro (Maru, Zamfara), Baba-Doka and Gobirawar Challi (coded separately). 12 militia members were killed, others fled with gunshot wounded and the troops recovered weapons, ammunition, 18 cows and 10 motorcycles. 12 fatalities split across 3 events coded as 4.

On 12 April 2024, overnight, an unidentified armed group attacked residents of Egan Oriomi in Oto Awori local council development area in Oto (Ojo, Lagos) over a leadership tussle. 10 persons were shot (it is unclear if they died), houses were broken into and set ablaze, and an unspecified number of persons were injured. A one-year old child was burned to death.

On 12 April 2024, an unidentified armed group killed two people and injured others after attacking some residents in the Maitubi area of Minna (Minna, Niger). They looted houses and shops. They also vandalized cars, tricycles and motorcycles.
Around 12 April 2024 (as reported), ISWAP and Boko Haram (JAS) clashed in Lake Chad, coded to Malam Fatori (Abadan, Borno). Scores of militia members were killed. Scores fatalities coded as 20.

On 12 April 2024, a Black Axe militia member also known as Aiye confraternity killed a civilian at Ile film, Bolanta area of Ilorin (Ilorin West, Kwara). The victim was shot for challenging the militia who were searching for a member of a rival group. Some sources claimed that the incident happened on 12 April, while the police claimed 13 April.

On 12 April 2024, suspected Fulani pastoralists attacked Kopnanle, coded to Tangu (Bokkos, Plateau) and Mandung-Mashu villages, coded separately. The armed pastoralists shot and killed at least twelve people from the two villages. They also set fire to homes and worship places. Twelve fatalities split across two events coded as 6.

On 12 April 2024, about 4 soldiers from the Nigerian Air Force beat up four staff of a hotel where an air force cadet drowned in Umuahia (Umuahia North, Abia). One of the staff was killed as a result of the beating while others sustained injuries.

On 12 April 2024, an unidentified cult militia shot and killed a man at UNIZIK Junction, Awka (Awka South, Anambra). The shooting added to a series of cult killings that occurred in the city in recent times.

On 12 April 2024, troops of the joint task force of Operation Hadarin Daji carried out an offensive and engaged a Zamfara militia in an armed clash at Gobirawar Challi in Maru LGA (Zamfara), Baba-Doka and Kaboro (coded separately). 12 militia members were killed, others fled with gunshot wounded and the troops recovered weapons, ammunition, 18 cows and 10 motorcycles. 12 fatalities split across 3 events coded as 4.

On 12 April 2024, two unidentified cult militias from Nasamu and Iyalode streets engaged in an armed clash at Ajegunle (Ajeromi, Lagos). One person was killed after he sustained injuries and was taken to a hospital where he died, six commercial vehicles were vandalized and two suspects were arrested by the police.

On 12 April 2024, suspected armed pastoralists shot and wounded a man, abducted his wife and their house help in Makurdi (Makurdi, Benue). The man was the former chief of staff of former governor Ortom, they were returning from his farm when the assailants attacked. A ransom of 100 million naira was demanded. The abductees were released on 16 April after an undisclosed amount was paid as ransom.

On 13 April 2024, a Kaduna militia killed two abductees around Rijana forest (Kachia, Kaduna) after they were abducted from Azzara (coed separately). The abductees were killed over their inability to pay a ransom of 5 million naira.

On 13 April 2024, an unidentified armed group ambushed Benue state livestock guards and community volunteer guards at Mbabuande (Gwer West, Benue) and killed six of them. The guards were deployed to provide security for a family that was burying their relative in the community.

On 13 April 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked a group of mourners who were part of a burial procession at Edikwu Ankpali, coded as Ankpali (Apa, Benue) and killed one person. The victim and others in the procession were IDPs, and were forced to flee to the Ugbokpo IDP community after the attack.

On 13 April 2024, an unidentified cult militia attacked and wounded a motorcycle rider with a machete at Ile-Alawo compound, Igboro area of Ilorin (Ilorin West, Kwara). The reason for the attack is unknown and the victim who sustained an injury to his head was taken to an unknown location by his brother. Fatality is unknown.
On 13 April 2024, suspected Fulani pastoralists attacked the Mbar settlement near Bokkos (Bokkos, Plateau), killing three defense communal militia.

On 13 April 2024, suspected Fulani pastoralists attacked GSS Kopyal and Baba Rafi in Bokkos LGA, coded to Bokkos (Bokkos, Plateau). They killed two people and injured four others. They also rustled cattle from the villages.
On 13 April 2024, an unidentified armed group killed 14 civilians when they attacked Jaroa community, coded to Naka (Gwer West, Benue).

On 13 April 2024, Yoruba Nation agitators clashed with police forces and other security agents, coded as military forces at the Oyo state government secretariat in Agodi (Ibadan North, Oyo). The agitators attempted to take over the secretariat and declare independence of the Yoruba nation, some of them manned the house of assembly entrance and other were in front of the governor's office. 20 of the Agitators were arrested by the police, weapons, cartridges and an Odu'a nation flag were recovered.

Around 14 April 2024 (as reported), an unidentified cult militia attacked and killed two persons at Amuzu and Ezzama communities (Ezza South, Ebonyi). The victims were a motorcycle mechanic and a wheel barrow pusher.
On 14 April 2024, an unidentified cult militia killed a suspected member of a rival militia at South Ibie (Etsako West, Edo). The attack is related to clashes between rival militias.

On 14 April 2024, suspected unidentified cult militias from rival groups engaged in clashes at Baboko, Ile Onimago, Adabata and Eruda areas of Ilorin (Ilorin West, Kwara) using stones and broken bottles. Police forces from C division were deployed to quell the clashes, casualties are unknown. The policemen arrested 46 suspects, 14 of whom they claimed had links to the cult clashes.

On 15 April 2024, members of the Enugu state neighborhood watch shot and killed a restaurant owner at Ogrute junction in Enugu-Ezike (Igbo Eze North, Enugu). The victim was shot in the back following an altercation between him and the assailants who tried to arrest a client from the restaurant.

Around 15 April 2024 (as reported), soldiers ambushed and engaged a Kaduna militia in an armed clash at Rafin Sarki village in Giwa LGA (Kaduna). Two militia members were killed and the soldiers recovered a rifle, ammunition and a locally fabricated revolver frame.

Around 15 April 2024, a Zamfara communal militia abducted an unknown number of people while raiding Gidan Dan Zara village in Zurmi (Zurmi, Zamfara). They also burned two vehicles and stole food items.
On 15 April 2024, a Zamfara militia attacked and killed one person and injured two others in Kwalawa village near Birnin Magaji (Kiyawa, Zamfara).
On 15 April 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted nine people from Dumfawa village, coded to Gurbi (Zurmi, Zamfara).

On 15 April 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted a student from his off-campus hostel in Nsukka (Nsukka, Enugu). The abductee was a campus blogger and the abductors arrived in a Hilux vehicle and a jeep. There are no details on ransom demands.
On 15 April 2024, a suspected Zamfara militia killed the Zamfara state secretary of the PDP at the front of his residence in Tsafe (Tsafe, Zamfara).

On 15 April 2024, the Nigerian troops killed an unspecified number of Zamfara communal militia in Maru LGA, coded to Maru (Maru, Zamfara). They destroyed the militia's camps. The troops recovered ten operational motorbikes and 18 rustled cows. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.
On 15 April 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked a community along Naka - Adoka road (Gwer West, Benue). Six persons were killed and their bodies were recovered, many others were injured.
Around 15 April 2024 (month of), two unidentified rival cults clashed in the Ikorodu area (Ikorodu, Lagos), killing 3 people for unknown reasons.

Around 15 April 2024 (month of), ISWAP/Boko Haram (JAS) members abducted 40 people, including children and women, in Muya LGA, coded to the LGA HQ Sarkin Pawa (Muya, Niger). They were rescued at the beginning of July 2025, after some of the women had been forcibly married and held at an unspecified location in Muya LGA.
On 16 April 2024, a Kaduna militia killed two civilians in Anguwan Tanko Dogon Sarki and abducted some locals from Tashar Keji, both under Kakangi (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna).

Around 16 April 2024 (as reported), an unidentified armed group that attempted to abduct civilians were engaged in an armed clash by military forces who responded to a distress call at Zaki Biam (Ukum, Benue). One of the assailants was killed, a beretta pistol with four rounds of ammunition was also recovered by the troops.

Around 16 April 2024 (week of), a Kebbi communal militia abducted two people from Suru LGA, coded to Suru (Suru, Kebbi). A joint security team involving the military, NSCDC, DSS and Zuru communal defence militia trailed the abductors to Zugu Liba forest and rescued the hostages.

On 16 April 2024, a Kaduna militia abducted nine people in Unguwar Iya in Jere (Kagarko, Kaduna). They demanded a 30-million-naira ransom for their release. They later released the hostages on 15 June 2024 after collecting a 16-million-naira ransom and killing the ransom bearer, coded separately.

On 16 April 2024, an unidentified armed group suspected to have come from Obbo-Ayegunle community in Kwara state seriously wounded one person when they attacked the local government secretariat in Eda-Oniyo (Ilejemeji, Ekiti). The assailants vandalized the building and other council property and the attack was related to a land dispute between the two communities.
On 16 April 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted an unspecified number of people in transit between Mayanchi and Talata Mafara, coded to Talata Mafara (Talata Mafara, Zamfara).
On 16 April 2024, the Nigerian troops of 151 Battalion shot and killed a Boko Haram fighter in Banki Junction, Banki (Bama, Borno). The militiaman was alleged to be on an espionage mission.
On 16 April 2024, a Katsina militia shot and killed one person on the road between Birnin Gwari and Funtua, coded to Funtua (Funtua, Katsina).

On 16 April 2024, an unidentified armed group led by a suspected land grabber clashed with NURTW members at a motor park in Iyana-Ipaja, coded as Ipaja (Alimosho, Lagos). The clash was over control of the park, one transporter was killed, several other persons sustained bullet wounds.
On 16 April 2024, a Kaduna militia killed one civilian at Rafin Gora village, two kilometers aways from Dogon Dawa (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). Seven other persons were abducted by the militia.

On 17 April 2024, a Kaduna militia attacked Anguwar Danko, also spelt as Ungwan Danko (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna) and Kanawa, coded separately. They killed nineteen people and abducted many others. The militia also rustled cows in the community.
On 17 April 2024, a Kaduna militia abducted scores of civilians from Anguwan Doka in Kakangi (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). The militia shot sporadically during the attack.

On 17 April 2024, the Nigerian police and Community Watch engaged a Katsina militia in a firefight in Sabuwa (Sabuwa, Katsina) as the militia attempted to overrun the community. One Community Watch member sustained gun wounds, and a militia member got killed in the confrontation. Other members escaped with gun wounds. The police recovered one walkie-talkie as well as a military-grade hand grenade. There was one fatality.

On 17 April 2024, a customs operative shot and killed a civilian at Gamjin Makaho village, along Dankama road (Kaita, Katsina). The victim was one of the passengers in a truck, whose driver refused to stop at a customs checkpoint and was shot at by the operatives.

On 17 April 2024, EFCC operatives shot sporadically when the convoy of the Kogi state governor was leaving the home of the immediate past governor of the state at Wuse Zone 4 (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The EFCC had laid siege to the former governor's home in an attempt to arrest him, before the governor arrived and took him away which prompted the shooting. There were no casualties.

Around 17 April 2024 (as reported), the Nigerian troops, Hybrid Forces and CJTF clashed with ISWAP and killed scores of their fighters in Timbuktu Triangle, coded to Damboa (Damboa, Borno). Unspecified number of fatalities coded as 10.

On 17 April 2024, a policeman shot a businessman at a checkpoint along Aba - Owerri road (Aba South, Abia). The victim was heading home when an argument ensued between him and the policemen following is refusal to give a bribe of 500 naira and he died at a hospital on 19 April. The police claimed that the assailant was arrested.

On 17 April 2024, a Niger militia abducted a retired prison guard from along Ilorin - Minna road (Ilorin West, Kwara). The abductee was released on 28 April after soldiers invaded the abductors' camp (coded separately).

Around 17 April 2024 (as reported), ISWAP executed a CJTF member captured around Kukawa (Kukawa, Borno). They accused the victim of supporting the Nigerian military. His execution took place in an unknown place and was videoed and circulated online.

On 17 April 2024, a Kaduna militia attacked Kanawa, coded to Dogon Dawa (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna) and Ungwar Danko, coded separately. They killed four people and abducted many others. The militia also rustled cows in the community.

On 17 April 2024, an unidentified cult militia shot and killed a man in Awka (Awka South, Anambra). The victim was a tricycle revenue collector. The militia trailed him from the Ifite area and shot him at close range. The killing forced the traders in the area to close their shops and scamper for safety.

On 18 April 2024, a Plateau Militia attacked Tilengpat village (Pankshin, Plateau). The victims were mostly women. The attackers invaded the community at night and opened fire on the residents, killing between twelve and fifteen people. Fatalities coded as 12.

On 18 April 2024, a Plateau Militia attacked the Mandung community (Bokkos, Plateau), Butura and Chikam, coded separately. They sporadically fired at the residents and killed six people, including a student of Plateau State University in his off-campus hostel. Six fatalities split across three events coded as 2.

Around 18 April 2024 (as reported), the Nigerian troops repelled the IPOB attack and killed scores of the militia in Orkija (Ihiala, Anambra). The militia, armed with AK-47 rifles, were riding in two Lexus vehicles and motorbikes when they launched the attack on the Nigerian troops. One soldier died, and two others were injured. Scores of the militia and a Nigerian soldier were killed. There were at least 21 fatalities.

On 18 April 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed the traditional ruler of Sensani in his palace, also spelt as Sansani village (Gassol, Taraba). The assailants invaded the community on motorcycles at night and shot him dead. They also shot and wounded a motorcyclist who met them on the way as they were leaving. The monarch was killed at the time he was hosting the Nwonyo Fishing and Cultural Festival. The assailants went away with his two mobile phones. There was one fatality.

On 18 April 2024, a local defense militia clashed with armed Fulani pastoralists at the weekly market in Gada (Gada, Sokoto) following an attempt by the defense militia's leader to arrest a suspected cattle rustler that was seen at the market. On 19 April 2024, a Sokoto militia attacked and injured an unspecified number of people and abducted eight others in Gidan Sale, coded to Isa (Isa, Sokoto). The militia also burned houses, vehicles, and other property.

On 26 April 2024, the Nigerian troops clashed with a Sokoto militia and killed several militiamen in Gangara village (Sabon Birnin, Sokoto) and Tidibale, coded separately. Several fatalities coded as 10. Ten fatalities split across two events. There were five fatalities.
On 26 April 2024, the Aye (Black Axe) and Vikings cult militias clashed and killed an unspecified number of people in Bida Street, Makurdi (Makurdi, Benue). Unspecified fatalities coded as 3.
On 27 April 2024, the Eiye and Vikings clashed and killed one member along the Otokutu Egbo Road in Effurun (Uvwie, Delta).
On 27 April 2024, the Vikings and Aiye (Black Axe) clashed around the stadium in Abaliki (Abakaliki, Ebonyi). One person was killed during the confrontation.
On 27 April 2024, a Kaduna militia killed three hunters at Abashiya (Kachia, Kaduna) coded to Gidan Azara. 14 civilians were abducted by the militia.
On 27 April 2024, the Maphite clashed with the Aiye (Black Axe) in Ogida (Egor, Edo). An unspecified number of the militiamen were injured. There were no fatalities.

On 27 April 2024, an unidentified armed group killed an APC member in front of his residence at Supare (Akoko South West, Edo). The victim was a supporter of the state governor and served as returning officer during the just concluded governorship primaries in the state.
On 27 April 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a man at the D-Line area in Port Harcourt (Port Harcourt, Rivers).

On 27 April 2024, a Sokoto militia killed an unspecified number of people and abducted many others in Shalla village in Sabon Birni LGA, coded to Sabon Birni (Sabon Birni, Sokoto). Unspecified fatalities coded as 3.

On 28 April 2024, an unidentified armed group killed one persons and abducted an unspecified number of others at Nde 3 corners (Ikom, Cross River). Four of the abductees were rescued by the police (means not stated) and an unspecified number of abductees were not yet found.

On 28 April 2024, Nigerian troops attacked and killed over twenty fighters of a Katsina militia around Bichi Mallamawa mountains, coded to Mallamawa (Kafur, Katsina). The ground troops were supported by air strikes launched by the Nigerian Air Force. Top militia leaders and their family members were killed.

On 28 April 2024, CPG members and the Zurmi defence militia repelled an attack by a Zamfara militia in the Dauran Market, coded to Dauran Birnin Tsaba (Zurmi, Zamfara). The militia proceeded to Tukurawa village and killed three people, coded separately. There were no fatalities.

On 28 April 2024, a Zamfara militia attacked and killed three people in Tukurawa village, coded to Dumfawa (Zurmi, Zamfara). They chose Tukurawa after they were repelled in Daura market, coded separately.
On 28 April 2024, a suspected Fulani militia attacked civilians at Ugwuijoro Nimbo community, in Nimbo (Uzo Uwani, Enugu). Four to several persons were killed and many others were critically injured.

On 28 April 2024, a Kaduna militia opened fire indiscriminately and killed the driver of a moving vehicle at Dogon Fili along the Abuja-Kaduna highway, coded to Katari (Kachia, Kaduna). They abducted two others.
On 28 April 2024, a Sokoto militia ambushed and killed nine CJTF members while responding to a distress call in Isa LGA, coded to Isa (Isa, Sokoto). They injured three and abducted many others.
On 28 April 2024, a suspected Fulani militia attacked civilians between Egba and Ogbaulu (Agatu, Benue) and killed two persons. The victim were returning from an event when they were attacked.
On 28 April 2024, a suspected Fulani militia killed five civilians across three communities in (Agatu, Benue) coded to Bagagi. The affected communities are a fishing area bordering Nasarawa state.

On 28 April 2024, soldiers engaged a Niger militia in an armed clash at their hideout in the Kontagora axis (Kontagora, Niger) and rescued one abductee. The abductee was abducted on 17 April (coded separately), casualties are unknown.
On 28 April 2024, the Eiye cult militia killed a member of the Aye (Black Axe) cult in Benin city (Oredo, Edo).

On 28 April 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted six persons who were traveling from Naka (Gwer West, Benue) to Makurdi. The abductees consisted of staff of Benue state university, his four siblings and wife. There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 29 April 2024, a suspected Fulani militia killed one local defense militia member at Abavo (Ika South, Delta) when he tried to rescue two abducted farmers. One other farmer who was a former PDP chairman in Abavo ward 10 was killed.

On 29 April 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted at least 23 farmers from Gandasamu, Kadawa, Jabanda and Nasamu communities in Zurmi LGA (Zamfara). In response, Nigerian army troops were deployed to Zurmi following reports that members of some Zamfara militias were regrouping and mobilizing to attack the area.

On 29 April 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted a student and his father along Benin - Ose road, coded to Ifon (Ose, Ondo). A ransom of 25 million naira was demanded, the abductees were rescued two days later by Amotekun operatives and the Nigerian Navy.

On 29 April 2024, SEC also called Eiye and SVC also called Vikings cult militias clashed at Obiaruku Quarters (Ukwuani, Delta) over unspecified reasons. The clash lasted till the following day and an unknown number pf persons were killed. Fatalities coded as 3.

On 29 April 2024, a Kaduna militia killed a driver and abducted two people who were traveling in his vehicle a few kilometers away from Jere town (Kagarko, Kaduna). One of the abductees was a farmer and the assailants also stole 980,000 naira from him.
On 29 April 2024, the Rumuekini and Aluu communities clashed and killed three people over a land dispute in the Rumuekini community (Obio, Rivers).
On 29 April 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted a singer along Eklat road in Ughelli (Ughelli North, Delta). A ransom of $200,000 was demanded to be paid within seven days.
On 29 April 2024, the Maphite clashed with the Aiye (Black Axe) in Ogida (Egor, Edo). An unspecified number of the militiamen were injured. There were no fatalities.

On 29 April 2024, Nigerian troops of operation 'Whirl Stroke' engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash when they responded to reports of the group's activity at Pukun area of Fikyu (Ussa, Taraba). The armed group retreated, one rifle and ammunition were recovered by the troops, there were no fatalities.

Around 29 April 2024 (as reported), troops of Operation 'Hadarin Daji' and Yansakai militia repelled a Zamfara militia that destroyed food items and set ablaze Rijiyan Malladan and Harin Shala villages in Isa LGA (Sokoto). The attack by the militia was in retaliation of an airstrike by the troops (coded separately). Casualties are unknown.
On 29 April 2024, a Plateau militia abducted a man and a woman along Maraban Jama'a road in Jos LGA, coded to Jos (Jos North, Plateau). The Nigerian military rescued the hostages.

On 29 April 2024, an unidentified armed group engaged security personnel, coded as police forces in an armed clash when they responded to a distress call at Bmuko community in Bwari Area Council (FCT). Four civilians were abducted by the armed group.

Around 29 April 2024 (as reported), ground troops in collaboration with Yansakai militia conducted a mop up and clashed with a Zamfara militia led by Bello Turji in Makwaruwa, also called Makwarua (Sabon Birni, Sokoto), after an airstrike which was targeted at the militia. Three of the group's commanders were killed, 13 others sustained varying degrees of injuries, some fled to Kagara in Sokoto for treatment and Turji escaped.

On 29 April 2024, troops of sub-sector 1A of operation 'Whirl Stroke' engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash at Vingir village (Guma, Benue). The armed group fled, one suspected abductor was arrested with the sum of 40,000 naira and two phones, the troops recovered one rifle from the group's hideout. There were no fatalities.

Around 30 April 2024 (as reported), policemen beat up some male students of the state polytechnic in Ozoro (Isoko North, Delta) and later arrested them. The victims' offence is unknown, and they were arrested after a crowd began to film the incident.

On 30 April 2024, a Zamfara militia attacked civilians in Zurmi town (Zurmi, Zamfara) and killed one person. Four other persons were abducted, the militia attacked the town after the soldiers who were deployed there departed. The soldiers were deployed to prevent an attack by the militia following reports of a likely attack.

On 30 April 2024, two members of unidentified rival cult militias clashed at Eyenkoro area (Asa, Kwara) coded to Afon and one of them was killed. Three members of the deceased's militia were arrested by police forces after the attacked the city. Other sources report that two houses belonging to the father of the leader of a rival cult militia were set ablaze.

On 30 April 2024, an unidentified cult group, casually called 'Burkina Faso' clashed with the Vikings in Nenwe (Aninri, Enugu) over the allegation that the Vikings recruited a Burkina Faso member to their militia group. One Vikings member was injured. There were no fatalities.

On 30 April 2024, a Zamfara militia killed one person and injured a CPG officer in Zurmi LGA, coded to Gurbi (Zurmi, Zamfara). The assailants were disguised in women's robes and the Community Protection Guards uniforms while attacking the community.

On 30 April 2024, soldiers, a special police unit and community protection guards conducted operations and engaged Zamfara militias in armed clashes at Gidan Marke, coded as Marke (Tsafe, Zamfara), Yan Doton Daji , Fegin Baza and Gidan Dawa (coded separately). Several militia members were killed, and the troops recovered some items belonging to the militia at Ba'a Wata Ba area. Fatalities assumed to be 10, split across 3 events and coded as 3.

On 30 April 2024, soldiers, a special police unit and community protection guards conducted operations and engaged Zamfara militias in armed clashes at Fegin Baza and Gidan Dawa (Tsafe, Zamfara) coded to Tsafe, Yan Doton Daji and Gidan Marke (coded separately). Several militia members were killed, and the troops recovered some items belonging to the militia at Ba'a Wata Ba area. Fatalities assumed to be 10, split across 3 events and coded as 3.

On 30 April 2024, soldiers, a special police unit and community protection guards conducted operations and engaged Zamfara militias in armed clashes at Yan Doton Daji (Tsafe, Zamfara), Gidan Marke, Fegin Baza and Gidan Dawa (coded separately). Several militia members were killed, and the troops recovered some items belonging to the militia at Ba'a Wata Ba area. Fatalities assumed to be 10, split across 3 events and coded as 4.

On 30 April 2024, a suspected Fulani militia attacked civilians at Ajokpachi Odo community, coded to Agojeju-Odo (Omala, Kogi). Three persons were killed, motorbikes and foodstuff were stolen and scores of person were declared missing. Some members of the community claimed that the assailants were relocating from Benue state.

On 1 March 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked Ikobi (Apa, Benue). Attacks occurred concurrently in Edikwu Icho, Akpanta and Ugbobi villages, coded separately. The attackers killed five people altogether in the four villages. There were no fatalities in Ikobi.

On 1 March 2024, a Sokoto militia shot and killed the PDP Treasurer for Yabo LGA at his residence in the Dagawa community (Yabo, Sokoto). The militia also abducted a newlywed couple. No further details.

On 1 March 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked and killed two people in Akpanta (Apa, Benue). Attacks occurred concurrently in Edikwu Icho, Ikobi and Ugbobi villages, coded separately. The attackers killed five people altogether in the four villages. Fatality split across 2 events coded to 2.

On 1 March 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked and killed one person in Ugbobi (Apa, Benue). Attacks occurred concurrently in Edikwu Icho, Akpanta and Ikobi villages, coded separately. The attackers killed four people altogether in the four villages.

On 1 March 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked and killed one person in Edikwu Icho (Apa, Benue). Attacks also occurred concurrently in Ikobi, Akpanta, and Ugbobi villages, coded separately. The attackers killed five people altogether in the four villages. Fatality split across 2 events coded to 3.

Around 1 March 2024 (as reported), the Nigerian troops on a fighting patrol engaged an unidentified armed group in a firefight in Katapka village (Toto, Nassarawa). They killed one of the group members and recovered two AK-47 Rifles, one Pump Action Semi-automatic rifle, three AK-47 magazines and 90 rounds of 7.62 mm Special ammunition.
On 1 March 2024, a Katsina militia abducted an unspecified number of people from Dangani village (Musawa, Katsina). They also set people's property on fire.

On 1 March 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked residents of Ledor community, coded to Saakpenwa (Tai, Rivers) in an attempt to grab land in the area. One person was killed and six others including the community's deputy paramount ruler were wounded as claimed by MOSOP. They also claimed that the attack happened a few days after NNPCL officials attempted to forcefully lay gas pipelines in the community and were turned back.
On 1 March 2024, two rival cult gangs clashed with each other around Ihiagwa (Owerri West, Imo). A student (likely to be a bystander) was stabbed and killed in the clash.

On 1 March 2024, ISWAP/BH fighters attacked the Nigerian troops and engaged them in a firefight at Mararaba on the outskirts of Pulka (Gwoza, Borno). The military reinforcements deployed ran into an IED, and the explosive killed one of them. There was one fatality.

Around 1 March 2024 (as reported), an unidentified armed group allegedly loyal to an APC faction engaged the police in a shootout in Makurdi (Makurdi, Benue). There is a brewing intraparty crisis in the state. They invaded the city in a convoy and opened fire sporadically before the police chased them away. There were no fatalities.

On 1 March 2024, two unidentified rival cult militias clashed at the Federal University of Technology Owerri (Owerri Municipal, Imo) when a group from the Imo State University entered FUTO in a motorcycle convoy. One student was killed and several people were wounded.

On 2 March 2024, a Benue militia killed the leader of a Taraba militia and members of his family after they were previously abducted at Chinka (Wukari, Taraba). 5 million naira was paid from the 100 million that was demanded as ransom and the abductees' murder resulted in a clash between two militia. Other sources report that the leader was killed due to an attempt at territory capture. Unknown number of fatalities coded as 3.

On 2 March 2024, a Fulani militia ambushed soldiers and engaged them in an armed clash at Ochumeku (Apa, Benue). One soldier was killed, another was wounded, three of the assailants were killed and several of them were wounded. The troops also recovered one rifle and rounds of ammunition.
On 2 March 2024, a Katsina militia attacked Nasara and Yanmazara villages in Safana LGA, coded to Safana (Safana, Katsina). No further details.

On 2 March 2024, troops of the Nigerian Army engaged IPOB/ ESN militants in an armed clash at their suspected crossing point in Akawa Nnaeto general area, coded to Nkwoagu Isuochi (Nneochi, Abia). The militants fled into the bushes, while the troops recovered a load rifle, ammunition and magazines. No casualties.
On 2 March 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked a residence and injured one person in the Yelwa community (Bauchi). They went away with money and other valuables. There was no fatality.
On 2 March 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked a convoy escorted by the police along the Atani Ogwu-Ikpele Road in Ogbaru LGA, coded to Atani (Ogbaru, Anambra). No further details.

On 2 March 2024, troops of the Nigerian Army engaged IPOB/ ESN militants in an armed clash at Orsu Ihiteukwa (Orsu, Imo). One militant was killed, 3 IEDs were recovered, vehicles, a gun and ammunition were recovered.

On 2 March 2024, a Kaduna militia killed two Fulani pastoralists at Hayin-Dam in Kachia LGA (Kaduna) and rustled 223 cows. The assailants raided three pastoralists camps in the area; 123 cows were stolen form one camp and 100 from another, the victims were killed for resisting the rustle of their cattle.

On 2 March 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted sixty people after ambushing their vehicles along the Gusau-Sokoto Road, between Dogon Karfe and the Mayanci Bridge in Maru LGA. Coded to Maru (Maru, Zamfara).

On 3 March 2024, an unidentified armed group numbering about six, attacked Kurmi (Ningi, Bauchi). They shot and injured a former LGA councilor and a nursing mother. They abducted some residents, including the son of the former councilor. There were no fatalities.

On 3 March 2024, the Nigerian troops engaged the suspected Fulani herders in a firefight in Apa LGA, coded to Ugbokpo (Apa, Benue). Three herders and one soldier were killed in the clash, and another soldier got injured. There were four fatalities.
On 3 March 2024, a Katsina militia abducted thirteen people from Albasu village in Sabuwa LGA, coded to Sabuwa (Sabuwa, Katsina). No further details.

On 3 March 2024, Icelanders from the Waja Marine deck abducted and forcefully initiated four young men into their cult at Elekahia (Port Harcourt, Rivers). The victims were physically assaulted as part of the initiation rites, they were targeted due to financial buoyancy which the militia considered would be an advantage.

On 3 March 2024, a Zamfara militia shot and injured five people and abducted many others after blocking the Funtua-Gusau Highway in Gusau LGA, coded to Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara). There were no fatalities.
On 3 March 2024, Nigerian troops and CJTF ambushed and killed four ISWAP fighters at Moula in Ngala LGA, coded to Ngala (Ngala, Borno). Moula was regarded as one of their logistic routes

On 3 March 2024, a Zamfara militia attacked Dan Baza in Maradun LGA, coded to Maradun (Maradun, Zamfara). They also attacked some villagers on the Magazu-Kucheri Highway in Tsafe LGA, coded separately. There were no fatalities.

On 3 March 2024, suspected armed pastoralists killed several civilians when they attacked Udedeku community, coded to Jato Aka (Kwande, Benue). Other sources claimed that three civilians were killed and that the assailants numbered up to 500.

On 3 March 2024, a Zamfara militia attacked villagers on the Magazu-Kucheri Highway in Tsafe LGA, coded to Magazu (Tsafe, Zamfara). They also attacked Dan Baza in Maradun LGA, coded separately. There were no fatalities.

On 3 March 2024, a Zamfara militia wounded five civilians when they invaded Magazu (Tsafe, Zamfara) on motorcycles and shot sporadically. The residents' properties were stolen, fatalities are unknown.

On 3 March 2024, suspected Boko Haram/ ISWAP militants abducted over 200 IDPs in search of firewood in Jillam and Wurga villages of Gamboru-Ngala LGA, coded to Ngala (Ngala, Borno). Another source reported 400 were abducted, while others claimed that the abductees were 101 IDPS comprising 53 girls and 48 boys and that nine of them later returned to the camp. The hostages moved out of the protective trenches in search of firewood and trekked about 23 kilometers away from the camp when they were abducted. The state government claimed the abductees lost their way home and were not abducted because there were no ransom demands.
On 4 March 2024, armed Fulani pastoralists wounded a woman who is a native of Odejo (Agatu, Benue) in the community. The victim was taken to the hospital in a critical condition.

On 4 March 2024, troops of the Nigerian army engaged a Katsina militia in an armed clash during an operation in Kurfi LGA and Safana LGA and killed four militia members including a second in command of the militia. Location coded to Kurfi (Kurfi, Katsina). two rifles, magazines, ammunition and camouflage uniforms were recovered by the troops.
On 4 March 2024, armed Fulani pastoralists killed two civilians along Edikwu Ukpogo and Odugbo communities (Apa, Benue). The victims were from Odugbo and two other persons were declared missing.
On 4 March 2024, a Sokoto militia shot and killed one person and injured another in a shooting spree in Kwatsal village (Sabon Birni, Sokoto). They also abducted two people.

On 4 March 2024, a Kaduna militia shot and injured three people attempting to escape when they attacked their village in Azzara, coded as Gidan Azara (Kachia, Kaduna). The militia abducted eight family members, including the father, mother, and their children. There were no fatalities.
On 4 March 2024, ISWAP attacked the Nigerian troops and engaged them in a firefight in Dikwa town (Dikwa, Borno). No further details.

On 4 March 2024, a Zamfara militia attacked communities along Gabake Mesa- Kaura Road in Kaura Namoda LGA, coded to Kaura Namoda (Kaura Namoda, Zamfara). No fewer than three people were killed in the attacks.

On 4 March 2024, a Zamfara militia attacked Nigerian troops at a checkpoint in Gidan Kano village, along the Sokoto-Gusau Road in Maradun LGA, coded to Maradun (Maradun, Zamfara). One soldier was killed. There was one fatality.
On 4 March 2024, a Katsina militia killed at least seventeen people when attacking Zamfarawa, Doma and Gidan Kare villages in Bakori LGA, coded to Bakori (Bakori, Katsina).

On 4 March 2024, Riverside and Seaside communal militias engaged in an armed clash at Ibese (Ikorodu, Lagos) that continued until the following day. An unspecified number of persons were killed and several others were wounded. The reason for the clash is unknown, fatalities coded as 3.

On 4 March 2024, a Katsina militia shot and killed an unspecified number of people when attacking the Unguwar Baushe community in Kankara (Kankara, Katsina). They set many houses on fire. Unspecified fatalities coded as 3.
On 4 March 2024, the troops of the 202 Battalion killed one IS/BH fighter trying to infiltrate their location at night in Bama (Bama, Borno). They intercepted him and shot him dead.

On 5 March 2024, suspected Berom, Mwaghavul and Ron ethnic militia riding on motorcycles shot and killed a Fulani man herding his cows between Nafan Village and Fanzo, Ropp District of Barkin-Ladi LGA, coded to Ropp (Barkin Ladi, Plateau). They injured another man with a machete and shot 35 to 50 cows and sheep dead. There was one fatality.

On 5 March 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted a school teacher on his farm in Kugba-Ajagbe village in Odeda LGA, coded to Odeda (Odedah, Ogun). The police stormed the scene of the abduction but only found one AK 47 expended ammunition and a Bajajm motorcycle.

On 5 March 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a former General Manager of the Jigawa State Housing Authority and two others on the way to Birnin Kudu, coded to Birnin Kudu (Birnin Kudu, Jigawa). The assailants opened fire at their vehicle and killed the three occupants. There were three fatalities.

On 5 March 2024, the Nigerian troops engaged a Kaduna militia in a firefight in Rijana Forest (Kachia, Kaduna). They killed two militiamen and recovered two AK47 rifles, two magazines, four rounds of 7.62mm, and a machinegun belt.
On 5 March 2024, suspected herders attacked and injured two farmers on a farm in Gda Biyu, coded to Godogodo (Jema'a, Kaduna).

On 5 March 2024, troops of the joint task force of Operation Hadin Kai, coded as military and police forces responded to a distress call engaged a Zamfara militia in an armed clash at Tsohuwar Tasha in Kaura Namoda LGA (Zamfara). One militia member was killed, others fled with gunshot wounds and 15 abductees were rescued.
On 5 March 2024, a Zamfara militia attacked commuters in transit along the Gusau-Sokoto- Mayanchi Road in Maru LGA, coded to Mayanchi (Maru, Zamfara). No further details.
On 5 March 2024, a Kaduna militia shot and injured a farmer on his farm at Akwaya Hanya Village, coded to Kachia (Kachia, Kaduna).
On 5 March 2024, a Kaduna militia sexually assaulted a girl after killing one person in Kurmi Jarmi village, Kachia (Kachia, Kaduna). They also abducted eight people.

On 5 March 2024, Zamfara Community Protection Guards killed an Islamic scholar in Mada town (Gusau, Zamfara) after they picked him up for questioning over security related issues. The victim was killed a few meters outside the town. Other sources report that the victim was killed over an accusation against him from a year ago, about his involvement with a Zamfara militia because he intervened and rescued accused persons from a local defense militia.

On 5 March 2024, Riverside and Seaside communal militias engaged in an armed clash at Ibese (Ikorodu, Lagos) that started the previous day. An unspecified number of persons were killed and several others were wounded. The reason for the clash is unknown, fatalities coded as 3.

On 5 March 2024, two rival Benue militias led by Full Fire and Chain engaged in an armed clash at Gbagir (Ukum, Benue) over a tussle for supremacy in the Ukum LGA. One of the militias enlisted the help of a Fulani militia based in Taraba to support them in the clash. Over 45 persons, 12 of whom were civilians were killed, over 30 other persons were wounded. Some people were declared missing and residents were displaced.

On 5 March 2024, Nigerian army and Navy troops engaged IPOB militants in an armed clash at their camps in Ejemekwuru (Oguta, Imo). Five militants were killed, arms, ammunition and other items including a camouflage jungle hat were recovered.

On 6 March 2024, the Nigerian troops engaged an unidentified armed group in a firefight in Ososo Forest, Ososo (Akoko Edo, Edo). The armed group had abducted some people before the military engaged them. The troops rescued four hostages, including a lady and three men. They arrested one of the abductors. There were no fatalities.
On 6 March 2024, a Sokoto militia killed one person and injured another when attacking the Tozai community (Illela, Sokoto).
On 6 March 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed one person in Oba TT Dada Street, Ota, also spelt as Otta (Ado-Odo, Ogun).

On 6 March 2024, Nigerian troops repelled an attack by a Sokoto militia on Damba Diko village (Illela, Sokoto). The militia held some villagers hostage while trying to extort levies from the community. The troops engaged them in a firefight, killed two and rescued the hostages.

On 6 March 2024, the Nigerian military, the Police, and the Protection Corps engaged a Zamfara militia in a firefight in Kaura Namoda (Kaura Namoda, Zamfara). The militia invaded the community at night, and the security forces confronted them for hours. The clash triggered a mass exodus of residents from the community. There were no fatalities.
On 6 March 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted a teacher on his way to school in Alabata, coded to Akinyele (Akinyele, Oyo).
On 6 March 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted a man in front of his residence around Nchatancha (Enugu East, Enugu).

On 6 March 2024, armed Fulani pastoralists killed 12 civilians at Tyuruv community, coded to nearby Chito (Ukum, Benue). The assailants invaded Tse-Azande, Tse-Ajauka, Tse-Ugema, Tse-Guzo settlements were they shot sporadically, other residents escaped with bullet wounds.

On 6 March 2024, a policeman beat up a lawyer at a police station in Ikeja (Ikeja, Lagos) when he went to intervene in a matter concerning his colleague's client who was detained there. The victim claimed that a policeman admonished him that not all cases are handled by lawyers.

On 7 March 2024, Fulani armed pastoralists attacked the Wandor community (Gwer East, Benue), killing over sixteen people, including a retired soldier. The attackers, numbering about forty, entered the community at night through Mbasomb village and operated for about three hours. They burned over fifty houses, huts, and food barns. Reports varied from over 16 to 17 fatalities, coded as 16.

On 7 March 2024, KADVIS engaged a Kaduna militia in a firefight after the militia invaded LEA Primary School, Kuriga (Chikun, Kaduna). The militia attacked the school early in the morning and shot fire sporadically. They abducted between 232 and 287 pupils, including the schoolteachers and the head teacher. The KADVIS that responded to the distress call pursued the militia, and one of them was shot dead. One of the pupils was also shot and later died in the hospital. There were two fatalities. The militia demanded a billion naira ransom and threatened to kill the hostages in 20 days. The abductees were rescued by soldiers, the state government claimed that one teacher died in captivity due to health complications and that no ransom was paid.

On 7 March 2024, Boko Haram militants killed three civilians at a resettlement site in Ngurosoye (Bama, Borno). The victims consisted of two males and one female, whose goats were stolen. The women was killed while trying to pursue the militants to recover her goats.

On 7 March 2024, combined troops of Operation Udo KA comprised of the Nigerian Army, police, DSS and NSCDC engaged IPOB militants in an armed clash when they raided their camps at Mother Valley, coded to Orsu Ihiteukwa (Orsu, Imo). 20 militants were killed, their supreme headquarters, command and control centers and about 50 tents were destroyed, and the troops detonated several IEDs while around the axis of the camps. IPOB through its spokesperson denied ownership of the camp and claimed that it belonged to ''criminal infiltrators''.
On 7 March 2024, a Zamfara militia killed at least one person and abducted ten others when attacking Kara Zube village in Chafe town, also spelt as Tsafe (Tsafe, Zamfara).

On 7 March 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed an NSCDC officer at a construction site in Obangede (Okehi, Kogi). The armed group invaded the site and opened fire sporadically on the people. They abducted a Chinese engineer and injured many other people.

On 8 March 2024, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists killed a man on his farm in the Ubune-Ivbiaro community or Ivbiaro (Owan East, Edo). The assailants damaged his motorcycle and went away with his cutlass and mobile phone.

On 8 March 2024, suspected cult militia riding on motorcycles shot and killed four people in the Abacheke community (Ohaji, Imo). The shooting was suspected to be a reprisal of a previous killing among the rival cult groups. They invaded the community and fired shots sporadically, triggering panic among the residents. Five people were hit by their bullets, but one survived. There were four fatalities.

On 8 March 2024, a Kaduna militia attacked a mosque and shot two worshipers dead in Angwar Makera, Kwasakwasa Community, Birni Gwari LGA, coded to Sabon Kuyelo (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). They invaded the mosque in the afternoon during a prayer session and opened fire on the worshippers. The militia abducted many others.
Around 8 March 2024 (as reported), a Kaduna militia abducted nine people from Angwar Kanawa, Kwasakwasa area, coded to Sabon-Layilasan (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna).
On 8 March 2024, two unidentified rival cult militias clashed on the campus of the Abia state university in Onuaku Uturu (Isuikwuato, Abia). One student was killed.

On 8 March 2024, an Ofongama militia attacked civilians in Nnaorokpa community in Nta-Nselle (Ikom Cross River) and killed three persons while four others were injured. The assailants who crossed into the community from neighboring Obubura LGA attacked over a boundary disputes, and the murdered victims were two girls and a boy.

On 8 March 2024, suspected IPOB/ESN shot sporadically at the police and killed five cops on duty at the hilltop stop and search along Nwofe Road, on the outskirts of Abakaliki (Abakaliki, Ebonyi). The police returned fire, and the militia scampered and abandoned a rifle. Two civilians were caught in the crossfire and died during the encounter. There were seven total fatalities.

On 8 March 2024, the police clashed with an unidentified armed group along Amagu- Awgbu Road near Awgbu (Orumba North, Anambra). The armed group had abducted four people and tried to take them out of the city when they sighted the police and opened fire on them. They fled, and some escaped with gun wounds. The police rescued the hostages unhurt and recovered one pump action gun. They also recovered two SUVs - one 2017 edition Toyota Highlander. There were no fatalities.

On 8 March 2024, a Sokoto militia attacked Turba (Isa, Sokoto) and Tozai, coded separately. The militiamen killed seven people, including the village head, and abducted at least thirty women who were later released the following day. Fatalities split across two events coded as 4.

On 8 March 2024, ISWAP shot and injured one person trying to escape abduction around Gajigana (Magumeri, Borno). The militia abducted fourteen persons hunting for grasshoppers. Five escaped, and one got shot trying to flee. There were no fatalities.
On 8 March 2024, ISWAP killed three people while attacking Ngurosoye village (Bama, Borno). They rustled livestock.

On 8 March 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted two FRSC officers along the Abakaliki - Enugu expressway as they were returning home from the Nkalagu office (Ishielu, Ebonyi). An unspecified amount was demanded as ransom.
On 8 March 2024, a Sokoto militia opened fire indiscriminately at vehicles in transit along the Gusau-Sokoto Road in Mayanchi (Maru, Sokoto). No further details.
On 8 March 2024, an unidentified armed group killed a man in the Okuama community (Bomadi, Delta). The victim was abducted on 5 March 2024 while going to his mother's farm.

On 9 March 2024, an unidentified armed group engaged in an armed clash with hunters and a local defense militia in Lau town (Ardo Kola, Taraba). On 9 March 2024, an unidentified armed group killed a man and dumped his body in the Forcados River, coded to Forcados (Burutu, Delta). On 9 March 2024, the police and the Community Protection Guards clashed with a Zamfara militia after the militia attacked some commuters at Bakon Gebe along the Kaura-Zurmi Highway in Zurmi LGA, coded to Zurmi (Zurmi, Zamfara). On 9 March 2024, a Katsina militia opened fire indiscriminately at civilians at the Gangara weekly market in Gangara village (Jibia, Katsina). On 9 March 2024, a Kaduna militia abducted ten farmers from their farms at Kajuru station, Tantanu Ward, near Kajuru (Kajuru, Kaduna).

On 9 March 2024, three soldiers dressed in plain clothes stabbed and killed an NDLEA operative at a checkpoint manned by NDLEA officials in Bida town (Bida, Niger). On 9 March 2024, a Sokoto militia attacked and killed three people, including the village head at Turba village (Isa, Sokoto). The militia proceeded to Gada LGA and abducted fifteen pupils, coded separately. There were three fatalities.

On 9 March 2024, ISWAP fighters attacked and injured three Fulani pastoralists along the Nigeria- Niger Republic border around Joka village, also spelt as Jokka (Mobbar, Borno). They also rustled many cattle.

On 9 March 2024, a Sokoto militia shot and wounded one person and abducted 15 to 16 students of a boarding Islamic school and one woman in Gidan Bakuso village (Gada, Sokoto). On 9 March 2024, a Kaduna militia shot fire sporadically and injured one person in the Ungwan Shekarau community in Kachia (Kachia, Kaduna). They abducted three others.

On 10 March 2024, an unidentified armed group killed at least seven persons when they invaded the market at Zurak Campani, coded to New Zurak (Wase, Plateau). Many others were wounded and the assailants fled into the bushes. Policemen were later deployed to the community.

On 10 March 2024, a Katsina militia attacked and injured one person and abducted another in Muniya village, coded to Safana (Safana, Katsina).
On 10 March 2024, an unidentified armed group killed a farmer on his farm when they attacked Olakpoga (Otukpo, Benue) and Ipepe (coded separately).

On 10 March 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted a woman and her three children from their residence in the Samaru Bayan Nepa area, coded to Gusau (Gusau, Zmafara). The abductees included an infant.
On 10 March 2024, a Katsina militia engaged the Community Watch Corps in a firefight in Batsari town (Batsari, Katsina). They killed two members of the Corps.

On 10 March 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked Ipepe community (Otukpo, Benue) and Olakpoga (coded separately). Casualties are unknown.

On 10 March 2024, the Fulani and the Mumuye people clashed around the Lau community (Lau, Taraba). One person was killed, and another got injured in the clash. There was one fatality.

On 12 March 2024, a Kaduna militia abducted two teenage herders and rustled their animals in Kuchimi village (Kagarko, Kaduna). The hostages escaped when their abductors got drunk and slept off.

On 12 March 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted the deputy director of nursing services who is also a senior matron and a gate keeper from the University of Nigeria Teaching Hospital in Ituku Ozalla, coded to Ituku (Agwu, Enugu). On 13 March 2024, Setti and Kpasham communal militias engaged in an armed clash that started the previous day (coded separately) and spread to different communities. Location coded to Kpasham (Demsa, Adamawa), at least five persons were killed, fatalities split across two events coded as 2.

On 16 March 2024, a Kaduna militia attacked civilians at Dogonnoma (Kajuru, Kaduna) and inflicted serious injuries on one person. 14 to 17 other residents were abducted.

On 16 March 2024, an unidentified armed group killed the traditional ruler of Riruwai after he was abducted from his palace and dumped his body near the village, coded to Lame district (Toro, Bauchi). There were no ransom demands and the victim's corpse was found by a search party.

On 16 March 2024, Ayeke and Enweli communal militias continued a clash which began the previous day (coded separately) over a disputed parcel of land. On 16 March 2024, an unidentified cult militia trailed a man and killed him at mile axis of Diobu (Port Harcourt, Rivers). The victim was a printer, his mobile phone and motorcycle were stolen by the assailants and the reason for the attack is unknown.

On 17 March 2024, an ISWAP suicide bomber suspected to have been heading to a mosque detonated an IED at Biu (Biu, Borno) and killed himself. Two civilians were also wounded in the blast, other sources report an unspecified number of wounded persons.
On 17 March 2024, a soldier shot and injured a tricycle rider in Tashan Damboa, Gwoza LGA, coded to Gwoza (Gwoza, Borno), when the tricycle collided with his bicycle.
