On 18 March 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted a Lebanese construction worker between Umuchu and Umunze communities, coded to Umuchu (Aguata, Anambra).
On 18 March 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted six people from Tumba village near Matseri (Anka, Zamfara). No further details.
On 18 March 2024, a Zamfara militia killed and abducted an unspecified number of people in Bilbis (Tsafe, Zamfara). An unspecified number of fatalities, coded as 3.

One member of the group was arrested by the troops while the second person shot and killed himself to evade arrest. One rifle, ammunition and other items were recovered.
On 19 March 2024, a Niger militia attacked and killed the district head and four others in Pangu Gari (Rafi, Niger). There were five fatalities.

On 19 March 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked a young Fulani pastoralist in Alkaleri LGA, coded to Alkaleri (Alkaleri, Bauchi). They gouged out the victim's eyes. The police arrested the attackers. There was no fatality.

On 19 March 2024, suspected armed pastoralists attacked and killed two farmers on their farms in Onipi community (Otukpo, Benue). Other farmers were injured and some were declared missing. On 19 March 2024, a Katsina militia shot and killed a communal militiamen (off duty) at his residence in Kwari Mai Zurfi near Makera (Dutsinma, Katsina).

On 19 March 2024, a Modakeke militia attacked and killed three civilians in Ife villages, coded to Ile-Ife (Ife Central, Osun) as claimed by an Ife group who also claimed that two persons were missing and some villages were sacked. One of the murdered victims was a chief from Wanisanni village.
On 19 March 2024, a Kaduna militia attacked and killed two people in Mai Ido village near Awon (Kachia, Kaduna). No further details.

Around 19 March 2024 (as reported), Nigerian troops engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash at Rafin Bauna (Bassa, Plateau). One abductee was rescued, the troops recovered one rifle and two motorcycles. Casualties are unknown.
On 19 March 2024, a Zamfara militia, riding on motorcycles, fired indiscriminately and killed two people in Ruwan Baure, close to Ruwan Bore (Gusau, Zamfara). They injured five people.

On 19 March 2024, a Zamfara militia clashed with the Community Protection Guards and a communal militia in Ruwan Bore (Gusau, Zamfara). The militia killed two members of the Protection Guard and a communal militiamen and burned down an unspecified number of houses and shops. There were three fatalities. The militia attacked Gidan Zuma the following day (coded separately) and five civilians were wounded in the two attacks.

On 19 March 2024, armed Fulani pastoralists attacked Yongia Ukambie Tiev, coded to Ngambe-Tiev (Logo, Benue) and killed two people. The armed group returned to the village the following day and killed five more people, coded separately. There were two fatalities.

Around 19 March 2024 (as reported), military forces responded to a distress call and foiled an abduction attempt by a Zamfara militia on the outskirts of Kwatarkwashi (Bungudu, Zamfara). Three abductees were rescued, one of them sustained injuries and was taken to the hospital.

Around 19 March 2024 (as reported), an unidentified armed group abducted a woman from her residence at Abuja layout in Bukuru (Jos South, Plateau). The abductee was rescued by soldiers at Rafin Bauna (coded separately).

On 20 March 2024, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists abducted not less than ten people between Ifon and Sobe, coded to Sobe (Owan West, Edo). The hostages included five men and five women. No ransom was demanded.

On 20 March 2024, a suspected cult militia shot and killed a man and his pregnant wife in Ogwashi-Uku (Aniocha South, Delta). The killing took place amid a series of cult killings within the community. There were two fatalities.

On 20 March 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed two soldiers and three civilians in Shege (Toto, Nassarawa). The soldiers were responding to a distress call but were ambushed and killed on their way from Katakpa to Shege. The armed group set many houses on fire. There were five fatalities.

On 20 March 2024, armed Fulani pastoralists attacked Ugbobi village (Apa, Benue) and killed two people. The armed group returned to the village and killed eight more people the following day, coded separately. There were two fatalities.

On 20 March 2024, a Zamfara militia attacked civilians at Gidan Zuma in Bungudu LGA (Zamfara) and demanded that the residents provide all of the Ramadan relief materials that were donated to them. The militia had attacked Ruwan Bore the previous day (coded separately) and 5 persons were wounded in the two attacks.

Around 20 March 2024 (as reported), the Nigerian troops shot and killed a Taraba militiaman in Kutoko village, coded to Takum (Takum, Taraba). An AK-47 Rifle and a magazine containing four live rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition were recovered.

On 20 March 2024, armed Fulani pastoralists attacked Yongia Ukambie Tiev, coded to Ngambe-Tiev (Logo, Benue) and killed five people. The killing was in addition to the two people they killed when they attacked the community the previous day, coded separately. There were five fatalities.

On 20 March 2024, the Nigerian troops and a local defence militia killed a Sokoto militiaman during a firefight in Sokoto state, coded to Sokoto (Sokoto North. Sokoto). The militiaman often disguised as a policeman and abducted his victims. His logistic base was destroyed during the operation.

On 21 March 2024, the police and other security agencies, likely to be the military, clashed with the IPOB/ESN in their hideout in the Omni community forest in Izzi LGA, coded to Izi (Izzi, Ebonyi). The government forces killed three militiamen and arrested five. Others escaped and fled into the bush. One AK47 rifle with 16 rounds of live ammunition, a bag containing 2,000 rounds of live ammunition, A Police Warrant Card, and an Identity Card were recovered. There were three fatalities.

On 21 March 2024, the Anti-kidnapping unit of the Nigerian police engaged an unidentified armed group in a firefight, killing five of them in a forest in Odogbolu LGA, coded to Odogbolu (Odogbolu, Ogun). The police trailed the armed group to their hideout after they abducted a poultry manager in the area. The police rescued the hostage unharmed while other members of the armed group escaped with gun wounds. Money, one sword, cell phones, hard drugs, charms, empty shells of AK47 riffles and sticks were recovered.

On 21 March 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted four people around Emecourt Road Junction, Nnewi North LGA, coded to Nnewi (Nnewi North, Anambra). The armed group had abducted three people before their vehicle developed a fault. They stopped and seized a passing car and its driver and transferred the three hostages. One of the hostages escaped, but the abductors fled the scene with the remaining two and the female driver of the seized car.

On 21 March 2024, the Police engaged a Kaduna militia in a firefight near Corner Ugara, Buruku (Chikun, Kaduna). The Police were on a routine patrol when they sighted the militia hibernating by the roadside, attempting to abduct the commuters. The Police opened fire on them. The militiamen escaped with injuries. There were no fatalities.

On 21 March 2024, a Niger militia attacked and killed the village Head of Anguwan Bala and his two wives in Majanjan District, coded to Maguga (Rafi, Niger). The militia later attacked Madaka Market the same day, coded separately. There were three fatalities.

On 21 March 2024, armed Fulani pastoralists attacked Ugbobi village (Apa, Benue) and killed eight people. The armed group had earlier killed two people a day before, coded separately. There were eight fatalities.

Around 21 March 2024 (as reported), a Katsina militia shot and killed a driver and injured two others on Dustin Ma Road, coded to Dutsin Ma (Dutsinma, Katsina). The militia shot the driver dead after a driver had earlier resisted abduction and escaped with injuries. There was one fatality.

On 21 March 2024, a Niger militia attacked a market and killed 65 people, including the village head in Madaka (Rafi, Niger). They abducted many people, including women and children, and set many properties on fire.

On 21 March 2024, the special team of the Nigerian Military, the police, DSS and NSCDC attacked the IPOB/ESN camp in Mgbalukwu (Izzi, Ebonyi) and killed one of the militiamen. Other members escaped and fled into the bushes. The Nigerian security operatives recovered one AK-47 rifle, two AK-47 magazines, 54 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition, two handheld radios and three stolen Sienna buses.

On 21 March 2024, the Tsafe defence militia engaged a Zamfara militia in a firefight in Magazu village (Tsafe, Zamfara). There were no fatalities.
On 21 March 2024, a Zamfara militia attacked and killed a man and his son on a farm in Wanzamai village, Chafe, also spelt as Tsafe LGA, coded to Tsafe (Tsafe, Zamfara). There were two fatalities.

Around 21 March 2024 (as reported), a Zamfara militia opened fire indiscriminately and shot at least four people dead in Mashaya village, Jangebe District (Talata Mafara, Zamfara). The shooting triggered panic in the village.

On 21 March 2024, Boko Haram attacked a Fulani settlement around Fadana Garuwa near Duji (Mobbar, Borno). They opened fire on the residents, forcing them to scamper for safety. There were no fatalities.

On 21 March 2024, the Nigerian Military, the police, and members of the Community Watch Corps engaged a Katsina militia in a firefight after the militia intercepted a bus and abducted its passengers at Gidan Kifi village, between Burdugau and Yargoje, coded to Yargoje (Kankara, Katsina). On 22 March 2024, suspected Boko Haram fighters attacked Garkida (Gombi, Adamawa) and shot a woman dead. The militiamen set a military vehicle ablaze and shot fire indiscriminately at the residents. The villagers scampered for safety, and some fled to the bush for safety.

On 22 March 2024, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists killed two Tiv farmers who went fishing at the Tse-Aber Azir area in Kadarko (Keana, Nassarawa). The IDP resettlement camp was invaded by the assailants and the occupants fled to other areas including Giza. Other sources report that scores were wounded and the clash resulted from a disagreement over a stream.

On 22 March 2024, a Tiv ethnic militia killed a Fulani at Kadarko (Keana, Nassarawa) in a reprisal after two Tiv farmers were killed when they went fishing (coded separately). Other sources report that the victim was killed when he confronted Tiv fishers over a shared stream in the community and his death led to a reprisal against the Tiv.

On 22 March 2024, two members of rival unidentified cult militias clashed at Pataka area of Ilorin (Ilorin West, Kwara) over a disagreement. One person was killed and members of his militia carried out a reprisal (coded separately).

On 22 March 2024, hunters engaged an unidentified armed group in a firefight when the group attacked the Pompo community along the Damaturu-Buni Yadi-Biu Road, coded to Buni Yadi (Gujba, Borno). The hunters recovered the cattle rustled by the group. There were no fatalities.
On 22 March 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted ten passengers of a commercial bus in Jootar, Ukum LGA coded to Chito (Ukum, Benue). No ransom was demanded.

On 23 March 2024, a Katsina militia attacked and killed three people in Taka-Lafiya village, coded to Kunkuna (Safana, Katsina). They injured an unspecified number of others. There were three fatalities.

On 23 March 2024, a Katsina militia shot and killed two people in Torawa village, coded to Batsari (Batsari, Katsina). They also shot and wounded an unspecified number of others. There were two fatalities.

On 24 March 2024, an unidentified armed group killed three Eggon farmers at Kadarko (Keana, Nassarawa). The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 24 March 2024, a Kaduna militia killed four people and injured two others when attacking Ungwan Saidu village, coded to Magajin Gari 3 (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). They abducted fifty-eight people, but thirty of them later escaped. There were four fatalities.
On 24 March 2024, a Zamfara militia attacked civilians at Gidan Zuma village in Bungudu LGA (Zamfara). 11 persons were killed, 20 women and an unspecified number of children and were abducted.

On 24 March 2024, an unidentified cult militia killed a man at the village of Kudu (Pankshin, Plateau) over unknown reasons. On 24 March 2024, the Gigane defence militia engaged a Sokoto militia in a firefight after the Sokoto militia attacked and injured three people in Buwadi village (Illela, Sokoto). The Sokoto militia retreated after the confrontation. There were no fatalities.

On 24 March 2024, a Katsina militia who attacked civilians were engaged in an armed clash with policemen, community watch corps operatives and a local defense militia at Mairua (Faskari, Katsina). On 24 March 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted two siblings from a residence in Damba coded and spelled as Dunba (Gusau, Zamfara). No further details.

On 24 March 2024, the Ezeagu defence militia engaged in a firefight with an unidentified armed group attempting to abduct some people in Aguobu-Owa (Ezeagu, Enugu). One of the abductors was killed, and weapons were recovered. There was one fatality.

On 25 March 2024, police forces engaged a leader of Greenlanders cult militia in an armed clash at the forest in Anambra, coded to Akinima (Ahoada West, Rivers). The militia leader who was declared wanted by the police since 2016 was killed.

On 25 March 2024, Nigerian security, likely to be the police and a hunter group, clashed with an unidentified armed group in the Egbudu-Akah community (Aniocha South, Delta). On 25 March 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a man at his residence in the Ama-Ohuo community, Nguru (Aboh Mbaise, Imo).
On 25 March 2024, an unidentified group engaged police forces in an armed clash when they attacked a police station in Awgbu (Orumba North, Anambra). Two policemen were killed.

On 25 March 2024, a Katsina militia set up a checkpoint and abducted two people along the Faskari-Yankara Road, coded to Faskari (Faskari, Katsina).

On 25 March 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted the chief imam of Iyara from the front of his residence in Ilukpa, Iyara (Ijumu, Kogi) after they invaded the area and shot sporadically. The abductee was released on 5 April, there are no reports on ransom demands or payment.
On 25 March 2024, Ebube Agu operatives shot sporadically into the air at Awo-Omamma (Oru East, Imo). One man was hit and killed by a stray bullet.

On 25 March 2024, the Nigerian troops and the Community Protection Guards engaged a Zamfara militia in a firefight when the militia attempted to attack Tsafe (Tsafe, Zamfara). On 26 March 2024, a Zamfara militia attacked residents of Kita town, coded and spelled as Keta (Tsafe, Zamfara). The town's chief imam was killed and scores of residents were abducted.

On 26 March 2024, troops of the Nigerian army and assumed Katsina Community Watch Corps conducted an offensive and engaged a Katsina militia in an armed clash at Garin Rinji in Batsari LGA (Katsina). Two militia members were killed, several of their hideouts were destroyed, two rifles and 25 rustled cattle were recovered.

On 26 March 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted a man from Kofa Adamu village, coded to Takum (Takum, Taraba). The abductors demanded a two-million-naira ransom for his release. The Nigerian troops rescued the hostage on 4 April 2024 when raiding the armed group's enclave.
On 26 March 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted two residents from Magazu (Tsafe, Zamfara) when they invaded the area and shot sporadically. There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 26 March 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted a man and a pregnant woman in Asolo, Ikorodu (Ikorodu, Lagos).

On 26 March 2024, troops of the Nigerian army in collaboration with assumed Civilian JTF operatives engaged ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants in an armed clash at Gori, also called Limankara (Gwoza, Borno). On 27 March 2024, Boko Haram (JAS) attacked and killed three people on a farm in Kwam village, coded to Uba (Askira Uba, Borno).

On 27 March 2024, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists killed a man on his farm in Jattu community (Etsako West, Edo). The victim's body was discovered on 30 March with machete cuts, after a search was conducted following his disappearance for two days after leaving for his farm.

On 27 March 2024, the Nigerian troops engaged an unidentified armed group in a gun battle while on patrol around Chanchanji (Takum, Taraba). One member of the group was killed, and the troops recovered one locally fabricated FN Pistol, two rounds of 9MM ammunition and one mobile phone.

On 27 March 2024, a Zamfara militia attacked Mutumji community (Maru, Zamfara) and displaced 230 individuals from 40 households. The victims were displaced to Tsunami community in Gusau LGA, there were no fatalities or injuries in the attack.

On 27 March 2024, the Goronyo defence militia clashed with a Sokoto communal militia in Falaliya village, also spelt as Falalia (Goronyo, Sokoto). The defence militia rescued four women and three infants. There were no fatalities.

On 27 March 2024, the Nigerian troops clashed with a Zamfara militia in Gidan Gaye village, coded to Kutcheri (Tsafe, Zamfara), when the militia attempted to attack the village. The militiamen retreated after the gunfight with the Nigerian troops. There were no fatalities.

On 27 March 2024, Nigerian troops engaged a Zamfara militia led by Junaidu Fasagora in an armed clash in the Tsafe general area (Tsafe, Zamfara). On 27 March 2024, the Nigerian troops engaged IS/BH fighters in a firefight in the Gori general area in Gwoza LGA, coded to Gwoza (Gwoza, Borno). One of the militants was killed, and the troops recovered some rustled cattle.

On 27 March 2024, a Niger militia (described as bandits) abducted a civilian in Babanna ward, location coded to Babanna (Borgu, Niger) demanding N2.5 million ransom. On 27 March 2024, a Niger militia (described as bandits) attacked and killed 60 civilians in the Madaka community (Rafi, Niger). 30 others were injured and 86 civilians were abducted.

On 28 March 2024, a joint taskforce comprised of soldiers, policemen, hunters and a local defense militia raided the hideout of an unidentified armed group and engaged them in an armed clash at Yenche-Farakuti forest, coded to Yenche (Kuje, FCT). On 28 March 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted two Christian worshippers after invading the Celestial Church around Oriyarin village, Mowe (Obafemi, Ogun). On 28 March 2024, an unidentified armed group that attacked a police divisional headquarters were repelled by policemen in Neni (Aniocha, Anambra). On 28 March 2024, a Kaduna militia killed two pastoralists when they attacked Kurutu village (Kachia, Kaduna) and 7 other villages (coded separately) 128 cattle were rustled and foodstuff was stolen by the militia.

On 28 March 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted three students of the University of Calabar from one of the school's hostels in Calabar (Calabar Municipal, Cross River). There are no reports on ransom demands.

Around 28 March 2024 (week of), a suspected Irigwe militia killed a 12-year old Fulani pastoralist at Kitago community in Miango district (Bassa, Plateau) as claimed by GAFDAN. The Irigwe Development Association denied the claims.

Around 30 March 2024 (as reported), ISWAP clashed with the Nigerian troops after launching attacks in Gajiganna near Gajiram (Nganzai, Borno). They retreated after sighting the military fighter jets. There were no fatalities.

The soldier was displeased with the service that the trader provided and demanded for a refund, he invited his colleagues to join him in collecting his money and one of them stabbed the victim before they fled.

On 31 March 2024, policemen and neighborhood watch corps engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash along Eke - Ebe road (Udi, Enugu) after the group had abducted civilians from the location. The group abandoned the abductees and fled.

On 31 March 2024, Nigerian army soldiers killed a civilian at Ishinkwo autonomous community in Onicha LGA (Ebonyi) as claimed by the Ishinkwo Community Development Union.

On 31 March 2024, a Kaduna militia abducted 10 civilians from Azzara community, coded to Gidan Azara (Kachia, Kaduna). The abductees included a 5 day old baby and its mother who were abducted after her husband who was the target was not found by the militia.

On 31 March 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a suspected member of Black Axe militia, also called Aiye at the front of his residence in Abeokuta (Abeokuta South, Ogun) where he was relaxing with other persons. The assailants arrived in an unmarked vehicle.

On 31 March 2024, an unidentified armed group killed a lecturer at the University of Maiduguri in his office on the university's campus in Maiduguri (Maiduguri Metro, Borno). The police claimed that eight persons were arrested in connection with the attack.
Around 31 March 2024 (as reported), an unidentified cult militia killed a retired member of a rival militia in Amansee (Awka North, Anambra). The attack led to reprisals in Awka (coded separately).

On 31 March 2024, a Fulani militia attacked civilians as they were returning from Oviri-Oghor, coded to Otu-Jeremi (Udu, Delta). Two persons escaped with injuries while a woman and her baby were abducted.

On 1 February 2024, the Katsina militia shot and killed a commercial motorcycle rider and seized his motorcycle at Tashar Nadaya, near Gazari (Sabuwa, Katsina). The militia also shot a group of four individuals (assumed to be injured) and seized their motorcycles. There was one fatality.

On 1 February 2024, an unidentified armed group killed a woman and her granddaughter at their residence in Tudun Wada area of Daura town (Daura, Katsina). On 2 February 2024, an unidentified armed group killed one person and abducted two others in the Fier community (Pankshin, Plateau). There was one fatality.

On 2 February 2024, troops of 114 battalion engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash at Gampu hills and Ban Yorro area (Yorro, Taraba). The troops rescued four abductees after the group fled. No fatalities.

Around 9 February 2024 (as reported), an unidentified armed group abducted two people from Tudun Wada (Michika, Adamawa). The police, in collaboration with the Nigerian military, arrested the suspect on 8 February 2024.

One person was killed, another was seriously wounded and most of the village was razed by the assailants. The residents were displaced to neighboring communities, other sources report that there were no fatalities and the attack was a reprisal after the villagers denied the pastoralists entry because they had destroyed their watermelon farms.

On 13 February 2024, Sokoto Community Guards Corps operatives killed Fulani locals in Kaffe market (Gada, Sokoto) after they accused them of being linked with militias operating in the area. The victims were slaughtered before a crowd in the market.
On 13 February 2024, about six members of Kebbi militia abducted one person from Kwanar Jwara village, coded to Suru (Suru, Kebbi). No further details.
On 13 February 2024, the Zamfara militia shot and injured three miners when attacking a gold processing site in Abare village (Anka, Zamfara). There were no fatalities.
On 13 February 2024, ISWAP attacked Nigerian troops and engaged them in a firefight in Mairamri village, also spelt as Mairami (Konduga, Borno). No further details.

On 13 February 2024, a Zamfara militia attacked a police station where they killed two policemen and abducted 40 residents in Kasuwar Daji village, Kaura Namoda LGA (Zamfara). The assailants attacked the house to which the police station was attached and 21 of the abductees were residents of the house and members of the same family. Other sources report 4 fatalities.
On 13 February 2024, IS/BH fighters abducted three people from Kukawa town (Kukawa, Borno). No further details.
On 13 February 2024, a Sokoto militia abducted a village head and many residents from Tsabre village (Isa, Sokoto). No further details.

On 13 February 2024, the Zamfara militia opened fire indiscriminately at a truck along the Gusau-Kaura Namoda Road, coded to Kaura Namoda (Kaura Namoda, Zamfara). Four people sustained gunshot injuries. There were no fatalities.
On 13 February 2024, the Katsina militia killed three people when attacking Kan Biri village, coded to Dutsin Ma (Dutsinma, Katsina). No further details.
On 13 February 2024, the Zamfara militia attacked Janhu village, coded to Shinkafi (Shinkafi, Zamfara). No further details.
On 13 February 2024, ISWAP attacked the Nigerian Army and killed two soldiers at a checkpoint in Kanama (Yunusari, Yobe). No further details.

On 14 February 2024, armed Fulani pastoralists killed three people while attacking three communities, including Bulama Bukar village near Gujba town (Gujba, Borno). They razed many houses. They fled on sighting the military deployed to the area. There were three fatalities.

On 14 February 2024, suspected Fulani pastoralists, in a renewed attack, killed four people in Ikobi (Apa, Benue). They raided the community at night when the people were already asleep. One man was injured. There were four fatalities.

On 14 February 2024, the police and vigilantes engaged the Sokoto militia in a firefight on the outskirts of Gigani village (Gwadabawa, Sokoto). The militia had shot a boy in his leg when the victim was fetching water from a well, and the police responded. The police killed one of the militiamen in the encounter and recovered a GPMG Rifle with six live ammunition. There was one fatality.

On 14 February 2024, the Nigerian police exchanged gunfire with the Viking cult militiamen while attacking their hideout in the Mbieri community (Mbaitoli, Imo). A militia member suffered gunshot injuries on his leg and was arrested alongside three others, including their leader. The police recovered two locally made revolvers, shotguns, five rounds of live cartridges, military camouflage shorts and face masks. There were no fatalities.

On 14 February 2024, the Katsina militia invaded a mosque and opened fire on the worshippers in Yargoje (Kankara, Katsina). The Muslims were observing the late-night prayer (Ishai) when they were shot. The militia killed two worshippers inside the mosque, and the third was butchered outside the mosque for resisting abduction. Four people sustained injuries. They abducted a man and two women. There were three fatalities.
Around 15 February 2024 (as reported), the Sokoto militia abducted three men from Gedawa (Wamakko, Sokoto). The victims paid ten million naira each to regain their freedom.

On 15 February 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked the Delta State Polytechnic raped two female students and shot a male student in the leg at their off-campus hostel in Ogwashi-Uku (Aniocha South, Delta). There were no fatalities.

On 15 February 2024, armed Fulani pastoralists attacked and killed several people in the Adijah community in Ugbokpo (Apa, Benue). They opened fire on the residents in broad daylight, triggering panic among the residents who fled to neighboring villages. Unspecified fatalities coded as 3.

On 15 February 2024, the Zamfara militia shot and killed seven people in Nasarawa Godel in Birnin Magaji / Kiyawa LGA, Nasarawa Godel (Kiyawa, Zamfara). The militiamen invaded the community in Toyota Hilux vans. They abducted twenty other people, mostly women. There were seven fatalities.

On 15 February 2024, the Nigerian police clashed with a Kaduna militia trying to abduct some commuters along the Tumburku-Galadimawa Road, coded to Galadimawa (Giwa, Kaduna). The militiamen in large numbers, had blocked the road before the police engaged them. They fled into the bush with gun wounds. The police recovered an AK47 rifle, three AK47 magazines, five rounds of 7.62 x 39mm live ammunition, a Techno mobile phone and two Bajaj motorcycles. There were no fatalities.

On 15 February 2024, the Nigerian police engaged in a firefight with an unidentified armed group while raiding their hideouts between Nasarawa State and the Kuje LGA, coded to Kuje (Kuje, FCT). The police arrested one member of the group and rescued two hostages. There were no fatalities.

On 15 February 2024, a Naval officer shot and killed a man at a military checkpoint at Owerri-Nta (Isiala Ngwa South, Abia) after he refused to stop at the checkpoint. The Navy claimed that the victim was shot because he was struggling for a gun with the soldier after he was invited over an allegation of theft levelled against him.

On 15 February 2024, the Katsina militia opened fire sporadically, trying to abduct a wealthy man in Dangani (Musawa, Katsina). They abducted scores of people instead when they missed their target, who had visited the community for condolences.

On 15 February 2024, a Katsina militia engaged in an armed clash with a local defense militia when they invaded Dangani (Musawa, Katsina) and attempted to abduct a prominent businessman who was visiting. The abduction was foiled and the assailants abducted eight young men instead, there are no reports on ransom demands.

On 15 February 2024, the Katsina militia attacked the house of a local defence militia member and abducted his wife and son in Ungwar Tudun Boka community in Kankara town (Kankara, Katsina). They targeted the defence militia, but he escaped through the back door.

Around 16 February 2024 (as reported), the police shot and killed a member of an unidentified armed group during a clash in Emure LGA, coded to Emure-Ekiti (Emure, Ekiti). The armed group was suspected to have been responsible for abducting some school children in the area. There was one fatality.

On 16 February 2024, suspected Boko Haram (JAS) killed one person while raiding travelers along the Damaturu-Biu highway near Mahdiya village, Gujba LGA, coded to Gujba (Gujba, Yobe). They laid ambush for travelers and abducted an unspecified number of people.

On 16 February 2024, the Kaduna militia killed three people and abducted thirty others in Gwada and Kerawa, coded to Kerawa (Igabi, Kaduna). Seven people were injured in the attack. There were three fatalities.

On 16 February 2024, around midnight, an unidentified armed group numbering up to 100 abducted 16 civilians from Lama and Dekko villages (Zing, Taraba), Monkin village (coded separately) when they invaded the area. The abductees included a catholic priest.
On 16 February 2024, the Niger militia shot and killed two artisanal miners at a mining site close to Alawa (Shiroro, Niger).

On 16 February 2024, around midnight, an unidentified armed group numbering up to 100 abducted 16 civilians from Monkin (Zing, Taraba), Lama and Dekko villages (coded separately) when they invaded the area. The abductees included a catholic priest.

On 16 February 2024, a Niger militia engaged the Nigerian military in a firefight while attempting to invade Alawa (Shiroro, Niger). The troops repelled the attack. The militia shot a vigilante member dead and abducted twelve people. There was one fatality.

On 16 February 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked the Delta State Polytechnic students (for the second time in the week) at their off-campus hostel in Ogwashi-Uku (Aniocha South, Delta). They shot a male student dead and raped one female student while many other students were injured.
On 16 February 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked and injured one person at a residence in Millenium Quarters, Yelwa (Bauchi). No further details.
On 16 February 2024, a Katsina militia killed one person and injured another in Wagini town (Batsari, Katsina). No further details.

On 16 February 2024, the Nigerian troops killed four ISWAP fighters and rescued some hostages in Lamisuri village (Gujba, Yobe). The military responded to a distress call over the abduction of some commuters near Yobe State College of Agriculture, along Buni Yadi. There were four fatalities.

On 16 February 2024, the Kaduna militia killed six people at Kwassam (Kauru, Kaduna) and abducted five others, including a former CBN Director. Two people were injured in the attack. There were six fatalities.

On 16 February 2024, the Anti-Touting Squad shot and killed one person and injured another at the Science Equipment Market, Onitsha (Onisha North, Anambra). The Squad had pursued a man alleged to have urinated in a restricted area into the market. They opened fire sporadically, and two people were hit. Many traders fled for safety. There was one fatality.
On 16 February 2024, a Kaduna militia shot and killed three people and abducted thirty others in Unguwar Tofa in Igabi LGA, coded to Igabi (Igabi, Kaduna).
On 16 February 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a man and abducted his wife in Mai Katako, Bokkos LGA, coded to Bokkos (Bokkos, Plateau). There was one fatality.
On 16 February 2024, IS/BH shot and injured one person in the Ndawang community along the Damboa-Chibok Road, coded to Damboa (Damboa, Borno). No further details.
On 17 February 2024, an unidentified armed group killed the publicity secretary of the APC in Plateau state at a pub in Pankshin town (Pankshin, Plateau). He was killed alongside one other person.
On 17 February 2024, Boko Haram (JAS) attacked and killed two people around Jege village (Gwoza, Borno). No further details.
On 17 February 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted one person in Sarkin-Kudu (Ibi, Taraba). No further details.
On 17 February 2024, the community vigilante group killed three people and injured two others suspected to be spying for marauders in Damba (Illela, Sokoto).
On 17 February 2024, a Katsina militia shot and killed two people and injured four others in Nahuta village (Batsari, Katsina). They abducted an unspecified number of people.

On 17 February 2024, a Sokoto militia shot and injured a male nurse in Raka School, Gwadabawa (Gwadabawa, Sokoto). The victim was attacked when returning home from work. The militia went away with his phone.
On 17 February 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted twenty commuters along the Gusau-Funtua Road coded to Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara). They set vehicles on fire.

On 17 February 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted eight persons as they were traveling along Chokochoko - Obajana - Lokoja highway (Kabba, Kogi). The victims consisted of two women, four men and two students, and a ransom of 30 million naira which was later reduced to 2.6 million was demanded.
On 17 February 2024, a Kaduna militia abducted a 73-year-old man from a Fulani settlement in Janjala village (Kagarko, Kaduna). No further details.
On 17 February 2024, a Kaduna militia abducted thirteen people in Amala-Dam village in Kachia LGA, coded to Kachia (Kachia, Kaduna).

On 17 February 2024, an unidentified armed group physically assaulted a group of women, and stripped them naked along Okolochi - Ihiagwa road (Owerri West, Imo) as a reprisal, after a traditional ruler whom they tried to abducted escaped (coded separately). The assailants were chased away by some youths in the area.

On 17 February 2024, an unidentified armed group shot at the car of the traditional ruler of Okolochi community as he was driving along Okolochi - Ihiagwa (Owerri West, Imo). The traditional ruler sustained an injury, his driver drove through the shooting and hit one of the assailants.
On 17 February 2024, the Kaduna militia killed three people in Samunaka and Ungwar Sarkin Noma villages, coded to Ungwan Sarkin Noma(Kudan, Kaduna). They destroyed houses and livestock.
On 17 February 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted nine women in Mareri (Gusau, Zamfara) when they invaded the area and shot sporadically. There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 17 February 2024, a Zamfara militia killed one person and abducted scores of others at Gidan Kaji in Magazu (Tsafe, Zamfara).

On 17 February 2024, a joint team of security operatives, comprised of police forces, soldiers and NSCDC operatives engaged an Icelander cult militia in an armed clash in their hideout at Idu-Ekpeye, Ahoada LGA (Rivers). The leader of the militia, 2baba who was declared wanted and accused of killing a police officer months prior (coded separately) was killed.

On 17 February 2024, an unidentified armed group disrupted the collation of APC primaries results at a hotel in Benin City (Oredo, Edo) and attacked the journalists and other persons at the venue. Their cameras and other equipment were damaged.
On 17 February 2024, IS/BH fighters attacked and injured an INGO vendor in Wajare Ward, Bama LGA, coded to Bama (Bama, Borno). No further details.
On 17 February 2024, a Katsina militia attacked the Yargoje community (Kankara, Katsina). No further details. Casualties unknown.
On 17 February 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted four people from Guiwa village, Kurya Madaro district, coded to Kuriya (Kaura Namoda, Zamfara). No further details.

On 18 February 2024, a Kaduna militia attacked civilians and killed 12 persons at Gidin Dutse Makyali village in Kufana district (Kajuru, Kaduna). Some of the victims were burned to death, nine others sustained burn injuries and about 17 houses were burned by the assailants who shot sporadically upon arriving the village.

On 18 February 2024, Boko Haram (JAS faction) militants and Nigerian soldiers engaged in an armed clash at Alawa (Shiroro, Niger) when the militants attacked the area, shot sporadically and shouted 'Allahu Akbar'. The militants razed over 30 houses, and stole livestock and valuables. There are no casualties, an unspecified number of civilians were declared missing.
On 18 February 2024, a suspected Fulani militia killed two civilians and injured five others at Rawuru in Barkin Ladi LGA (Plateau) for unclear reasons.

On 18 February 2024, overnight, a Zamfara militia killed the Divisional Criminal Officer and wounded several policemen when they invaded Zurmi town (Zurmi, Zamfara). The divisional police station in the town was set ablaze by the militia in the attack which was a reprisal after their colleagues were killed by a local defense militia (coded separately). The militia fled when they sighted military forces. Some sources report that the militia were dressed as community protection guards and also engaged the guard whom they overpowered in a clash, other sources report 7 fatalities including two policemen.

On 18 February 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted a 16-year-old female from Buma village (Shani, Borno). The abductors demanded an eight-million-naira ransom. The police and local hunters invaded (no reported clash) the abductors' hideout around Fotta village, Gombi, Adamawa, arrested three members of the armed group and rescued the hostage.

On 18 February 2024, a Niger militia killed three civilians and abducted 15 women at Bassa community (Shiroro, Niger). The attack was a retaliation for the killing of their colleagues by security operatives three weeks earlier.

On 18 February 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted commuters and a corpse at Umuoka (Udi, Enugu). The corpse was being conveyed from Lagos to the deceased hometown in Enugu. The number of other occupants in the vehicle who were all abducted is unspecified and a ransom of 50 million naira was demanded. Other sources report that the corpse was later recovered by soldiers (means not stated) and the abductees were three.

On 18 February 2024, troops of sector 2 of Operation Hadin Kai and Yobe state hunters group engaged ISWAP militants in an armed clash during an operation at Maltari village, coded to nearby Kukareta (Damaturu, Yobe). Three militants were killed, rifles, ammunition, grenades and motorcycles were recovered by the troops.

On 18 February 2024, the Nigerian troops engaged ISWAP in a firefight in Malari village (Konduga, Borno). The ISWAP members were extorting zakat levies from the community when the army attacked them. They killed three ISWAP members and recovered two AK 47 riffles, two magazines, two hand grenades and one motorcycle.
On 18 February 2024, a Zamfara militia killed four civilians and abducted seven others in Maradun (Maradun, Zamfara). The victims were working to clear a field when they were attacked.
On 18 February 2024, IS/BH shot and injured a businessman at Burum junction in Damboa LGA, coded to Damboa (Damboa, Borno). No further details.
On 19 February 2024, a Niger militia abducted 30 civilians, most of whom were women from Dangunu (Muya, Niger). At least 15 other persons were abducted from Pai and Katerma, (coded separately).
On 19 February 2024, a Niger militia abducted at least 15 civilians from Pai and an unspecified number of others from Katerma (Muya, Niger) coded to Sarkin Pawa.

On 19 February 2024, a Katsina militia attacked civilians at Yar Nasarawa, coded and spelled as Nassarawa (Faskari, Katsina). Between three and six persons including the ward head were killed, about 10 others were wounded, ten motorcycles, shops and three houses were set ablaze by the assailants.

On 19 February 2024, a Katsina militia attacked civilians at Ruwan Godiya (Faskari, Katsina), Nassarawa and Kyarbishiyar Danfillo (coded separately). An unspecified number of residents were wounded, the villages were attacked simultaneously.

On 19 February 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a councilor representing Ohwase ward (Udu, Delta) at his residence. Other sources report that the attack was related to cult activities.

On 19 February 2024, Opolo and Okutukutu communal militias clashed following a land dispute in Opolo (Yenagoa, Bayelsa). Two persons were killed in the clash. The Mbiama- Yenagoa road was blocked with bonfires and traffic was disrupted as a result of the clash.

On 19 February 2024, an unidentified armed group killed a man between Ikobi and Oloba, as he was returning to Ugbokpo (Apa, Benue). Other sources claim that one other person escaped with gunshot injuries.

On 19 February 2024, police forces invaded the hideout of an unidentified armed group and engaged them in an armed clash at Achalla (Awka North, Anambra). The group was responsible for enforcing sit-in orders in the area. An unspecified number of its members sustained injuries, they all fled, five exotic cars, arms and ammunition were recovered.

On 19 February 2024, a local defence militia engaged a Zamfara militia in a firefight in the Boko community (Zurmi, Zamfara). An unspecified number of the Zamfara militia were killed, three arrested, and motorcycles were recovered. Unspecified fatalities coded as 3.
On 19 February 2024, a Sokoto militia shot and injured a United Nations Community Focal Person around Girls' high school in Gwadabawa (Gwadabawa, Sokoto). No further details.
On 19 February 2024, the Aye, alias Black Axe, and Eiye cult militiamen clashed in Kwale (Ndokwa West, Delta). 4 people were killed.

On 19 February 2024, a Zamfara militia attacked civilians at Makera (Talata Mafara, Zamfara) and killed nine persons. 53 others were abducted, the murdered victims were shit when they attempted to escape abduction.

On 19 February 2024, a Katsina militia attacked civilians at Kyarbishiyar Danfillo (Faskari, Katsina), Nassarawa and Ruwan Godiya (coded separately). At least one person was killed and an unspecified number of residents were wounded, the villages were attacked simultaneously.
On 19 February 2024, ISWAP fighters abducted many women gathering firewood around Borno College of Basic Studies in Bama town (Bama, Borno). No further details.

On 19 February 2024, a joint security team, coded as police and military forces killed a Sokoto militia leader called Mai Dubu Dubu during an armed clash at Kware forest in Kware LGA (Sokoto). Other members of the militia fled, and 21 rounds of live ammunition were recovered by the troops.

On 20 February 2024, Nigerian troops came under fire from the Kaduna militia while on a clearance Operation in Yadi Forest, coded to Birnin-Gwari (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). The troops responded and killed one of the attackers. Other militiamen fled the scene. The military recovered two AK 47 Rifles, six AK 47 Magazines, five rounds of 7.62mm Special ammunition, 331 rounds of 7.62mm x 54 PKT Machine Gun ammunition, and two PKT Machine Gun ammunition links. There was one fatality.

On 20 February 2024, Katsina militia shot and killed nine people in the Lambo community near Wurma (Kurfi, Katsina). The militia also set houses and vehicles on fire and burnt down grains. There were nine fatalities.

On 20 February 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed one person around Isokan Estate, behind Premier Grammar School Abeokuta North, coded to Ibara-Orile (Abeokuta North, Ogun). No further details.
On 20 February 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed three people in Opah (Otukpo, Benue). They killed two more people the next day, coded separately.
On 20 February 2024, a Katsina militia abducted 26 commuters at Ungwuwan Boka, Faskari LGA (Katsina) which is located along Funtua - Gusau highway. The victims were occupants of two vehicles.

On 20 February 2024, ISWAP fighters on sixteen motorcycles attacked the Nigerian troops in Khaddamari (Jere, Borno) and Zabarmari (coded separately). The troops engaged them in a firefight until they retreated. There were no fatalities.

On 20 February 2024, ISWAP fighters on sixteen motorcycles attacked the Nigerian troops in Zamarmari, also spelt as Zabarmari (Jere, Borno) and Khaddamari (coded separately). The troops engaged them in a firefight until they retreated. There were no fatalities.

On 20 February 2024, ISWAP attacked Nigerian troops on the eastern outskirts of Buniyadi, also spelt as Buni Yadi town (Gujba, Yobe). The army responded and engaged them in a firefight. ISWAP killed one soldier and injured another. They set a gun truck on fire.
On 20 February 2024, a Katsina militia abducted four women and a man from Bayan Gidan Rediyo Quarters in Dutsin Ma town (Dutsinma, Katsina). The man later escaped. No further details.

On 20 February 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed two Ebubeagu operatives (Neighbourhood Vigilante members) in Iboko (Izzi, Ebonyi). The armed group first shot two fuel attendants dead at a fueling station before proceeding to attack the vigilante members. They axed the corpses of the vigilante members after killing them. The onslaught raised tension in the community, and the people scampered for safety. There were four fatalities.
On 20 February 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted an unspecified number of commuters at Gidan Kaji in Magazu (Tsafe, Zamfara).

On 20 February 2024, a Zamfara militia were engaged in an armed clash with policemen who responded to a distress call at Kwaren Kirya village in Maru LGA (Zamfara) along Gusau - Sokoto highway and foiled an abduction attempt, as claimed by the Zamfara state command of the police force. Other sources claimed that 26 commuters were abducted before security operatives arrived. No casualties.

On 21 February 2024, the police exchanged gunfire with an unidentified armed group and shot one dead in Tunga Umoru village (Borgu, Niger). The clash occurred when the police ambushed the armed group attempting to pick up 3 million naira extorted from a man they threatened to abduct. The police rescued a female hostage after other members of the armed group escaped with gun wounds. There was one fatality.

On 21 February 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked and killed two people in Opah (Otukpo, Benue). They raped women and burnt farm produce and other property. The armed group had killed three people the previous day, coded separately. There were two fatalities.
On 21 February 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted a female from her residence in Zone B, Apo Resettlement (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The abductors demanded a ransom. No further details.
On 21 February 2024, a Katsina militia ambushed and killed at least five members of the Community Watch Corps patrolling the Dogon Daji area of Sabuwa LGA, coded to Sabuwa (Sabuwa, Katsina).

On 21 February 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a police inspector when attacking a police checkpoint at the Eliozu flyover in Obio/Akpo LGA coded to Rumuodomaya (Obi, Rivers). The police returned fire and killed one of the assailants. Other members of the armed group escaped and fled the scene. There were two fatalities.

On 21 February 2024, a Katsina militia killed an unspecified number of people while attacking Munhaye village, Faskari LGA, coded to Faskari (Faskari, Katsina). They abducted many others. Unspecified fatalities coded as 3.
On 21 February 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked two communities in Turan District, Kwande LGA, coded to Kwande (Kwande, Benue). No further details. Casualties unknown.

On 21 February 2024, the Nigerian troops of Operation Whirl Stroke exchanged gunfire with an unidentified armed group in Jootar village in Ukum LGA, coded to Chito (Ukum, Benue). The armed group had abducted twelve people and was transporting them from Imo to Adamawa state when the troops intercepted them. They abandoned their hostages and fled after the gunfight with the military. There were no fatalities.

On 21 February 2024, a joint Task Force involving the police, KSCWC and vigilantes invaded the Katsina militia camp, newly acquired by Dankarami and Barbaru in Yar Tepa, Birdigau near Malumfashi (Malumfashi, Katsina) in an attempt to dislodge the militia from the hideout. The ensuing firefight claimed the lives of the KSCWC commander for Kankara, four local vigilantes and two volunteers from Birdigau and Gidan Gwanji. The militia group lost about twenty fighters. Another source reported that a police officer sustained an injury, and the force rescued 332 rustled cattle. There were about twenty-seven fatalities.

Around 22 February 2024 (as reported), the Nigerian troops on patrol clashed with the Kaduna militia in Birnin Gwari LGA, coded to Maganda (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna), Igabi and Giwa LGA, coded separately. They killed two militiamen and recovered 1 AK 47 rifle,1 AK 47 Magazine, three rounds of 7.62mm Special, 1 Techno phone, 3 Hilux and motorcycle keys, wraps of substance suspected to be marijuana, tramadol tablets and the sum of 13,200 Naira only. Many rustled cattle used as shields were shot dead in the process. Two fatalities shared within the three events-one fatality coded.

On 22 February 2024, the Nigerian troops engaged the Kaduna militia in a firefight around the Bada/Riyawa general areas of Chikun and Igabi LGA, coded to Ungwan Liman Riyawa (Chikun, Kaduna). The military killed six militiamen, including Boderi Isyaku, A kingpin responsible for many attacks in the state. The troops recovered two AK47 rifles, 300 rounds of ammunition, nine AK47 magazines, one magazine carrier, one Baofeng radio set and five motorcycles. There were six fatalities.
On 22 February 2024, an unidentified cult militia killed one member of rival SVC in Ogwashi-Uku (Aniocha South, Delta). Three others were wounded and the murdered victim was a leader of the cult.

On 22 February 2024, the Niger militia killed two people and injured one other in Bassa (Shiroro, Niger). They abducted an unspecified number of people and rustled livestock. There were two fatalities.

Around 22 February 2024 (as reported), the Nigerian troops on patrol clashed with the Kaduna militia in Giwa LGA, coded to Magaba (Giwa, Kaduna), Igabi and Birnin Gwari LGA, coded separately. They killed two militiamen and recovered 1 AK 47 rifle,1 AK 47 Magazine, three rounds of 7.62mm Special, 1 Techno phone, 3 Hilux and motorcycle keys, wraps of substance suspected to be marijuana, tramadol tablets and the sum of 13,200 Naira only. Many rustled cattle used as shields were shot dead in the process.

On 22 February 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted many commuters from two vehicles around Fakun Shanu, along the Mayanchi-Anka Road in Talata Mafara LGA, coded to Talata Mafara (Talata Mafara, Zamfara). No further details.

Around 22 February 2024 (as reported), the Nigerian troops on patrol clashed with the Kaduna militia in the Igabi LGA, coded to Igabi (Igabi, Kaduna), Giwa and Birnin Gwari LGA, coded separately. They killed two militiamen and recovered 1 AK 47 rifle,1 AK 47 Magazine, three rounds of 7.62mm Special, 1 Techno phone, 3 Hilux and motorcycle keys, wraps of substance suspected to be marijuana, tramadol tablets and the sum of 13,200 Naira only. Many rustled cattle used as shields were shot dead in the process. Two fatalities shared within the three events-one fatality coded.
On 22 February 2024, a Katsina militia abducted a woman from a residence in Kankara town (Kankara, Katsina). No further details.

On 23 February 2024, an unidentified armed group engaged in a clash with hunters and a local defense militia when they attacked civilians between Maloko and Sulu villages in Omupo district, coded to Omupo (Ifelodun, Kwara). Two abductees were rescued, the third one escaped earlier and one of the assailants was killed, two others were arrested, other sources reported that five of the assailants were arrested.

On 23 February 2024, the Nigerian troops and the community defence militia clashed with a Sokoto militia after the militia attacked the Arba Community (Wurno, Sokoto). They abducted an unspecified number of people. The troops killed five militiamen. There were five fatalities.

Around 23 February 2024 (as reported), suspected Aye cultists, also called Black Axe, killed a mechanic in the Okelele near Ibagun (Ilorin East, Kwara). The militia invaded the area, shot the mechanic at close range, and smashed his head with a big stone. A cloth weaver was also killed by the cultists in the Baruba area of Ilorin East, coded separately. There was one fatality.

Around 23 February 2024 (as reported), suspected Aye cultists, also called Black Axe, killed a cloth weaver in Baruba, Ilorin East, coded to Illorin (Ilorin East, Kwara). The militia also killed a mechanic in Okelele, coded separately. There was one fatality.

On 23 February 2024, the NSVC engaged a Niger militia in a firefight when the militia attacked Unguwan Usman and Bassa, coded to Bassa (Shiroro, Niger). The militia had burnt down houses and food supplies before NSVC intervened and engaged them. Three NSVC members were killed during the confrontation. There were three fatalities.

On 23 February 2024, a Kaduna militia killed two civilians, wounded five and abducted 16 others when they attacked Gidan Busa (Kachia, Kaduna). Eight of the abductees were residents of the same house.

On 23 February 2024, an unidentified armed group killed one abductee who was among the seven people that were abducted from Kuduru community (Bwari, FCT). The victim one of the seven people from the community abducted on December 2023 (coded separately). The victim was killed over the failure of the abductees' families to pay the demanded ransom of 290 million naira. Location coded to where the abduction happened.

On 23 February 2024, an unidentified armed group, numbering about fifteen, shot and killed the President General of the Umuoji community in Umuoji (Idemili North, Anambra). The attack triggered panic in the community.

On 23 February 2024, an unidentified armed group opened fire sporadically and shot two people, including an NDLEA officer (likely unarmed), along the Airport Road, Sokoto (Wamakko, Sokoto). They also abducted three persons. There were two fatalities.

On 23 February 2024, the Nigerian troops and the community protection guards engaged in a firefight with a Zamfara militia after the militia had attacked the Ruwan Tofa community in Kwatarkwashi (Bungudu, Zamfara). The militia had killed an unspecified number of people and abducted many others before the military intervened. Two soldiers and an unspecified number of militia and protection guard members were killed in the encounter. An unspecified number of the militia, the villagers, the protection guards members were killed, coded as 10, and two soldiers killed. Total fatalities coded as 12.

On 23 February 2024, Red Axe and Black Axe cult militia, also called Red and Black, respectively, engaged in an armed clash at North Bank (Makurdi, Benue) that continued until the following day (coded separately). Seven people were killed, including one who was beheaded. Security operatives consisting of soldiers, police and DSS were deployed to the area and made arrests. 7 fatalities split across two events, coded as 4.
On 23 February 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a man at Umugada Market Junction, Irete (Owerri West, Imo). The victim was shot dead while the group attempted to abduct him.

On 24 February 2024, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists numbering up to 50 killed one civilian on his farm and set many houses ablaze when they invaded Tsokar, a farming community in Agagbe (Gwer West, Benue). Several persons were wounded and others escaped.
On 24 February 2024, an unidentified armed group killed a civilian when they invaded Ago Are community (Atisbo, Oyo). Some sources claim that there has been some boundary dispute in the community.

On 24 February 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted 8 travelers along Ughelli - Patani road (Ughelli North, Delta) while they were heading to Yenagoa. Four of the abductees consisting of three women and one man were released, under unknown circumstances.

On 24 February 2024, Nigerian troops engaged a presumed Katsina militia in an armed clash at Aliero West axis. Two militia leaders, Baldi and Baban Yara, acting on the Zamfara/Katsina axis, and 28 other militia members were killed. Location coded to Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara)

On 24 February 2024, a Katsina militia engaged in an armed clash with a rival Zamfara militia led by Ado Aliero at Hayin Al haji and Munhaye forests, coded to Munhaye (Tsafe, Zamfara). The clash took place after the Katsina militia invaded the area, which is Ado Alieru's village and attempted to abduct residents. Scores of militia members were killed, coded as 20.

On 24 February 2024, the Nigerian troops repelled an ISWAP attack and engaged them in a firefight in Miringa (Biu, Borno). The troops killed one ISWAP fighter and recovered one PKT gun and many ammunitions.

Around 24 February 2024 (as reported), an unidentified group killed 12 out of the 19 people whom they abducted from Galadimawa (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The victims were abducted in November 2023 (coded separately). One of the murdered abductees was an aide to Senator Ned Nwoko. Location coded to where they were abducted from.
On 24 February 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted eleven commuters along Chafe-Gusau Road in Chafe LGA, coded to Chafe, also spelt as Tsafe (Tsafe, Zamfara).

On 24 February 2024, Red Axe and Black Axe cult militia, also called Red and Black, respectively, engaged in an armed clash at North Bank (Makurdi, Benue) for the second consecutive day. Seven people were killed, including one who was beheaded. Security operatives consisting of soldiers, police and DSS were deployed to the area and made arrests. 7 fatalities split across two events coded as 3.

On 25 February 2024, MNJTF deployed from the Damasak base engaged the Boko Haram (JAS faction) militants in an armed clash at Alayi Bulanti, coded to Damasak (Mobbar, Borno). The militants fled, two AK47 rifles, five magazines and ammunition were recovered by the troops. There were no fatalities.

On 25 February 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted 16 passengers from two vehicles along Ette - Enugu-Ezike road, coded to Enugu-Ezike (Igbo Eze North, Enugu). The abductees were rescued the following day in Kogi state by police forces who combed the bushes (no interaction was reported).

On 25 February 2024, an unidentified armed group killed the driver of a bus and one passenger and abducted two others at Opanda (Uzo Uwani, Enugu). The victims were traveling to Nsukka from Adani, one of the abductees was a popular business man based in Adani.

On 25 February 2024, a Katsina militia engaged in an armed clash with military and police forces who were on patrol along Kukar Babangida to Yar Gaya feeder road, coded to Kukar Babangida (Jibia, Katsina). Ten abductees were rescued by the troops.
On 25 February 2024, Boko Haram (JAS) attacked ISWAP fighters around Kangarwa village (Kukawa, Borno). No casualties.
On 25 February 2024, a Katsina militia killed one civilian and abducted 17 women and children at Burdugau village (Malumfashi, Katsina). Hundreds of livestock were stolen by the assailants.

On 25 February 2024, a Zamfara militia opened fire sporadically at vehicles and abducted many people along the Chafe-Funtua Road in Chafe LGA, coded to Chafe, also spelt as Tsafe (Tsafe, Zamfara). There were no fatalities.

On 25 February 2024, a Zamfara militia riding over 40 motorcycles attacked policemen at a checkpoint an engaged them in an armed clash in Tazame, less than one kilometers away from Kwatarkwashi (Bungudu, Zamfara). One policeman was killed, an unspecified number of others were injured, and the rest fled while the militia set valuables ablaze.
On 25 February 2024, NSCDC operatives tortured two members of the PTD branch of NUPENG in Owerri (Owerri Municipal, Imo) as claimed by the union. The reason for the torture was not mentioned.

Around 26 February 2024 (as reported), police forces, hunters and local defense militia operatives raided the hideouts of an unidentified armed group and engaged then in an armed clash at Yorro LGA, coded to Yorro (Taraba) and Zing LGA (coded separately). 40 abductees were rescued, many of the group's members were killed and 10 of them were arrested. Many fatalities coded as 10 and split across two events, coded as 5 in this event.

Around 26 February 2024 (as reported), police forces, hunters and local defense militia operatives raided the hideouts of an unidentified armed group and engaged then in an armed clash at Zing LGA, coded to Zing (Taraba) and Yorro LGA (coded separately). 40 abductees were rescued, many of the group's members were killed and 10 of them were arrested. Many fatalities coded as 10 and split across two events, coded as 5 to this event.

On 26 February 2024, civilians JFT engaged a Katsina militia in a firefight after the militia attacked a health facility at Wurma village (Kurfi, Katsina). They first chased the police away without any resistance and later injured many people and abducted 13 others. They also burnt an ambulance, two Hilux vans and three private vehicles. The hunters succeeded in driving the militia out of the village. There were no fatalities.

On 26 February 2024, Nigerian troops, coded as military forces, raided a hideout of IPOB militants and engaged them in an armed clash at Egbuoma/ Osiam (Oguta, Imo). One militant was killed and a car was retrieved from the hideout.

On 26 February 2024, a Kaduna militia shot and killed five people and injured many others when attacking the Ungwan Ganye B and Sabon Gida communities, coded to Gwantu (Sanga, Kaduna). The militia rode on motorcycles and invaded the communities when the residents were already sleeping.
On 26 February 2024, an unidentified armed group stabbed and killed a motorcyclist in Yelwa (Bauchi). They stole his motorcycle.
On 26 February 2024, a Zamfara militia killed four people while attacking Kurar Mota (Bungudu, Zamfara). They injured an unspecified number of others.
On 26 February 2024, a Katsina militia killed six people and injured many others in Unguwar Mai Rabo village (Malumfashi, Katsina).
On 26 February 2024, an unidentified armed group killed two policemen and 12 civilians at Katapka village (Toto, Nassarawa). The village head was one of the fatalities.

On 26 February 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted three civilians who were witnesses for the AA Kogi state gubernatorial candidate at the election tribunal that sat at the National Judicial Institute, Karonmajigi (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The Kogi state chairman of the APC denied the claims made by the AA, insisting he was at the venue and did not witness an abduction. Some sources claimed the abductees were released while others denied the claims.

On 26 February 2024, the Eket and Esiet Eket clashed with the Ibeno people in Ibeno LGA, coded to Ibeno (Ibeno, Akwa Ibom), over a lingering land dispute between the two communities. The Eket accused the Ibeno people of destroying molded blocks belonging to an Eket person and accused them of land encroachment. They attacked the community at night, and many people were killed and injured on the two sides. They also abducted many others. The residents of the affected communities fled their homes for fear of a reprisal attack. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 26 February 2024, Nigerian troops of Operation Hadarin Daji engaged a Zamfara militia in a firefight in Bayan Ruwa, near Maradun (Maradun, Zamfara). The troops blocked the Bayan Ruwa crossing and opened fire on the militia as they were crossing into the forest. They destroyed the militia's enclaves and rescued eight hostages. They killed scores of the militiamen. Scores of fatalities coded as 20.
On 26 February 2024, a Zamfara militia shot and killed three people in Kaura Namoda LGA, coded to Kaura Namoda (Kaura Namoda, Zamfara).

On 26 February 2024, an unidentified armed group killed three civilians at Tse Achigbe community in Kwande LGA, coded to Kwande (Benue). The assailants prevented the other locals from retrieving the corpses for burial.
On 26 February 2024, suspected Fulani herders killed one person in Agena-Ya village, Ngenev, Borikyo (Ukum, Benue). No further details.

On 26 February 2024, an unidentified armed group engaged in an armed clash with police forces who foiled the group's attempt to attack some residents of Mabel community, on the outskirts of Bokkos town (Bokkos, Plateau). The assailants fled.
On 26 February 2024, a Katsina militia shot and killed one person in Unguwar Makera village near Malumfashi (Malumfashi, Katsina). They burned down five houses, shops and vehicles.
On 27 February 2024, an unidentified armed group killed one person and injured others along the Nyido-Manya road near the Tosso community (Kurmi, Taraba). They also abducted four people.

On 27 February 2024, the Nigerian troops clashed with IPOB/ESN while raiding their camps in Egbuoma and Oslam communities, coded to Egbuoma (Oguta, Imo). One IPOB fighter was shot dead, and many others escaped with gun wounds. The troops recovered a vehicle and charms. There was one fatality.
On 27 February 2024, a Sokoto militia shot and killed a village head on his way to the farm in the Rumbuje community, Asara Ward, Gwadabawa (Gwadabawa, Sokoto).

On 27 February 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted an unspecified number of commuters after blocking the Sokoto- Gusau Highway in Gusau LGA, coded to Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara). Nigerian security forces, likely to be the Army, trailed them. No further details.
On 27 February 2024, ISWAP killed one person on a farm around Banki junction, Bama town (Bama, Borno).

On 27 February 2024, KADVIS clashed with a Kaduna militia when they attacked Angwan Gedage village in Kachia LGA, coded to Kachia (Kachia, Kaduna). The militia was outgunned and forced to retreat. There were no fatalities.

Around 28 February 2024, an unidentified armed group suspected to be illegal miners ambushed soldiers and forest guards at Ifumkpa community (Akamkpa, Cross River), coded to Akankpa. One rifle belonging to the forest guards was destroyed, casualties unknown.

On 28 February 2024, the Nigerian military engaged a Kaduna militia in a firefight at Ligari village (Chikun, Kaduna). The clash occurred as the militiamen were trying to escape with their hostages after the abduction and killing of two vigilante members in Ungwar Auta, coded separately. The military vehicles got burnt during the shootout. There were no fatalities.
On 28 February 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked and killed a youth leader in Nakere (Wamba, Nassarawa). They abducted a businessman and a woman married to a pastor and injured many others.
On 28 February 2024, Fulani armed pastoralists ambushed and attacked some police officers on a rescue mission in Agadama (Ughelli North, Delta). No further details.

On 28 February 2024, a Kebbi militia attacked and injured one person and abducted another at the Fadama area on the outskirts of Zaima village, coded to Wasagu (Danko, Kebbi). There were no fatalities.

On 28 February 2024, a Kaduna militia shot and killed two local defense militia in Anguwan Auta, coded to Goni Gora (Chikun, Kaduna). The militia stormed the community at night and sporadically opened fire on the residents. Many residents were abducted, other sources report that the abductees were 16, and others sustained injuries from the attack. They also clashed with the military at Ligari village (coded separately). A ransom of 40 trillion naira, 11 Hilux vans and 150 motorcycles were demanded.
On 28 February 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted at least twelve women in Dundaye and Taketsaba villages in Talata Mafara LGA, coded to Talata Mafara (Talata Mafara, Zamfara).

On 28 February 2024, a Zamfara militia attacked and injured an unspecified number of people in transit along the Funtua-Gusau Highway, coded to Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara). Many others were abducted. There were no fatalities.

On 28 February 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked Alokpa (Agatu, Benue). The attack lasted until the other day (coded separately). Five people were killed altogether. Five fatalities split between the two events, coded as 3 on this event.
On 28 February 2024, hunters killed one member of an unidentified communal militia and recovered 74 stolen cows at Jarkuka village in Bachaka ward (Arewa, Kebbi).

On 28 February 2024, an assumed Fulani militia attacked a traditional ruler in Agbede (Etsako West, Edo) while he and his wife were working on their farm. The man was seriously injured, and in a critical condition in a hospital, as claimed by a coalition of civil rights group who petitioned the IGP. He was wounded for resisting the assailants' attempt to abducted them, while his wife was abducted.

Around 28 February 2024 (as reported), SEC, also called Eiye Confraternity, clashed amongst themselves in Benin City (Oredo, Edo) over the non-payment of monthly dues by some members. Five of the militia members were arrested by police forces who were on patrol.

On 28 February 2024, a Zamfara militia attacked and killed 69 people in Danbawa, Mazzabi, Danmaji, Burmukai, Katuge, and Tabbani villages in Maru LGA, location coded to the administrative headquarters, Maru (Zamfara).

On 28 February 2024, the Nigerian troops, MNJTF and CJTF, came under attack from IS/BH in the Timbuktu triangle in the Lake Chad Region, coded to Damboa (Damboa, Borno). The military killed three IS/BH fighters after they returned fire, and the militiamen fled. They recovered one MRAP, one gun truck, one Dushka Machine Gun, one AK 47 Rifle and one locally fabricated gun. They also captured one Rocket Propelled Grenade (RPG) Bomb, 273 rounds of 7.62mm Special ammunition, one Pumping machine, 65 Dushka links, 48 General Purpose Machine Gun links and three motorbikes.
On 28 February 2024, a Zamfara militia attacked the district police station in Magami (Gusau, Zamfara). They killed one police officer and injured another.

On 29 February 2024, a Zamfara militia engaged troops of Operation Hadarin Daji who responded to a distress call in an armed clash at Unguwar Sarkin Muslumi, coded to Bukuyum (Bukkuyum, Zamfara). One militiaman was killed and two abductees were rescued.

On 29 February 2024, and for the second consecutive day, an unidentified armed group attacked Alokpa (Agatu, Benue). Five people were killed altogether. Five fatalities split between the two events, coded as 2 for this event.

On 29 February 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted twenty-three people from the Kawu community in Bwari (Bwari, FCT). Among the victims, a former PDP Ward Chairman and a son of the District Head. The armed group numbering about forty invaded the community from the Kuyeri Forest in Kaduna State.

On 29 February 2024, ISWAP claimed to have fired artillery shells at a Nigerian Army barracks in Chiralia town (Damboa, Borno). Another source debunked the claim that there was a military barrack in Chiralia. The source reported that CJTF Hilux Van triggered an IED planted by ISWAP, killing two CJTF members. The Nigerian troop killed a suicide bomber deployed by ISWAP during the encounter. There were three fatalities.

On 29 February 2024, a Zamfara militia attacked a mosque and abducted scores of worshippers in Kwarin Mai-Saje, on the outskirts of Tsafe town (Tsafe, Zamfara). The militia attacked the mosques when the early morning prayer was being said with the intent of carrying out a massive abduction. Another source reported that the worshippers escaped the abduction except for three older men who were taken away by the militia. The militia abandoned one of the hostages when he could not walk fast, and the police rescued him.
On 29 February 2024, suspected IS/BH abducted an unspecified number of IDPs who ventured out of the camps in search of firewood in Ngala (Ngala, Borno).

On 1 January 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted the council chairman of Akwanga LGA, his friend and two NSCDC operatives who were his security detail at Ningo village, coded as Anjoju (Akwanga, Nassarawa) as they were traveling along Akwanga - Andaha road. The NSCDC operatives were armed, but hid their guns from the abductors who did not notice them. A ransom of 50 million was demanded, the abductees were released on 2 January after a ransom of 10 million naira was paid. The police spokesperson denied the payment of ransom.

On 1 January 2024, suspected Boko Haram [JAS faction] dressed in military uniform attacked civilians at Tsiha, coded and spelled as Chiha (Chibok, Borno). Three persons were killed, one young lady was abducted by the militants who also attacked Gatamarwa village [coded separately].

On 1 January 2024, suspected Boko Haram [JAS faction] dressed in military uniform attacked civilians at Gatamarwa ward, coded to Chiha (Chibok, Borno). Nine persons were killed, two others were wounded by the militants who proceeded to attack Chiha village [coded separately].
On 1 January 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted several travelers around Kwanar Sado, coded to Sado (Talata Mafara, Zamfara). The abductees were en route Gusau from Sokoto.
On 1 January 2024, an unidentified armed group killed eight civilians in Katapka community (Toto, Nassarawa). The assailants set vehicles and houses, including the palace of the village head, ablaze.
On 1 January 2024, an unidentified armed group killed a commercial motorcyclist (Okada rider) around Bokkos market (Bokkos, Plateau) while he was bringing a passenger to the area.

On 1 January 2024, an unidentified armed group killed the chief imam of a mosque at Ndun village in Tangu district (Bokkos, Plateau) when he and his brother who was wounded by the assailants went to the community to recover their belongings following a prior attack [coded separately]. Both victims were also Fulani pastoralists.

Around 2 January 2024 (as reported), a soldier killed two of his colleagues when he wrongly handled an artillery weapon during an operation around Molai area (Jere, Borno). Five others were wounded, the Army spokesperson denied that there were fatalities and stated that five persons were wounded.
On 2 January 2024, a Niger militia abducted three civilians from Garam community (Tafa, Niger). The victims were members of the same family.

On 2 January 2024, a suspected unidentified cult militia attacked civilians at Ikem community in Okehi division (Etche, Rivers). Two persons were killed, fours others were wounded, some of them in critical condition. The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 2 January 2024, armed Fulani pastoralists shot one person whom they abducted with seven others around the Port Harcourt International Airport Omagwa (Ikwerre, Rivers). Other sources report an unspecified number of wounded persons. Three abductees were rescued by the police who claimed to have mounted pressure on the abductors.

On 2 January 2024, the Nigerian troops engaged an unidentified armed group in a firefight in Bang, Zamtip, and Gwantim villages, Wase LGA, coded to Wase (Wase, Plateau). The troop arrested four members of the armed group and recovered three motorcycles. There were no fatalities.
On 2 January 2024, suspected Boko Haram (JAS) fighters shot and killed two loggers in Dure-wale, Dure (Gwoza, Borno). The victims had gone to fetch firewood when they were attacked.
On 2 January 2024, an unidentified armed group killed one civilian and abducted two others at Furaka community, coded to Jos (Jos North, Plateau). The abductees included one female and a male.

On 2 January 2024, a Zamfara militia who attempted to attack civilians were engaged in an armed clash with security operatives [coded as military forces] and a local defense militia at Nahuche (Bungudu, Zamfara). Six civilians were killed and one was wounded by the militia.

On 2 January 2024, an unidentified armed group engaged in an armed clash with police forces at Zuma community in Bwari (FCT). Two policemen were wounded and later died, an unspecified number of residents were abducted. A ransom of 30 million naira, other sources report 60 million, 10 for each of the six girls was demanded for a family who were abducted, after their father was released to gather the ransom. The eldest of the abductees was killed over a delay in ransom payment, the ransom was increased to 65 million naira. The abductees were released.

On 2 January 2024, an unidentified armed group suspected to be assassins killed the paramount ruler of Anwunugbokor community at his home in Odimeneyi (Ahoada, Rivers). The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 3 January 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted three travelers on the Obiri-Ikwerre - Airport Road, coded to Port Harcourt International Airport (Ikwerre, Rivers). The armed group blocked the left flank of the highway and ambushed vehicles going and coming from the airport.

On 3 January 2024, the troops of Operation Hadarin Daji clashed with the Zamfara militia while on a search and rescue operation at Dan Sadau (Maru, Zamfara) and Dandalla, coded separately. The troops rescued nine hostages while the militiamen fled after being outgunned. There were no fatalities.

On 3 January 2024, the troops of Operation Hadarin Daji clashed with the Zamfara militia while on a search and rescue operation at Dandalla (Maru, Zamfara) and Dan Sadau, coded separately. The troops rescued nine hostages while the militiamen fled after being outgunned. There were no fatalities.

On 3 January 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted one person along Kaskara-Mangu Road in Barkin Ladi LGA, coded to Barkin Ladi (Barkin Ladi, Plateau). The Nigerian military rescued the hostage and arrested one of the abductors.

On 3 January 2024, the troops of Operation Hadarin Daji engaged in a firefight with the Katsina militia at Safana LGA, coded to Safana (Safana, Katsina) and Batsari LGA, coded separately. The troops killed ten militiamen in the attacks. The troops recovered an AK-47 Rifle, ammunition, seven Dane guns, three locally fabricated guns, military uniforms and four Motorcycles from the militia. Ten fatalities split between the two events; five fatalities coded.
