On 3 January 2024, the troops of Operation Hadarin Daji engaged in a firefight with the Katsina militia at Batsari LGA, coded to Batsari (Batsari, Katsina) and Safana LGA, coded separately. The troops killed ten militiamen in the attacks. The troops recovered an AK-47 Rifle, ammunition, seven Dane guns, three locally fabricated guns, military uniforms and four Motorcycles from the militia. Ten fatalities split between the two events; five fatalities coded.

On 3 January 2024, the Zamfara militia shot and killed seven people in Nahuche (Bungudu, Zamfara). The militia invaded the community early in the morning, shot and killed the people and abducted scores of others.
On 3 January 2024, ISWAP claimed to have attacked the Nigerian Army base with five mortar shells in Buni Yadi (Gujba, Yobe). No further details.

On 3 January 2024, the Zamfara militia shot and killed ten people in Kwanar Dutse village, Maru LGA, coded to Maru (Maru, Zamfara). The militia invaded the community with hundreds of fighters for failure to pay the 20 Million naira levy imposed on the people. They burned homes and shops, forcing the residents to flee and seek refuge in the nearby villages.

On 4 January 2024, Boko Haram (JAS) invaded the police checkpoint at Malari (Konduga, Borno). The police repelled the attack and were later reinforced by the military. Boko Haram fighters retreated and fled. There were no fatalities.

On 4 January 2024, ISWAP abducted and executed a Nigerian soldier after setting up an illegal checkpoint along the Gujba- Buni Yadi road, coded to Buni Yadi (Gujba, Yobe). They also abducted a Christian civilian. There was one fatality.

On 4 January 2024, an unidentified armed group killed a Fulani herder in Mortal in Bokkos LGA, coded Bokkos (Bokkos, Plateau). The victim was the third herder killed within two days in what is suspected to be a reprisal over the killing of over 100 people in the community on 24 December 2023.

On 5 January 2024, a Kaduna militia clashed with a local defense militia at Kunkurai, Dokan Karji and Anguwan Sako in Kauru LGA (Kaduna). 17 civilians were killed, nine of whom died in the clash, 20 locals were rescued from the militia and about 38 others were abducted.
On 5 January 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted ten people from the Owukpa community (Ogbadibo, Benue). No further details.
On 5 January 2024, an unidentified armed group killed three members of the same family at their residence in Ishiagu (Aniocha South, Delta). The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 5 January 2024, an unidentified armed group shot sporadically and abducted 10 persons from Wuro Musa (Yorro, Taraba), including the village chief whose dead body was recovered later, and 7 women. The assailants asked for a ransom of 1 million naira for each person.

On 5 January 2024, the Nigerian troops engaged the Katsina militia in a firefight around Makera (Dutsinma, Katsina). The militia ambushed the military convoy guarding some traders at the Yantumaki weekly market. The militia shot and killed eight traders and wounded many others. The community Watch Corps and an army reinforcement later supported the convoy and chased the militia away.

On 5 January 2024, suspected ISWAP fighters slit the throats of five people and killed them in a beer parlor in Quarry village, coded to Geidam (Geidam, Yobe). The militia tied the victim's hands before slaughtering them. They set three houses, the brothel and a car on fire and fled on sighting the military.

On 5 January 2024, a Katsina militia that attacked traders were engaged in an armed clash with police forces on the road between Maidabino and Yan Tumaki market (Dan-Musa, Katsina). At least six persons were killed and two others including security agents were wounded while 16 militiamen were killed. At least 22 fatalities.
On 5 January 2024, the Katsina militia abducted eight people in Maru LGA, coded to Maru (Maru, Katsina). The hostages included a man and his four daughters.

On 5 January 2024, the Nigerian troops engaged IS/BH in a firefight in Yaleri Kurna, also called Yaleri Kurnawa (Konduga, Borno). Two militiamen were killed, and many others were injured. There were two fatalities.
On 5 January 2024, ISWAP claimed to have killed two CJTF members during a clash near Gwoza (Gwoza, Borno). They forced others to withdraw and seized some property. There are two fatalities.
On 6 January 2024, suspected Boko Haram fighters abducted a graduate of the University of Maiduguri along the Maiduguri- Biu road coded to Biu (Biu, Borno). No further details.

On 6 January 2024, an unidentified armed group killed a woman and her daughter whom they set ablaze in their residence at Oketewe in Idah (Idah, Kogi). The woman was the sister of the Attah of Igala and the reason for the attack is unknown.
On 6 January 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a civil servant around Mile Six, Jalingo LGA, coded to Jalingo (Jalingo, Taraba). No further details.
On 6 January 2024, a Kaduna militia wounded one civilian and abducted six others from Kidandan (Giwa, Kaduna). Five persons were abducted at a spot called Shalele and one from his farm.

Around 6 January 2024 (between 4 January - 7 January), a Kaduna militia abducted at least 85 civilians near Katari (Kachia, Kaduna) on the Kaduna - Abuja expressway. Over 30 of the abductees were abducted on 7 January [coded separately]. A total ransom of 50 million was demanded from the victims.

On 6 January 2024, an unidentified armed group of 4 abducted the traditional ruler of Odumara Orodo from his domain in Orodo (Mbaitoli, Imo) and drove off with him towards Umaka-Orlu road. The abductee's cousin who was with him escaped. The abductee was rescued around 18 January by a joint team of security operatives who also claimed to have arrested suspects in connection with the abduction.

On 6 January 2024, the Nigerian military and the police clashed with the Zamfara militia in Danjibga town (Tsafe, Zamfara). An unspecified number of militiamen, two police officers and two soldiers were killed in the clash. Fatalities coded as 7.
On 6 January 2024, ISWAP claimed to have attacked a CJTF checkpoint in Gujba (Gujba, Yobe). They claimed the attack forced CJTF members to withdraw. No further details.

On 6 January 2024, ISWAP claimed to have ambushed a Nigerian military patrol along the Katafila- Pulka road, coded to Pulka (Gwoza, Borno). They claimed to have killed two soldiers during the ambush and forced others to withdraw. They seized a rifle, an RPG and two motorcycles. There were two fatalities.

On 6 January 2024, ISWAP abducted six women and stole their pushcarts along the Banki-Kumshe Road, Bama LGA, coded to Bama (Bama, Borno). The women were gathering firewood when the militiamen took them.
On 6 January 2024, a Kaduna militia killed one farmer and abducted sixteen others at Dinki village in Igabi LGA (Kaduna). An unspecified number of others were declared missing.

On 7 January 2024, a suspected Fulani militia together with a Jukun militia attacked civilians at Mchia (Logo, Benue) coded to Ugba. The attack happened in the morning and in the evening, resulting in at least 5 persons killed and several others wounded in the attack in the morning, and at least 2 persons killed and scores of persons missing in the evening. 7 fatalities coded.

Around 7 January 2024 (week of), an unidentified armed group killed the village head of Wuro Musa an dumped his body in the forest near a mountain. Location coded to Wuro Musa (Yorro, Taraba) were the victim was abducted from alongside about 10 others [coded separately].

On 7 January 2024, a Kaduna militia clashed with military forces when they barricaded the Kaduna - Abuja road around the Dogon-Fili area near Katari (Kachia, Kaduna) when the militia attacked civilians. One civilian driver was shot, over 30 civilians consisting of travelers and villagers from nearby Bishini and Kokore communities were abducted. The Kaduna police command claimed that the militia was repelled by the security forces and six persons including civilians caught in the crossfire were wounded. A total ransom of 50 million was demanded from the victims who included about 55 others.

Around 7 January 2024 (as reported), troops of Operation Hadin Kai engaged ISWAP militants in an armed clash at Ukuba in Sambisa, coded to Sambisa Forest Reserve (Gwoza, Borno). 11 militants were killed, one gun truck loaded with their ammunition exploded in the clash and the troops recovered various weapons and equipment. ISWAP claimed to have killed six soldiers and wounded many others without mentioning loss on their side.
On 7 January 2024, ISWAP claimed to have clashed with the CJTF in the Gajibo-Ngala area, coded to Ngala (Ngala, Borno). They captured a motorbike and forced CJTF to retreat. There were no fatalities.
Around 7 January 2024 (as reported), military forces ambushed and killed two ISWAP militants at Katarko (Gujba, Yobe) and recovered two AK-47 rifles.
On 7 January 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a commercial motorcyclist around the NTA junction along the Takum-Katsina-Ala Road, coded to Takum (Takum, Taraba).

On 7 January 2024, the Nigerian troops engaged an unidentified armed group in a firefight in Kopre (Hong, Adamawa) after the group opened fire indiscriminately in the community. The attackers retreated after the confrontation. There were no fatalities.

On 7 January 2024, armed Fulani pastoralists abducted at least ten civilians when they invaded Sagwari estate layout (Bwari, FCT). Two staff members of a nearby hotel were part of the abductees, other sources report that the assailants were dressed in military uniforms. A ransom of 60 million naira each was demanded and later increased to 100 million, after three of the abductees were murdered [coded separately] over a delay in payment.

On 7 January 2024, an unidentified armed group stabbed a 15-year old pastoralist and left him in critical condition around the TCNN - Bukuru general area (Jos South, Plateau). The victim was tending to cattle when he was attacked.

On 7 January 2024, ISWAP/ Boko Haram attacked civilians at a drinking joint called Bakassi in the outskirts of Gajiram town (Nganzai, Borno). Six civilians were killed and four others were wounded by the militants who snuck into the town through one of the porous areas of the trenches dug by security agents.

Around 7 January 2024 (as reported), troops of Operation Hadin Kai killed six ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants including the suspected Amir of Garin Munzo when they cleared out Garin Abu Umaru, Old/ New Mjimia, Garin Munzo, Alafa I and Alafa II areas, coded to Alafa (Gwoza, Borno). The militants' newly established camos were discovered and destroyed.

Around 8 January 2024 (as reported), some soldiers beat up a civilian at a residence in Port Harcourt (Port Harcourt, Rivers) and filmed the attack. The reason for the attack is unknown, but the victim was heard promising to confess in the video.

On 8 January 2024, an unidentified armed group ambushed and killed soldiers and two local defense militia operatives in Katapka (Toto, Nassarawa). The soldiers were part of the detachment deployed to the community after an attack on 1 January 2024 (coded separately).
On 8 January 2024, ISWAP abducted two people after staging an illegal checkpoint around Bindundul village along the Gubio-Damasak Road, coded to Gubio (Gubio, Borno).

On 8 January 2024, ISWAP claimed to have clashed with a Nigerian military patrol near Sambisa Forest Reserve (Gwoza, Borno). They claimed to have wounded an unspecified number of soldiers. There were no fatalities.

Around 8 January 2024 (as reported), an unidentified armed group with affiliation to the Gwagwalada council chairman beat up and tortured the persons that they met at the house of an activist in Gwagwalada (Gwagwalada, FCT). The activist who was an organizer of a protest over the state of road [coded separately] claimed that the assailants were sent by the chairman and that other protest organizers were also attacked for their participation in the protest.

On 8 January 2024, JTF troops comprised of soldiers and police forces engaged IPOB militants in an armed clash at their camp in Ihite-Owerri (Orlu, Imo). One militant was arrested, others fled with gunshot wounds, weapons, ammunition and military uniforms were recovered from the camp by the troops.

On 8 January 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted a Director in the Zamfara state ministry of finance alongside his wife and two children from their residence in Damba, coded and spelled as Dunba (Gusau, Zamfara). The director's wife was later released on the grounds of ill health, other residents claimed that the militia went straight to the victims' house with shooting in the area, a ransom of 100 million naira was demanded.
On 9 January 2024, an unidentified armed group of three suspected to be assassins killed a traditional chief in Shagamu (Shagamu, Ogun). The reason for the attack is unknown.
On 9 January 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted a businesswoman from her shop in Opolo (Yenagoa, Bayelsa). The abductors demanded a ransom for her release.

On 9 January 2024, ISWAP clashed with the Nigerian military after they launched an attack on the troops on the outskirts of Konduga town (Konduga, Borno). The attackers went away with three loggers. There were no fatalities.
On 9 January 2024, ISWAP claimed to have clashed with a Nigerian military patrol in Kirenawa (Marte, Borno). They claimed they forced the soldiers to retreat. There were no fatalities.

On 9 January 2024, police forces engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash at their hideout in Agbonchia forest (Eleme, Rivers). One abductee was rescued, the members of the group escaped with gunshot injuries, while one was arrested, weapons, ammunition and vehicles were recovered by the police forces. The abductee's family had paid a ransom equivalent to 25 million naira in dollars before the was rescued.
On 9 January 2024, an unidentified armed group ambushed and killed eight commuters in Kwapre, also called Kopre (Hong, Adamawa). No further details.

On 10 January 2024, the Zamfara militia clashed with security personnel (coded as the military) while trying to abduct a lecturer of Gusau University in the Damba area, coded and spelled as Dunba (Gusau, Zamfara). The militia outgunned the security and took the man away. There were no fatalities.
On 10 January 2024, ISWAP claimed to have killed a CJTF member while raiding his house in Kanama (Yunusari, Yobe).
Around 11 January 2024 (as reported), the Nigerian troops of Operation Hadin Kai shot and killed two Boko Haram fighters caught harvesting and stealing farm produce in Firgi, Pulka (Gwoza, Borno).

On 11 January 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted about 45 passengers from three commercial vehicles at Orokam (Ogbadibo, Benue) as they were traveling along the Otukpo - Enugu road. A ransom of 15 million naira each which was later reduced to 3 million each was demanded. The victims were rescued by a local defense militia in collaboration with police forces and soldiers [coded separately].

On 11 January 2024, the Gwadabawa Militia hacked a Fulani man to death while trying to arrest him in Mammande (Gwadabawa, Sokoto). The militia suspected the victim of being an informant to the marauding group raiding the community.

Around 11 January 2024, the troops of Operation Hadin Kai clashed with Boko Haram members rustling livestock from Fulani communities in Gajiram (Nganzai, Borno). The army shot and killed one of them and captured another one alive. They recovered two motorcycles and one rifle.

On 11 January 2024, the Katsina militia shot and killed nine people in Kukar Babangida (Jibia, Katsina). The victims included the traditional ruler of the village, two of his sons and six other people. The militia burnt down houses, shops and cars during the attack.

Around 11 January 2024 (as reported), ISWAP militants cut off the right arms of two fishers in Marte (Marte, Borno). The militia accused the fishers of stealing two cartons of fish out of the eight cartons confiscated from them for failing to pay their taxes.
On 11 January 2024, ISWAP claimed to have killed a military informant in Dikwa (Dikwa, Borno). They burned his house after killing him.

On 11 January 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted twenty-three people from the Kawu community in Bwari (Bwari, FCT). The attackers invaded the community from the Kuyeri Forest and went from house to house. The hostages included a local chief, Sarkin Pawan Kawu and his family members and a former PDP chairman in the area. Seven of the abductees were released on 12 January to raise a ransom of 20 million naira and two motorcycles for the other abductees' release.

Other: Around 11 January 2024 (as reported), the decomposing corpses of 11 Fulani locals were discovered in a forest near an area called crossing in Kachia LGA (Kaduna). The victims were arrested by soldiers from Ladugga community at different times, the Nigerian Army denied involvement in the incident.

Around 11 January 2024 (as reported), an unidentified armed group beat up an off-duty policeman into a coma at his residence in Dei-Dei (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The victim's wife, mother-in-law and infant were abducted, the two women were later murdered (coded separately) before the 90 million, later reduced to 10 million naira ransom was paid.

On 11 January 2024, a Niger militia (described as bandits) clashed with the local defense militia in Chachi community, coded to nearby town, Gauraka (Suleja, Niger). 1 local defense militia member was killed and four civilians were abducted, including a pregnant woman and her two children and her sister.

On 12 January 2024, suspected Fulani Pastoralists attacked and killed a woman in the Kwahilli community, coded to Kwabula (Askira Uba, Borno). The victim was washing clothes when the attackers launched the onslaught.
On 12 January 2024, ISWAP claimed to have attacked the Nigerian troops near Alagarno Forest (Biu, Borno). They killed and wounded an unspecified number of soldiers. Unspecified fatalities coded as 3.

On 12 January 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed four of their hostages around Idah Junction on Bwari-Jere Road, coded to Bwari (Bwari, FCT). The killing was suspected to have been caused by a failed ransom negotiation. Three females and one male were shot dead. There were four fatalities.

On 12 January 2024, the Nigerian troops and the vigilantes clashed with the Katsina militia in Yan Shantuna village, coded to Dutsin MA (Dutsinma, Katsina). The militiamen had rustled cattle from the village before the military intervened and killed one of them. The troops recovered the rustled cattle.

On 12 January 2024, a Plateau Militia stabbed (with an unspecified object) and killed a Fulani pastoralist while grazing his cattle in the NBA community, also spelt as Mbar (Bokkos, Plateau). No further details.

On 13 January 2024, the Nigerian military engaged in a firefight with an unidentified armed group after the group had abducted four people in Adani (Uzo Uwani, Enugu). A stray bullet killed one person. The armed group went away with the hostages, including a former LGA councilor. They demanded a 25 million naira ransom for their release.

On 13 January 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted sixteen people, including four women, on a farm in the Agwe community, Kuje (Kuje, FCT). A team of vigilantes rescued the hostages after tracing the abductors to their hideout, where they engaged them in a firefight, coded separately.

On 13 January 2024, twenty-five vigilantes from Kwali and Sabo communities in Kuje engaged an unidentified armed group in a shootout in a forest bordering Nassarawa and Kuje, coded to Kuje (Kuje, FCT). The armed group had abducted 16 people, coded separately, and the vigilante traced them to their hideout. Some of the abductors fled after they were outgunned. The vigilante rescued the 16 hostages. There were no fatalities.

On 13 January 2024, ISWAP claimed to have clashed with the Nigerian military and the CJTF near Sambisa Forest Reserve (Gwoza, Borno). They forced the military and the CJTF to retreat. There were no fatalities.
On 13 January 2024, the Sokoto militia shot and killed two people in the Takakume community (Goronyo, Sokoto). They abducted four others.

On 13 January 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted the police orderly (assumed on duty) of the Ukum LGA chairman, his principal, and two others at the Tongov axis (Katsina-Ala, Benue) as they were traveling along Zaki Biam - Katsina Ala road. A ransom of 50 million naira was demanded. The abductees were released on 24 January, after soldiers continued to trail the abductors.

On 13 January 2024, a vigilante group loyal to the Nigerian military shot and killed an IS/BH fighter in Bazanbari village, coded to Malari (Konduga, Borno). The IS/BH fighters were conveying logistics and fuel into the bush when the vigilante opened fire on them, killing one. Others fled, and the vigilante group recovered five bicycles, four gallons of fuel, and other items. There was one fatality.

On 13 January 2024, the Nigerian troops engaged in a firefight with Boko Haram (JAS) after the militiamen attacked and injured a hunter around Gadamayo village near Gwoza town (Gwoza, Borno). Boko Haram fighters fled after the military outgunned them. There were no fatalities.

On 14 January 2024, a Katsina militia invaded a joint military camp (coded as military forces and police forces) and engaged the troops in an armed clash at Nahuta (Batsari, Katsina). The militia set the troops' vehicles and property ablaze. They were repelled and proceeded into the town where they looted valuables and livestock from houses and shops. There were no casualties.

On 14 January 2024, an unidentified armed group of about four shot and killed the community development chairman of Mgboshimini at his church in Mile 4, Port Harcourt (Port Harcourt, Rivers). The victim's family claimed that the assailants were dressed in police uniform.
On 14 January 2024, ISWAP claimed to have fired two mortal shells at the Nigerian Army's position in Nduva (Damboa, Borno). There were no fatalities.
On 14 January 2024, an unidentified armed group killed a man when they attacked residents of Chukuku (Kuje, FCT). The assailants shot sporadically in the area for several hours.

On 14 January 2024, a Zamfara militia engaged a local defense militia and security operatives [coded as police forces] in an armed clash when they invaded Magizawa community in Kaura Namoda LGA (Zamfara). Three local defense militia members including a leader were killed, two to five others were wounded, 50 locals 36 of whom were women were abducted.

On 14 January 2024, an unidentified armed group suspected to be affiliated with the PDP shot sporadically at the market square in Ekpoma (Esan West, Edo) and vandalized a campaign vehicle belonging to Philip Shuaibu. The attack happened when the coordinator of the campaign went to the market to make a purchase after meeting with some of Shuaibu's supporters at Illeh Ward 10. There were no fatalities.

On 14 January 2024, a member of an unidentified cult militia killed his neighbors, a woman and her maid in Makurdi (Makurdi, Benue) in relation to a cult clash between rival gangs. The maid was having an affair with a member of a rival gang which provoked her neighbor to kill her. Her mistress was killed when she tried to intervene in the attack. The assailant fled.
On 15 January 2024, a Kaduna militia wounded a man at his residence in Dogarawa (Sabon Gari, Kaduna). A woman and her son were abducted while two other tenants were tied up.

On 15 January 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted a lecturer of the Kebbi state university of science and technology. Location coded to Aliero (Alieru, Kebbi) where the school is located, there are no details on ransom demands.
On 15 January 2024, Nigerian troops took over a Boko Haram [JAS faction] enclave at Kirenawa (Marte, Borno). Casualties are unknown.

On 15 January 2024, a suspected Katsina militia abducted two female students of Al-Qalam university as they were on their way back to school in Katsina (Katsina, Katsina). There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 15 January 2024, ISWAP claimed to have fired five mortal shells and a 40 mm grenade at the Nigerian Army's position in Aumma, also spelt as Auma (Damboa, Borno). There were no fatalities.

On 15 January 2024, ISWAP fighters led by Ali Kwaya and Abou Hassaini engaged Boko Haram [JAS faction] fighters from the Buduma faction in an armed clash at the islands of Kandahar and Kaduna Ruwa in Kukawa LGA (Borno). Scores of militants were killed from both factions, with ISWAP suffering higher casualties. Fatalities coded as 20.

On 15 January 2024, an unidentified armed group killed a 43-year old Fulani pastoralist at Kop Mandarken community in Bokkos LGA (Plateau) as he was on the way home. The victim was found the following day and died in the hospital.

Around 15 January 2024 (as reported), armed Fulani pastoralists killed four abductees out of those that were abducted at different times within the FCT [coded separately] over a delay in the payment of the demanded ransom and dumped their bodies at Ida, near Ushapa (Bwari, FCT). Three abductees were abducted from Sagwari estate, one was abducted alongside her sisters at Zuma area.

On 15 January 2024, the Nigerian troops clashed with IS/BH fighters attacking loggers around Galtimari near Konduga town (Konduga, Borno). IS/BH fighters had shot and wounded a logger and abducted others before the military intervened. The militiamen retreated after the army outgunned them. There were no fatalities.

On 16 January 2024, Bassa and Gbagyi ethnic militias clashed at Kudu village (Toto, Nassarawa) over a land dispute after the Bassa militia invaded the area where Gbagyi locals had settled for farming purposes. Seven persons were killed, several others were injured, houses and farm produce worth millions of naira were destroyed.

On 16 January 2024, a Niger militia killed one civilian and abducted nine others at Garam community (Tafa, Niger). The assailants who spoke in Fulfulde burgled shops in the area, one woman and her two children were let go and tied to a tree. Other sources report that one victim who is a serving policeman was shot and wounded in his house and that 14 persons were abducted.

On 16 January 2024, BSCVG in collaboration with soldiers and police forces engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash at the group's hideout and rescued abductees. The group had abducted commuters around Orokam (Ogbadibo, Benue) [coded separately], one BSCVG operative was wounded in the clash, one AK47 rifle machine gun among other item were recovered from the group.

Around 16 January 2024 (as reported), a Kaduna militia abducted a man who volunteered to deliver ransom to them in Birnin Gwari LGA (Kaduna). The victim is a retired school teacher and an unspecified amount was demanded as ransom from his family. The victim was released after he an unknown amount was paid as ransom, he was also thoroughly beaten before he was released, due to the delayed payment of the ransom [coded separately].
On 16 January 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed two people in Oke-Ode (Ifelodun, Kwara). No further details.
On 16 January 2024, police forces engaged an unidentified cult militia in an armed clash at Mosogar (Ethiope West, Delta). A policeman accidentally shot and killed his colleague during the clash.
On 16 January 2024, a Niger militia abducted three civilians from Zhibi community (Tafa, Niger) coded to Sabon Wuse. There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 16 January 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted four people from Afin community (Ifelodun, Kwara). The abductees included the local community chief and three teenagers, three suspected informants were apprehended by the police and hunters who trailed the abductors.

On 16 January 2024, the Guba militia engaged in a firefight with IS/BH fighters crossing from Go nori to Katarko, coded to Katarko (Gujba, Borbo). Three IS/BH fighters were killed, and a Gujba militia member was injured after stepping on an IED. There were three fatalities.

On 17 January 2024, an unidentified armed group, suspected to have come from Mbayongo Council Ward, killed nine people in Anyom (Katsina Ala, Benue). The attack was suspected to be a result of a gang war. The militia burned many houses and destroyed other property. There were nine fatalities.

On 17 January 2024, police forces responded to a distress call and engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash at Tse Gaagum village (Logo, Benue) coded to Ugba. Two of the assailants were killed; other sources report one killed, one motorcycle that was part of the valuables that were stolen was recovered.

On 17 January 2024, an unidentified armed group engaged the Ngboejeogu Central Security operatives in an armed clash at Ngbo Court community, coded as Ngbo (Ohaukwu, Ebonyi). A female security operative was killed, one other was wounded. The attackers destroyed properties worth millions of naira and looted a motorcycle.

Around 17 January 2024 (as reported), an unidentified armed group ambushed and killed two NIS who were on duty at a border post in Gari Garba, approximately 12km away from Kangiwa town (Arewa, Kebbi).

On 17 January 2024, an unidentified cult militia killed two people in Ota or Otta (Ado-Odo, Ogun). The attack disrupted the communal peace, and the people fled for safety. The two victims were suspected to be members (unarmed) of a rival cult group as the militia cut off their arms after butchering them to death.

On 17 January 2024, two rival Benue militia engaged in an armed clash at Anyom (Katsina Ala, Benue). Seven people were killed and houses were set ablaze. The clash lasted over a few days and properties were destroyed [coded separately].

On 17 January 2024, an unidentified armed group dressed in military uniforms attacked commuters at Ofosu (Idanre, Ondo) as they were traveling along the Benin - Ore expressway. One person was wounded and an unspecified number of others were abducted, a ransom of 20 million naira was demanded for their release.

On 17 January 2024, an unidentified armed group trailed a man who was part of a mob that was collecting market tolls and killed him in Mkpat Enin LGA (Akwa Ibom). The attack was related to the change in revenue collection agents by the chairperson of the Local Government Transition Committee without the inputs of the host community leaders where markets are located.

On 17 January 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted a man from his home at Garki (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The police intercepted the abductors in Kaduna the following day and rescued the hostage, coded separately.

On 17 January 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and wounded a man in a failed abduction attempt in Lugbe (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The armed group shot at the victim's car, and the bullets penetrated and hit him.

On 17 January 2024, the Zamfara militia shot and injured one person and abducted six others while raiding a vehicle along the Anka-Mayanchi Road near Mayanchi junction, coded to Mayanchi (Maru, Zamfara). There were no fatalities.
On 17 January 2024, a VSN operative shot and injured a motorcyclist at Ipara (Remo North, Ogun) after he attempted to take a way the victim's motorcycle. The assailant fled.

On 17 January 2024, a Fulani militia killed one Fulani local in Batura (Bokkos, Plateau). The victim and two other persons who escaped were conveying millet from the market to their house, the vehicle and millet were set ablaze by the assailants.
On 17 January 2024, a Fulani militia killed a local farmer who went to harvest crops on his farm at Gada village in Bokkos LGA (Plateau).

On 17 January 2024, a Plateau Militia attacked and injured one person in Butura, also called Batura (Bokkos, Plateau). The victim is the community Point of Contact for the United Nations Agencies, Funds and Programs.

Around 17 January 2024 (as reported), a suspected Ekowe militia attacked police forces and palace chiefs who were sent to carryout boundary demarcation between Ekowe and Isuikhuku communities. Location coded to Ekiadolor (Ovia North East, Edo). Several of the palace chiefs were injured in the land dispute.
On 17 January 2024, a Niger militia abducted a total of 17 civilians from Zhibi, coded to Garam (Tafa, Niger) and Garam (coded separately). Civilians fled the communities for safety.
On 17 January 2024, a Niger militia (described as bandits) abducted a total of 17 civilians from Garam (Tafa, Niger) and Zhibi (coded separately). Civilians fled the communities for safety.

On 18 January 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked some travelers between Ikere Ekiti and Iju, coded to Ikere (Ikere, Ekiti). The armed group opened fire on the travelers' vehicles before taking them into the bush.

On 18 January 2024, a suspected Fulani militia shot and killed two soldiers and two civilians in Okokolo (Agatu, Benue). The soldiers were responding to the activities of the marauders when they were ambushed. The militia opened fire indiscriminately on some villages, forcing the villagers, including women and children, to flee their homes and scamper for safety. One soldier was also injured in the ambush. Some sources report that 4 soldiers and 1 NSCDC operative were killed, while the commander of operation whirl punch claimed that two soldiers, 1 NSCDC operative were killed, while two other soldiers were wounded.

On 18 January 2024, the Katsina militia, disguised in a veil, shot and killed a police officer and wounded another at their duty post in Saki Jiki village, coded to Kurmayai (Batsari, Katsina). There was one fatality.
On 18 January 2024, the Kaduna militia abducted an unspecified number of people in Federe village (Lere, Kaduna). No further details.

On 18 January 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted an unspecified number of commuters after raiding a commercial vehicle along the Abeokuta-Ibadan Expressway in Odeda LGA, coded to Odeda (Odedah, Ogun).

On 18 January 2024, the Zamfara militia shot and wounded two people in Gargam village (Anka, Zamfara). The militia took away unspecified amounts of money and other valuables. There were no fatalities.
On 18 January 2024, the Zamfara militia shot and killed four people in Burwaye village, coded to Dan Gulbi (Maru, Zamfara). The militia abducted many other people.
On 18 January 2024, the Zamfara militia attacked the Dan Kawari community near Jangebe and Gwaram, coded to Gwaram (Talata Mafara, Zamfara). There were no fatalities.

Around 18 January 2024 (week of), the Zamfara militia shot and killed three people in Baichen Dauran, coded to Kagara Dauran (Zurmi, Zamfara). They abducted several people. There were three fatalities.
On 18 January 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted the son of the Emir of Pupule (Yorro, Taraba) from his residence. The abductee was rescued by soldiers on 2 February (coded separately).

On 18 January 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted two people from the Nigerian Army Post-Housing Estate, Kurudu (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The abductors invaded the estate and shot fire sporadically to scare the people away before abducting a woman married to a lawyer, and a woman who is the mother-in-law of the lawyer. The lawyer was reportedly the target, but the armed group missed their target and instead took the women away. The abductors demanded a 30 million naira ransom.

On 18 January 2024, the police engaged in a shootout with an unidentified armed group in Kaduna (Kaduna North, Kaduna). The armed group was intercepted while they were en route to Kano after abducting a man in Abuja, coded separately. One of the abductors was arrested, but the others managed to escape. The police rescued the hostage and recovered his car along with two Retay G17 model pistols, one Berretta pistol, ten 9mm P.A.K. ammunition and five 9mm special ammunition from the abductors. There were no fatalities.

On 18 January 2024, suspected Fulani militia clashed with the Bokkos militia as they attempted to invade Batura village (Bokkos, Plateau). The Fulani militia, suspected to have masterminded the killing of several people at the Bokkos on Christmas Eve, were repelled in what seemed to be a renewed attack on the communities. There were no fatalities.

On 18 January 2024, the Plateau militia shot and killed a Fulani pastoralist while grazing his cattle in Makada, coded to Mangar (Bokkos, Plateau). The victim was grazing alongside other pastoralists when the armed group opened fire on them. They rustled about 400 cattle, but the military later recovered them. The killing was suspected to be part of the targeted assassination of pastoralists to avenge the killing of over one hundred villagers on Christmas Eve.
On 18 January 2024, the Zamfara militia shot and killed two people in Danjikko village in Maru LGA, coded to Maru (Maru, Zamfara).
On 18 January 2024, the Nigerian troops fired artillery at the IS/BH locations upon sighting them around Damboa (Damba, Borno). There were no fatalities.
On 18 January 2024, the Zamfara militia killed one person and abducted ten others in Gidan Anna village, Kurya Madaro District in Kaura Namoda LGA, coded to Kuriya (Kaura Namoda, Zamfara).

On 19 January 2024, the Kaduna militia shot and killed a school principal for resisting abduction in Kuriga (Chikun, Kaduna). The militiamen abducted his wife and daughter after killing him. The victim was the Head of Kuriya Government School.

On 19 January 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed two people over land disputes in Akpano near Akpaji (Eleme, Rivers). The suspected land grabbers invaded the community and opened fire on the people for resisting them. There were two fatalities.

Around 19 January 2024 (between 18 - 20 January), an unidentified armed group abducted a person in the border hamlet of Chinabarka (Sabon Birni, Sokoto). Soldiers intervened and liberated the hostage. No clash was reported.

On 19 January 2024, government security forces (likely to be the police) clashed with an unidentified armed group raiding a residence at Anguwan Baraya in the Jalingo metropolis (Jalingo, Taraba). Two members of the armed group were killed. There were two fatalities.
On 19 January 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed three people at the T.Y. Danjuma University site in Jalingo (Jalingo, Taraba). There were three fatalities.

On 19 January 2024, the police engaged in a firefight with an unidentified armed group while raiding a forest along the Ibiono Ibom axis of the Calabar-Itu-Ikot Ekpene, coded to Oko Ita (Ibiono Ibom, Akwa Ibom). The militiamen laid an ambush to abduct the Chinese expatriates working in the area. The police stormed the hideout and engaged them in a shootout. They outgunned the militiamen and arrested ten. They recovered four AK-47 rifles and some locally made pistols from them. There were no fatalities.

On 19 January 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted a man at Sabon Lugbe, coded to Lugbe (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The victim and his wife were driving when the abductors shot at their tires, while the wife escaped.
On 19 January 2024, the Zamfara militia shot and killed one person in the Yankaba community (Kaura Namoda, Zamfara). The militia abducted unspecified many others.

On 19 January 2024, the Katsina militia attacked seven villages in Musawa LGA, coded to Musawa (Musawa). The militia killed sixteen people and abducted an unspecified number of others. They also set houses on fire.

Around 19 January 2024 (as reported), suspected armed pastoralists attacked civilians at Imamamaru community in Aguamede (Isi Uzo, Enugu). One person was killed, several others were injured and four houses were set ablaze.

On 20 January 2024, soldiers, Civilian JTF operatives and a local defense militia on an operation were ambushed by Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants at Kirenawa (Marte, Bono). One soldier and two local defense militiamen were killed, one other soldier was wounded as the troops retreated to Marte town.
On 20 January 2024, an unidentified armed group wounded one person and abducted two others at Otu town (Itesiwaju, Oyo). The wounded victim is the husband of one of the abductees.

On 20 January 2024, a Niger militia killed one person and abducted 21 others at Dangunu (Muya, Niger). One of the abductee who was a pregnant woman was released, other sources claimed that 16 farmers were abducted. The 16 abductees were rescued by security operatives who chased after the militia on 3 February (no report of a clash).
On 20 January 2024, the Katsina militia attacked and injured one person in Tsaskiya village (Safana, Katsina). The militia abducted another person. There were no fatalities.

On 20 January 2024, the Nigerian military ambushed and killed an ISWAP fighter around Luskori village, coded to Mafa (Mafa, Borno). The military recovered an AK-47 rifle with one magazine and nine rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition. There was one fatality.
On 20 January 2024, suspected Fulani pastoralists attacked the Abagana community along the Makurdi-Laafia road, Makurdi (Makurdi, Benue). There were no fatalities.
On 20 January 2024, suspected armed pastoralists attacked civilians at Isiado community in Aguamede (Isi Uzo, Enugu). Two locals were killed and residents fled the area.

On 21 January 2024, Nigerian troops ambushed and killed a Boko Haram (JAS) fighter in Luskori, coded to Konduga (Konduga, Borno). Another one escaped with gun wounds. The military recovered an AK 47 rifle. There was one fatality.

On 21 January 2024, a Katsina militia dressed in military uniforms abducted 31 civilians from Tashar Nagule village in Batsari LGA (Katsina). The abductees included women, men and children, the residents claimed that the militia claimed to have been soldiers who came to help them and threatened to shoot those who ran away. The militia shot in the air to scare the residents. A ransom of 60 million was demanded, the abductees were rescued by soldiers who raided the militia's camp on 28 January (coded separately).
On 21 January 2024, Boko Haram fighters [JAS faction] engaged rival ISWAP fighters in an armed clash at their camp at Tumbun Jaki (Abadan, Borno). Casualties are unknown.
On 21 January 2024, ISWAP staged a checkpoint and abducted four people around Bindundul village along the Damasak-Maiduguri Road, Gubio LGA coded to Gubio (Gubio, Borno).

On 21 January 2024, Black Axe also called Aiye and SEC also called Eiye engaged in an armed clash in Benin City (Oredo, Edo). Three persons were killed across different areas including Igan street and 2nd East Circular area at different times on the same day.

On 21 January 2024, suspected Fulani pastoralists killed one civilian and burned a house at Odoba and Isi Agbuhu villages in Aguamede (Isi Uzo, Enugu). The residents claimed that there wasn't an intervention from security forces during the attack that lasted for up to 4 hours.

On 22 January 2024, a Zamfara militia attacked and wounded the executive secretary of the Zamfara Investment Promotion Agency a few kilometers away from Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara) where she was headed for a meeting with investors. The victim was taken to the hospital for treatment.

On 22 January 2024, ISWAP fighters invaded the camp of rival Boko Haram [JAS faction] fighters in a reprisal and engaged them in an armed clash at Tunbun Rago (Abadan, Borno). Scores of fighters mostly from the Boko Haram faction were killed, fatalities coded as 20.

Around 22 January 2024 (as reported), ISWAP opened fire on the Nigerian troops and the CJTF in Krinowa, coded to Marte (Marte, Borno). An unspecified number of CJTF died, and the military equipment was damaged. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.

Around 23 January 2024 (as reported), a Kaduna militia thoroughly beat up a retired school principal whom they had abducted when he went to deliver ransom for another abductee in Birnin Gwari LGA (Kaduna). The victim was beat up for not having and paying the demanded ransom on time. He lost a tooth in the process and was later released after the payment was made.

On 23 January 2024, the Katsina militia launched simultaneous attacks on Dan Alhaji, also known as Dan Alhaji Yangayya (Batsari, Katsina) and Yandaka, coded separately. The militia killed two people and abducted 29 others. Two fatalities shared between the two events. One fatality coded.

On 23 January 2024, the Katsina militia launched simultaneous attacks on Yandaka near Kurmayai (Batsari, Katsina) and Dan Alhaji, coded separately. The militia killed two people and abducted 29 others. Two fatalities shared between the two events. One fatality coded.

On 23 January 2024, soldiers from 1 Battalion of the Nigerian army in collaboration with a local defense militia engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash at Sabon Birni forest in Shanga LGA (Kebbi). Four members of the group were killed, four abductees were rescued by the troops who also recovered weapons, ammunition and pairs of military uniforms.
On 23 January 2024, the Niger militia shot and killed one person and abducted nine others in Garam (Tafa, Niger). The militia looted several shops.

On 23 January 2024, Zurmi militia clashed with Zamfara militia, who were robbing a commercial vehicle in Dutsi Uku around Yanbuki (Zurmi, Zamfara). The militia fled the scene when the military outgunned them. There were no fatalities.

On 23 January 2024, the Zamfara militia shot and killed two people around Yanbuki (Zurmi, Zamfara). The militia who had retreated from a firefight with the vigilante killed the two people as a reprisal for what the vigilante did to them at Dutsi Uku village.
On 23 January 2024, the Kaduna militia abducted four people, a couple and two children, at their residence in the Hayin Kinini community, Kakangi village (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). No further details.

On 23 January 2024, the Nigerian military, in collaboration with the NSCDC and vigilantes, raided the Kebbi militia's hideout in Sabon Gari village (Shanga, Kebbi). The military killed one militiaman and rescued four hostages. They recovered three magazines, 142 rounds of 7.62mm ammunition, and two pairs of camouflage uniforms. There was one fatality.

On 23 January 2024, policemen and a local defense militia pursued and engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash after the group abducted five persons around Runde village (Ardo Kola, Taraba) coded to Sunkani. Two of the assailants were arrested.

On 23 January 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted 5 civilians from around Runde village (Ardo Kola, Taraba) coded to Sunkani. Police forces trailed the abductors and rescued the victims on the same day (coded separately).

Around 23 January 2024 (as reported), police forces raided the hideout of an unidentified armed group and engaged them in an armed clash at Kofai ward in Jalingo (Jalingo, Taraba). One of the group's members was killed following injuries he sustained in the clash, another was arrested and the others escaped with various degrees of injuries.

On 23 January 2024, a Fulani militia of 5 abducted four women at Ogurugu community (Uzo Uwani, Enugu). The women ere abducted after the manager and farm owner who were the targets were not seen by the militia, they were released six days later after 2 million naira and food stuff were paid as ransom.

On 23 January 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted four people in Fugar (Etsako Central, Edo). The police arrested members of the armed group in Kano around 1 February 2024 after collecting a ransom.
On 23 January 2024, the Katsina militia abducted six people from Garin Karbau village, coded to Wagini (Batsari, Katsina). No further details.

On 23 January 2024, the Katsina Community Watch Corps engaged the Katsina militia in a firefight after the militia invaded Zakka (Safana, Katsina). The militia killed one of the Community Watch Corps members. There was one fatality.

On 23 January 2024, suspected Fulani pastoralists killed two civilians when they attacked Okpokpolo village (Agatu, Benue) coded to Bagagi and Ikpele [coded separately]. An unspecified number of persons were injured, at least 17 houses were set ablaze by the assailants who invaded the area from neighboring Nasarawa state.
On 23 January 2024, an unidentified armed group killed and beheaded a woman around the Banking Layout in Udo Udoma Avenue, Uyo (Uyo, Akwa Ibom).

On 23 January 2024, the Nigerian military and the Katsina Community Watch clashed with the Katsina militia after the militia rustled cattle in Rugar Gamji village, coded to Gatakawa (Kankara, Katsina). An unspecified number of the militia were killed and injured. The military recovered the rustled cattle. An unspecified fatality coded as 3.

On 23 January 2024, suspected Fulani pastoralists wounded an unspecified number of civilians when they attacked Ikpele (Agatu, Benue) and Okpokpolo [coded separately] where two other were killed. At least 17 houses were set ablaze by the assailants who invaded the area from neighboring Nasarawa state.

On 23 January 2024, a Niger militia (described as bandits) attacked and killed a civilian in Tsohon-Dangunu, location coded to the closest known town, Dangunu (Muya, Niger) and abducted 16 members of his family.

On 24 January 2024, Police and Tabbital Pulaku hunters clashed with Adamawa militia in Karlahi (Fufore, Adamawa). The militiamen abducted two people from a cattle ranch, and the Police and the hunters mobilized and engaged them in a firefight, killing three while others escaped with gun wounds. The Police rescued the two hostages and recovered a pump action gun, a single barrel gun, a locally fabricated revolver gun, handsets, chains, mats, and charms. There were three fatalities.

On 24 January 2024, the Zamfara militia, dressed in military camouflage, killed two people and wounded four others in Baichen Dauran, coded to Kagara Dauran (Zurmi, Zamfara). They abducted several women and children and rustled domestic animals. There were two fatalities.

On 24 January 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed two people at the Tempo Junction along the Enugu-Onitsha highway, Enugu North LGA, coded to Enugu (Enugu North, Enugu). No further details.
On 24 January 2024, ISWAP attacked the Nigerian troops in Banki (Bama, Borno). The ensuing firefight forced the IS fighters to retreat. There were no fatalities.

On 24 January 2024, police clashed with an unidentified armed group while raiding their hideouts in Ukya village (Toto, Nassarawa). The police shot and killed a member of the group while others escaped with gun wounds. Fourteen hostages were rescued after the clash. There was one fatality.
On 24 January 2024, ISWAP attacked the Nigerian troops' position in Buni Yadi (Gujba, Yobe). No further details.

On 24 January 2024, the Nigerian military shot and killed three members of an unidentified armed group in Chibi, Karim Lamido LGA, coded to Karim Lamido (Karim Lamidu, Taraba). The military recovered 2 AK-47 rifles, a motorcycle and a cache of 40 rounds of 7.62 MM Special ammunition.

On 24 January 2024, an unidentified armed group killed about 20 to 30 civilians at Kwahaslalek and some surrounding communities in Mangu LGA (Plateau). An unspecified number of persons sustained gunshot injuries, houses were burned.

On 24 January 2024, an unidentified armed group killed a POS operator at his shop in Mgbala Agwa, coded as Mgbele (Oguta, Imo). A source claimed that the victim had an encounter with a group of youths in the community which is suspected to be connected to the attack.
On 24 January 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked and injured two vigilante members in the Bakin Dutse community (Madagali, Adamawa). There were no fatalities.
Around 25 January 2024 (as reported), a suspected Fulani militia killed one farmer at IDP camp 1 in Gbajimba (Guma, Benue) as claimed by the coordinator of the IDP camp.

On 25 January 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted the PDP chairman for Lagos State on the Lagos-Ibadan expressway around Bamboo, coded to Ogere (Ikenne, Ogun). The chairman was abducted alongside other party members returning from the Zonal Caucus Meeting held in Ibadan. The police rescued some of the hostages. The abductors demanded a 200 million naira ransom, the abductees were rescued on 29 January after police forces engaged the abductors in an armed clash, one of the abductees died in the clash.

On 25 January 2024, the Katsina militia disguised as women shot and killed two police officers at a police checkpoint along Jibia-Batsari road, Gurbin Magarya village, coded to Wagini (Batsari, Katsina). The militiamen seized the police riffles and went away with them. There were two fatalities.

On 25 January 2024, ISWAP claimed to have killed a soldier and wounded another while attacking a joint Military-Police outpost in Gajigana (Magumeri, Borno). They seized two rifles and burned the outpost. There was a fatality.

On 25 January 2024, an unidentified armed group killed a woman and her daughter both of whom they had previously abducted from a residence at Dei-Dei (Abuja Municipal, FCT) (coded separately). The victims were killed before the 10 million naira demanded as ransom was paid, location coded to where the victims were abducted.

On 25 January 2024, a Niger militia numbering over 50 killed one civilian and abducted 31 others from Jagaba village in Pan Dongari (Rafi, Niger). The murdered victim was shot when he tried escaping and the assailants shot sporadically during the attack.
On 25 January 2024, the Sokoto militia shot and killed one person among the commuters attacked along the Sabon Birni-Gidan-Tudu road in Gudu LGA, coded to Tudu (Gada, Sokoto). There was one fatality.

On 25 January 2024, the Nigerian police engaged in a firefight with a Katsina militia and killed one in Dandume (Dandume, Katsina). The militiamen were advancing towards the village in an attempt to abduct the villagers when the police intercepted them. The police recovered a general-purpose machine gun loaded with 27 rounds of 94.5mm live ammunition. There was one fatality.

On 26 January 2024, the Katsina militia shot and killed four people in the Gangara community (Jibia, Katsina). They injured six villagers and abducted an unspecified number of people, mostly women and children. There were four fatalities.

Around 26 January 2024 (as reported), Plateau militia attacked and fired gunshots at the Nigerian troops enforcing the 24-hour curfew in Kerang (Mangu, Plateau). The government imposed a 24-hour curfew to stem the tide of the escalating communal crisis in the state. The youth claimed the military was not neutral in the crisis. There were no fatalities.
On 26 January 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted the proprietress of a private school from the school's premises at Agbado in Ifo LGA (Ogun). There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 26 January 2024, the Nigerian troops shot and killed seven members of the Katsina militia while on a clearance operation at Pada, Matso-Matso and Yarlumu, coded to Nahuta (Batsari, Katsina). The military destroyed the militia's enclaves, and many of them escaped with gun wounds. There were seven fatalities.

On 26 January 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted the Deputy Vice-Chancellor of Abia State University while fueling his car at a fuel station in Umu Opara (Umuahia South, Abia). The abductors dragged him into their SUV and collected his wife's ATM card before driving him away. A ransom of 35 million naira was demanded and the victim was released on 6 February after 25 million was paid.

On 26 January 2024, the Nigerian troops engaged the Zamfara militia in a firefight and killed two at Getso and Ubaka villages, coded to Malele (Maru, Zamfara). The military recovered an AK-47 rifle, one magazine 7.62mm special ammunition and two motorcycles. There were two fatalities.

On 26 January 2024, the Nigerian police clashed with an unidentified armed group around Bwari (Bwari, FCT). The police killed three members of the armed group, including their leader, who had been on the police wanted list. There were three fatalities.
On 26 January 2024, ISWAP claimed to have abducted and killed a man near Kukawa (Kukawa, Borno). The victim was accused of being a military spy.
On 26 January 2024, the Sokoto militia shot and killed two people while raiding two villages in Sabon Birnin LGA, coded to Sabon Birnin (Sabon Birnin, Sokoto).

On 26 January 2024, the Nigerian troops clashed with an unidentified armed group in Wukari (Wukari, Taraba). The military responded to a gunshot and found two people already shot dead and another wounded by the armed group, coded separately. They recovered two AK 47 Rifles with 36 Rounds of 7.62 MM Special ammunition, ten empty cases of 7.62 MM, 1 Double Barrel Rifle and 1 Single Barrel Rifle with 14 live cartridges. There were no fatalities.
On 26 January 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed two people in Wukari (Wukari, Taraba). They wounded another. The military intervened and engaged them in a firefight, coded separately.

Around 26 January 2024 (as reported), the Nigerian military engaged IPOB/ESN in a firefight after the militia abducted some people in Owerri (Owerri Municipal, Imo). The military killed one of the abductors and forced others to abandon their hostages and escape. The army recovered one AK 47 rifle and magazine, a G-3 rifle with mounted magazines and a vehicle. There was one fatality.
On 27 January 2024, a Kaduna militia ambushed Nigerian troops at Kwona Mutua (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). Casualties are unknown.

On 27 January 2024, suspected armed pastoralists attacked civilians at Ogwumogbo (Agatu, Benue) and killed ten persons. The assailants shot sporadically when they invaded the area and displaced civilians from the area.

On 27 January 2024, a Sokoto militia wounded a civilian and abducted another at Tambuwal motor park (Tambuwal, Sokoto). The abductee is a spare parts dealer at the park, who was abducted when his father that was the target was absent. The assailants shot sporadically during the attack.
On 27 January 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed three people and abducted five others in Orlu (Orlu, Imo).

On 27 January 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted the Oyo State Chairman of the Tipper, Lorry and Quary Park Management System in his residence in Ajiboye, Omi Apata, coded to Omin Adio (Ido, Oyo). No further details.

On 27 January 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked security operatives, coded as police forces at Oja village (Akoko Edo, Edo). The attack took place during a burial ceremony, properties were destroyed by the assailants and there were no fatalities.

On 27 January 2024, troops of Operation Hadarin Daji who were on a clearance patrol engaged a Katsina militia in an armed clash at Dumburum woodlands in Katsina, coded to nearby Dumburum forest (Zurmi, Zamfara). Two militiamen were killed, others escaped with gunshot wounds, and 35 abductees consisting of 19 males, 12 females, and 4 children were rescued.

On 27 January 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed an NSCDC officer in Idimu (Alimosho, Lagos). The assailants trailed the victim's vehicle when returning from duty and shot him in the stomach.

On 27 January 2024, police forces engaged a member of Icelanders in an armed clash at Borokiri (Port Harcourt, Rivers). The Icelander who was the leader of the militia and was on the police's wanted list was killed.

On 27 January 2024, the Zamfara militia abducted a man in Bungudu (Bungudu, Zamfara). The hostage is an INGO employee and was taken while travelling to visit his family in Kano State. The militia demanded a ransom.

On 27 January 2024, an unidentified armed group attacked a couple as they were returning home in Sabon Lugbe, coded to nearby Lugbe (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The woman sustained a gunshot injury and her husband was abducted by the assailants. The abductee was rescued by the police the following day (no details of a clash).

On 27 January 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted the PDP chairman of the Nsit Atai chapter alongside two others from M-Lounge in Uyo (Uyo, Akwa Ibom) where they were watching a football match. The abductees were rescued by the joint task force around 20 March, there are no details on ransom payment.

On 27 January 2024, Okuama and Okoloba communal militia clashed over a land dispute, and six persons were killed as a result. Location coded to Okoloba (Bomadi, Delta) which shares a boundary with Okuama community, where three of the victims hailed from while the other three were mercenaries from other communities.

On 27 January 2024, an unidentified armed group clashed with Nigerian troops who responded to a distress call at Satguru and Tyop villages, coded to Gindiri (Mangu, Plateau). 30 members of the group were killed, 50 others were arrested and four soldiers were wounded.

On 28 January 2024, two unidentified cult militias engaged in an armed clash over supremacy in Oriuzor community (Ezza South, Ebonyi). Three persons were killed and one person was killed the next day following a continuation of the clash. The police claimed to have arrested two persons in connection with the incident.

On 28 January 2024, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists abducted three policemen and took their rifles at Ohoro village (Ughelli North, Delta). The policemen were responding to a distress call following a robbery incident. The bodies of policemen were discovered in the community around 6 March.

On 28 January 2024, two unidentified cult militias engaged in an armed clash at Igando (Alimosho, Lagos) and policemen responded to a distress call in the area. One person was wounded in the clash, two suspects were arrested by the police and the others fled.

On 28 January 2024, a Zamfara militia abducted a newly wedded couple from Madabanciya village in Bungudu LGA (Zamfara). The militia who entered the village on foot and left their motorcycles outside also went from house to house, stole food and other valuables.

On 28 January 2024, Nigerian soldiers engaged a Katsina militia in an armed clash at their hideout in a forest linking Rugu forest in Batsari LGA (Katsina). 35 abductees were rescued, the militia fled.
On 28 January 2024, ISWAP claimed to have clashed with CJTF patrol near Pulka (Gwoza, Borno). One CJTF member was wounded in the attack, and others retreated. There were no fatalities.
On 28 January 2024, ISWAP claimed to have abducted and killed two men near Kukawa (Kukawa, Borno). They accused the men of spying for the Nigerian military. There were two fatalities.

On 28 January 2024, a Kaduna militia killed a man and his son and abducted 15 other residents from Gidan Makeri, coded to Janjala which is 1km away (Kagarko, Kaduna). The militia parked their motorcycles on the banks of River Gurara before invading the community.

On 28 January 2024, police forces trailed and engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash in the bushes between Karmo and Gwagwa (Abuja Municipal, FCT). Three victims who were abducted earlier on the same day were rescued, casualties are unknown.

On 28 January 2024, an unidentified armed group of about seven abducted three Christian worshippers while they were praying at Idu Gbagyi mountain in Karmo, coded to near by Idu (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The abductees were rescued by police operatives who trailed the abductors.

On 28 January 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted two girls from their home in Guita community, Kubwa (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The abductors who escaped through a bush path that links the community with another had abducted three siblings but sent the boy back home. A ransom of 30 million naira was demanded and later reduced to 5 million with a deadline for payment.

On 29 January 2024, suspected armed pastoralists killed a man on his farm at Gege village in Ogbomosho (Ogbomosho North, Oyo). The victim was also a pastor, three persons were arrested in connection with the attack.

On 29 January 2024, suspected armed pastoralists killed the traditional rulers of Imojo Ekiti and Esun Ekiti as they were traveling along the Oke Ako - Irele road (Ikole, Ekiti) together with the traditional ruler of Ara Ekiti who escaped the attack. The assailants took the personal belongings of the victims and dragged their bodies into the bush.

On 29 January 2024, troops of Operation Hadarin Daji conducted clearance operations and engaged Zamfara militias in clashes at their hideouts in Rukudawa, Dumburum, Tsanu, Birnin Tsaba, Magare and Shamshusalle in Zurmi LGA (Zamfara) and Kiyawa LGA (coded separately). The militias fled, and their hideouts were destroyed including those belonging to a militia leader called Sule. There were no fatalities.

On 29 January 2024, two unidentified cult militias engaged in an armed clash over supremacy in Oriuzor community (Ezza South, Ebonyi) for the second day. One person was killed. three others were killed on the day before (coded separately). The police claimed to have arrested two persons in connection with the incident.

On 29 January 2024, troops of Operation Hadarin Daji conducted clearance operations and engaged Zamfara militias in clashes at their hideouts in Rukudawa, Dumburum, Tsanu, Birnin Tsaba, Magare and Shamshusalle in Kiyawa LGA (Zamfara) and Zurmi LGA (coded separately). The militias fled, and their hideouts were destroyed including those belonging to a militia leader called Sule. There were no fatalities.

Around 29 January 2024 (as reported), an unidentified armed group killed a lawyer whom they abducted together with his brother at Orsumoghu (Ihiala, Anambra). The victim was the PDP House of Representatives candidate for Ihiala federal constituency during the 2023 elections and the assailants accused him of writing petitions against them to the state government. His brother was released unhurt.

On 29 January 2024, police forces engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash and rescued nine out of the ten victims whom the group had abducted at the Ogere axis (Ikenne, Ogun) on 25 January (coded separately). One of the victims was killed during the clash, two others were injured and the rescued persons included the PDP chairman in Lagos state who was returning from Ibadan when he and others were abducted.
On 29 January 2024, a Kaduna militia wounded a man, and abducted his wife and their three children in Kidandan (Giwa, Kaduna). The man was wounded for resisting the attempt to abduct him.
On 29 January 2024, the Katsina militia abducted four people from Sabon Garin Bilbis, coded to Faskari (Faskari, Katsina). No further details.

On 29 January 2024, Ifon and Ilobu communal militias clashed following renewed hostilities related to a land dispute. 3 persons were killed and residents of both towns fled, the police claimed to have arrested two persons in connection with the clash and the state governor imposed a 6am to 6pm curfew on the towns. Location coded to Ifon (Orolu, Osun).

On 29 January 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted 10 civilians comprising 6 school children, three teachers, and a driver from a private school as they were returning to Eporo from Emure (Emure, Ekiti). A ransom of 10 million naira each was demanded. The abductees were released on 4 February except the driver who was murdered (coded separately), there are no reports on ransom payment.

On 29 January 2024, an unidentified armed group killed two policemen and two civilians at Ohii junction along Owerri - Orlu highway (Mbaitoli, Imo). The assailants also robbed some POS operators of their money.

On 29 January 2024, troops of Operation Hadarin Daji on patrol engaged a Zamfara militia in an armed clash along the Shinkafi - Isa road (Shinkafi, Zamfara) and rescued two travelers whom the militia had abducted. There were no fatalities.

On 30 January 2024, a local defense militia clashed with a Katsina militia at Dogon Marke village in Safana LGA (Katsina). The defense militia attempted to block the escape routes of the Katsina militia who were fleeing from an airstrike by the military, five of the defense militiamen were declared missing. Fatalities unknown.

On 30 January 2024, some police officers shot and wounded a Vigilante Commander and two members of the Idjerhe Kingdom's vigilante group in Jesse town (Ethiope West, Delta). The victims were admitted to the hospital for treatment. The police command ordered the arrest and detention of the police officers responsible for the shooting after the community protested, coded separately. There were no fatalities.

On 30 January 2024, the Zamfara militia shot and killed a man along the Gusau-Funtua highway, coded to Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara). The militiamen indiscriminately shot at commuters when the victim was hit. There was one fatality.

On 30 January 2024, troops of 114 battalion of the Nigerian Army trailed an unidentified armed group and engaged them in an armed clash at Apawa village (Lau, Taraba), reported as Yorro LGA. The group fled and abandoned three abductees who had previously been abducted from Ardo Kola LGA. Casualties are unknown.

On 30 January 2024, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked civilians at Agojeju-Odo community in Bagaji Odo district (Omala, Kogi) as claimed by the lawmaker representing Omala constituency at the state house of assembly. Four civilians were killed, and the assailants who numbered over 150, invaded the community through Bugana town which borders Benue and Nasarawa states, shot sporadically when they arrived.
On 31 January 2024, a Sokoto militia killed one civilian and abducted eight others at Katalan Kaura village in Atakwanyo (Gwadabawa, Sokoto).

On 31 January 2024, two unidentified rival cult militias who were also students of Community Grammar School and Ikotun High School clashed at a school in Ikotun (Alimosho, Lagos). Police forces intervened and shot sporadically which resulted in a stampede that led to ten persons being hospitalized, an unspecified number of students were arrested and later released.

On 31 January 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted two women from Kobi community, coded to nearby Guzape (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The abductees were rescued by security forces on the same day (coded separately).

On 31 January 2024, soldiers and policemen engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash along the Nyanya - Keffi expressway (Abuja Municipal, FCT) where they mounted security checkpoints. Two women who were abducted from Kobi village were rescued (coded separately) after the abductors abandoned them and fled.

Around 31 January 2024 (between 26 January - 6 February), an unidentified armed group tortured the Deputy Vice Chancellor of Abia state university, whom they had abducted at a filling station in Umu Opara (Umuahia South, Abia). The victim was tortured and recorded, the videos were sent to his family to threaten them and hasten the payment of ransom. He was released on 6 February after the ransom was paid, location coded to where the victim was abducted from.

On 31 January 2024, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked and killed fifteen people in Ugboju, coded to Bagagi (Agatu, Benue). The attack triggered panic, and many people fled in disarray. The armed group also abducted an unspecified number of children.

Around 31 January 2024 (week of), an unidentified armed group killed a driver who was abducted together with school children and their teacher as they were heading to Eporo from Emure (Emure, Ekiti). The other abductees were released on 4 February, location coded to where the abduction took place.

On 31 January 2024, a suspected cult militia shot and killed a police inspector after raiding his house in Afaha Ube within the Uyo metropolis (Uyo, Akwa Ibom). The militia, numbering over ten, invaded the police residence and shot fire sporadically to scare the residents away before killing the police officer. The militia cut off the victim's head, placed it beside his body, and fled. A source reported the killing could be a reprisal for the police action.
